candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct and coherent: trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all align to autism spectrum disorder; disease-focused ASD GWAS meta-analysis context.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Has moderate supportive signals despite lacking PRS-only AUC/R2: reports variance explained R²=0.0245 (appears full-model/unspecified) plus OR per SD=1.33 (moderate discriminative signal). Metrics are plausible under the heritability ceiling and more supportive than a very small partial R².
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR-only evaluation with a reasonably sized validation sample (n=7,148) and basic covariates (PCs, genotyping wave) consistent with PRS evaluation; multi-cohort development suggests better external orientation than a single-study framework.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Main risk is metric comparability (R² not explicitly PRS-only) and use of C+T (structurally weaker than genome-wide shrinkage), but no endpoint mismatch or heavy covariate leakage flags.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Strongest overall benchmark-transfer package in this shortlist: best endpoint fidelity, disease-focused consortium setting, and materially stronger reported signal (R² and OR) than the alternative.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Concept label matches ASD, but phenotyping_reported is explicitly different ('Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn)'), creating endpoint ambiguity/mismatch versus a direct ASD diagnosis endpoint.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Reports only partial R²=0.00546 with no effect size and no PRS-only discrimination metric; this is a weak signal and hard to compare across studies.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR evaluation but smaller validation sample (n=2,198). Record_count=50 does not add performance credibility; training sample is N/A, reducing interpretability.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Higher risk of non-comparable endpoint/analysis framing (sex-specific cross-psychiatric/cognition paper; withdrawn behavior phenotype) and weaker, less interpretable metric reporting.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Lower likelihood to rank #1 externally due to endpoint mismatch/ambiguity and weaker performance evidence, despite a stronger method label (SDPR) and large variant count.

rationale: Between the two, PGS000327 is the only candidate with clean endpoint fidelity to ASD diagnosis and provides stronger, more interpretable performance support (OR per SD and higher R²) in a disease-focused multi-cohort context with basic covariates. PGS002790’s phenotyping mismatch ('psychiatric behavior (withdrawn)') and weak partial R² make it less likely to top an external ASD benchmark even with a genome-wide shrinkage method.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match: trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all align to corneal dystrophy with no horizon/packaging or proxy phenotype indicated.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only PRS-comparable signal shown is partial correlation partial-r=0.0471 (EUR eval), which is modest but higher than the sibling candidate; no AUC/R2/effect sizes to further support.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same portability-study setting as the other candidate (UKB-derived, evaluated across multiple ancestry groups; selected record is European). Validation n=19,321 and record_count=6 are identical, so they don’t differentiate.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Framework/portability-paper origin (UKB-derived across many traits) is a general external-benchmark risk vs disease-focused PRS; however covariates are basic (age/sex/PCs etc.) with low leakage risk. No metric inflation via heavy clinical covariates apparent.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Best within-shortlist: stronger method family for polygenic signal capture (LDpred2 genome-wide shrinkage) plus much larger variant count (59,944) and higher partial-r than the sparse penalized-regression sibling; these structural+metric edges are the main differentiators given identical endpoint and validation context.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match: trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all align to corneal dystrophy; no endpoint mismatch signals.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Partial correlation partial-r=0.0384 (EUR eval), lower than the alternative; no AUC/R2/effect sizes to compensate.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same study family, same training cohort (UKB), same ancestry distribution pattern, same selected validation ancestry (European), and same validation n=19,321—no independent validation advantage.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same portability/framework-paper risk profile; covariates are similarly basic. Additional risk: extremely sparse model (38 variants) may under-capture polygenic signal and be less robust out of sample.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Weaker likely benchmark rank: lower partial-r and far fewer variants, with no compensating endpoint/validation advantages over the sibling.

rationale: Both candidates are near-clones from the same UKB portability paper with identical endpoint wording, covariates, and validation context, and both lack AUC/R2. The only meaningful differentiators are PRS-comparable partial-r and structural properties: PGS002042 has higher partial-r (0.0471 vs 0.0384) and uses LDpred2 with genome-wide coverage (59,944 variants), which is more likely to transfer and rank higher than a 38-variant sparse penalized-regression score in an external benchmark.

ontology: congenital vitamin k-dependent coagulation factors deficiency

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match: trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both align to the target disease concept (congenital deficiency of other clotting factors incl. factor VII) and trait_efo is the exact target EFO.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only partial correlation reported (partial-r=0.0563, CI 0.0424–0.0702) with no PRS-only AUC/R2; magnitude is modest and essentially identical to the sibling model, so metrics do not differentiate.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same validation setting as sibling (UKB portability framework; selected European validation; eval includes EUR/SAS; n=19,864). No independent external cohort signal beyond this framework evaluation.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Framework/portability study archetype (UKB-derived and applied within UKB ancestry groups) raises transfer-risk vs disease-focused multi-cohort studies; however covariates are basic (age/sex/PCs etc.) with low leakage risk.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Within a near-clone pair (same endpoint, cohorts, covariates, validation), the stronger structural signal is method/coverage: LDpred2 genome-wide shrinkage with 32,552 variants is more likely to capture polygenic signal than a 45-variant penalized-regression sparse score when observed performance is tied.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match: same trait_reported/phenotyping_reported and same target EFO mapping as the other candidate.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Partial correlation partial-r=0.0562 (CI 0.0424–0.0701), effectively indistinguishable from PGS002034; no PRS-only AUC/R2 to provide a clearer PRS-comparable edge.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same as sibling: European-selected validation within the same portability framework; eval includes EUR/SAS; n=19,864—no differentiating external-validation breadth.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same framework/within-UKB portability limitations and same basic covariate set; additional risk is extreme sparsity (45 variants) which can under-capture distributed signal and be less robust out of sample unless architecture is very oligogenic (not evidenced here).
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Given indistinguishable endpoint and metric evidence, the very low variant count is a negative structural signal versus the genome-wide LDpred2 sibling, making it less likely to top an external benchmark.

rationale: Both candidates are same-publication near-clones with identical endpoint, cohorts, covariates, and essentially identical partial-r performance, so reported metrics and validation context cannot separate them. The main differentiator is structural: PGS002034 uses LDpred2 with genome-wide coverage (32,552 variants) versus an extremely sparse 45-variant penalized regression score, making PGS002034 more likely to rank higher in an external performance benchmark under typical transfer conditions.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Concept label matches bipolar disorder, but phenotyping_reported is a non-disease endpoint (cognitive function: pattern comparison). This is not a direct BD case/control (or diagnosis-code) endpoint, so endpoint fidelity to the target trait is weak.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only a small full-model partial R² reported (0.00251) with basic covariates; no PGS-only AUC/R² or effect sizes. Metric is not directly comparable to disease-risk discrimination and is likely reflecting association with the non-disease phenotype rather than BD prediction.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR-only GWAS/EVAL and PGC training cohort are fine for transportability to EUR benchmarks, but validation N (~2.5k) is modest and the evaluation is on a different phenotype than the target.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: High risk of catalog/endpoint mismatch for the intended use: score is being evaluated for association with cognition, not BD status. Using it as a BD risk PRS would be poorly supported.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Low: weak endpoint fidelity dominates; even if the underlying GWAS is BD, the presented evidence package is not aligned with a BD benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Trait is bipolar I disorder (a subtype), but phenotyping_reported is again non-disease (psychiatric behavior: DSM5 depression). This is not a BD diagnosis endpoint; subtype label does not rescue the endpoint mismatch.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Small full-model partial R² (0.00275) with basic covariates; no PRS-only metrics/effect sizes. Not comparable to BD case/control performance.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR-only GWAS/EVAL; PGC training cohort; validation N (~2.2k) modest. Validation phenotype differs from target.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: High: evaluated on depression behavior rather than bipolar diagnosis; likely to underperform in a BD benchmark due to endpoint mismatch and non-comparable metric context.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Low: despite slightly higher partial R² than PGS002786, the evidence is still not benchmark-aligned to BD prediction.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Trait is bipolar II disorder (subtype), but phenotyping_reported is non-disease (psychiatric behavior: sluggish cognitive tempo). Endpoint fidelity to bipolar disorder diagnosis/risk is weakest among the three in practical benchmark terms.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Highest reported full-model partial R² (0.00307) with basic covariates, but still tiny and not PRS-only; no AUC/PRS-only R²/effect sizes. Metric is for a behavioral trait, not BD prediction.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR-only GWAS/EVAL; PGC training cohort; validation N (~2.5k) modest. Same general validation limitations as siblings.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: High: evaluated on an attention/behavior construct rather than bipolar diagnosis; strong risk that any apparent signal does not translate to BD benchmark performance.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Low-to-moderate within this weak set: all are endpoint-mismatched, so the only differentiator is the slightly stronger reported partial R² and similar transport context.

rationale: All three candidates are concept-labeled as bipolar disorder/subtypes but are evaluated against non-disease phenotypes (cognition/behavior), providing weak endpoint fidelity for a bipolar-disorder performance benchmark. With no PRS-only AUC/R² or effect-size evidence to separate them, the only usable within-shortlist signal is the (still very small) partial R² under similar covariates/ancestry/publication context; PGS002788 is marginally highest, so it is the best-supported choice among otherwise poorly benchmark-aligned options.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match: trait_reported and phenotyping_reported are Crohn's disease (no horizon/TTE packaging). Clean basic covariates (age, sex, PCs). Minor concern: publication framing is ICI-mediated colitis prediction, so the study context may be treatment/setting-specific even if the endpoint field says Crohn’s disease.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No PRS-only AUC/R² reported; only full-model AUROC=0.72 plus an OR=2.18 (likely per SD). The OR magnitude is strong supportive signal for PRS discrimination, but the AUROC is not PRS-comparable and could be partly covariate-driven.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR development and EUR evaluation; validation n=22,296 is solid. However, evidence appears to come from a narrower study context (immune checkpoint inhibitor colitis paper) rather than broad disease-focused external cohorts; limits inference about general external benchmark performance.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Key risk is comparability/transport: potential endpoint/context mismatch (therapy-mediated colitis setting) and reliance on full-model AUROC without PRS-only metrics. Training n=12,331 is modest and UKB-only, increasing risk of UKB-specific optimization.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Strong structural method/coverage (LDpred2-auto, ~745k variants) and strong OR suggest higher true PRS signal than sparse UKB framework scores, but missing PRS-only metrics and possible therapy-context specificity reduce certainty.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct Crohn’s disease endpoint (phenotyping_reported aligns; minor spelling noise only). Not TTE-packaged. Covariates are standard UKB demographic/array/PC adjustments.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Provides PRS-comparable metrics: PGS-only AUROC=0.579 and PGS-only R²=0.00677; incremental AUROC=0.027. These are modest but interpretable and below the heritability ceiling (h2_obs~0.0122), so not obviously inflated.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: From a pan-trait UKB sparse-score framework; evaluation includes multiple ancestries but selected validation ancestry is European. Validation n=24,905. Framework origin is a negative for external benchmark transfer despite clean reporting.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Primary risk is framework/sparse-model underperformance in independent benchmarks; very low variant count (257) suggests limited polygenic capture. Metrics are modest and likely reflect that limitation.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Good comparability (explicit PGS-only metrics) but typical of pan-trait sparse UKB scores that often rank below disease-focused genome-wide shrinkage models in external benchmarks.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Partial mismatch: explicitly time-to-event Crohn’s disease endpoint (TTE), which is less aligned to a generic Crohn’s disease case-control benchmark. Otherwise concept-aligned.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: PRS-comparable metrics available but slightly weaker than PGS001331 (PGS-only AUROC=0.576; PGS-only R²=0.00621; incremental AUROC=0.024). Still plausible vs heritability ceiling.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same pan-trait UKB framework family as PGS001331 with similar validation n=24,905 and mixed-ancestry evaluation; selected validation ancestry European.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Framework + sparse model risks plus added endpoint packaging risk (TTE) for a generic benchmark; no compensating metric advantage over PGS001331.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Likely to rank below PGS001331 due to TTE mismatch and slightly weaker metrics; unlikely to beat a strong genome-wide shrinkage direct endpoint model if that model transfers.

rationale: Across the shortlist, PGS004254 has the strongest structural signal for external performance (genome-wide LDpred2-auto with ~745k variants) and a strong reported effect size (OR=2.18), which together are more predictive of top benchmark rank than the modest PGS-only AUROC/R² from the sparse pan-trait UKB snpnet scores. While PGS004254 lacks PRS-only AUC/R² and has some context-specific risk (ICI-colitis framing), the two snpnet candidates are classic framework sparse models with low variant counts and modest PRS-only metrics; among them, PGS001331 is better than PGS001330, but both are less likely to rank #1 in a hidden external benchmark than a well-powered genome-wide shrinkage score if it transfers.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match to target: trait_reported and phenotyping_reported are both atrial flutter (not bundled with AF; not time-to-event). Strongest endpoint fidelity in shortlist.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Has explicit PRS-comparable metrics: PGS-only AUROC=0.617 and PGS-only R2=0.0252. R2 is plausible vs local h2_obs (~0.0157) given scale/definition differences and not obviously inflated; incremental AUROC ~0.022 suggests modest but real PRS contribution.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Evaluated in EUR (selected) with additional multi-ancestry evaluation listed; validation n=24,905. Single-biobank (UKB) framework evaluation context, but metrics are clearly reported and comparable.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Framework/pan-trait UKB sparse snpnet score ("813 traits") is a known generalization risk; relatively low variant count (2,087) consistent with sparse selection. Full-model AUROC is covariate-influenced and should not be over-weighted.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Best endpoint alignment plus available PRS-only metrics gives the cleanest, most benchmark-relevant evidence among candidates; despite framework penalty, it is the only direct atrial-flutter-specific model here.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Partial match: combines atrial fibrillation and flutter and is explicitly time-to-event (phenotyping_reported TTE). This is less faithful to the generic atrial flutter target than a direct flutter case-control style endpoint.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: PRS-only AUROC=0.613 and R2=0.0245 are slightly lower than PGS001263; incremental AUROC similar (~0.022). Metrics are usable but tied to a broader composite endpoint and TTE design.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Similar evaluation setting to PGS001263 (UKB, EUR selected; multi-ancestry listed) and same validation n=24,905, so no advantage on validation context.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same pan-trait UKB sparse snpnet framework risk as PGS001263, plus added endpoint-design risk from TTE and AF+flutter bundling.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Near-clone to PGS001263 but with weaker endpoint fidelity and slightly weaker PRS-only metrics; unlikely to outrank the direct flutter model in an external benchmark targeting flutter.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Partial match: atrial fibrillation and flutter composite (not flutter-specific). Endpoint is not time-to-event, but still broader than target.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only partial correlation reported (partial-r=0.1034); no PRS-only AUROC/R2 provided, limiting comparability to benchmark-style PRS discrimination metrics.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: UKB portability framework with EUR selected validation; n=19,230. Multi-ancestry evaluation listed, but still within-cohort portability study archetype rather than independent external cohorts.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Framework/portability paper; missing standard PRS metrics increases uncertainty. Although LDpred2 genome-wide (554,908 variants) is structurally strong, the evidence presented here is thinner for benchmark ranking.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Method/variant-count suggest potential, but lack of PRS-comparable AUROC/R2 and composite endpoint reduce confidence it would rank #1 for flutter in a hidden benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Partial match: atrial fibrillation and flutter composite (not flutter-specific).
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only partial correlation reported (partial-r=0.1026), slightly lower than PGS002050; no PRS-only AUROC/R2.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same portability framework context and validation n=19,230 as PGS002050; no clear validation advantage.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Framework/portability archetype and missing PRS-comparable metrics; penalized regression with 3,980 variants is less structurally compelling than genome-wide shrinkage here.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Weaker than its sibling PGS002050 on both structural signal and reported partial-r; unlikely top-ranked for the flutter target.

rationale: PGS001263 is the only candidate with direct atrial-flutter-specific phenotyping and it reports explicit PRS-only AUROC/R2, making its evidence most benchmark-relevant. The other candidates are composite AF+flutter (one also time-to-event) and/or lack PRS-comparable discrimination metrics, which increases uncertainty and weakens expected rank for a flutter-specific external benchmark despite some stronger method/variant-count signals.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match to target concept: trait_efo is alcohol dependence and phenotyping_reported is Alcohol use disorder (clinical disease endpoint, not a proxy/packaged risk horizon).
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No PRS-only AUC/R2 reported; has a reasonably strong stratification effect size (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96, CI 1.54–2.51), which is supportive of meaningful discrimination even without AUC/R2.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR evaluation (100%) with moderate n=7,900; multi-cohort development (MVP, UKB) suggests less single-biobank overfitting than UKB-only siblings, though covariates are unknown.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Unknown covariates reduce comparability; multi-ancestry GWAS mix is messy/unclear (percentages sum oddly) but evaluation is EUR so benchmark transfer depends on EUR setting; still not a framework-style score.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Strongest overall package in shortlist for a direct alcohol dependence endpoint: disease-focused AUD endpoint + multi-cohort development + strong OR signal; likely to transfer better than UKB-only problematic-use scores with small ΔR².

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Partial/adjacent endpoint: trait_reported is problematic alcohol use and trait_efo is alcohol dependence measurement; phenotyping is DSM-5 AUD criteria count (log-transformed), which is closer to symptom severity than a binary dependence diagnosis.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Provides PRS-comparable incremental signal (ΔR²=0.01192). This is below the local h2 ceiling (0.036) so plausible, but still modest.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR-only training (UKB) and EUR eval with n=7,599; covariates are explicitly basic (age/sex/PCs/array/site), which improves interpretability versus unknown covariates.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: UKB-only development is a transportability weakness versus multi-cohort disease-focused development; endpoint is a measurement/count phenotype rather than direct dependence diagnosis.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Good metric transparency, but modest ΔR² and less endpoint-fidelity to alcohol dependence than AUD case-control style; likely ranks below a stronger disease-endpoint model with strong OR evidence.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match on concept (trait_efo alcohol dependence; phenotyping AUD).
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No PRS-only AUC/R2; supportive effect size (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.76, CI 1.32–2.34) but weaker than PGS002738.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Evaluation is AFR-only (African American/Afro-Caribbean) with n=6,315; development includes MVP/PGC/UKB, but the score is gene-based with only 858 variants, which can limit captured polygenic signal.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Non-EUR-only evaluation is a consistent external-benchmark risk when benchmark is often EUR or mixed; very low variant count and gene-based construction increases risk of underperformance versus genome-wide PRS-CS in typical benchmarks.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Despite endpoint match, AFR-only evaluation and sparse/gene-based variant set make it less likely to top a generic external benchmark compared with a genome-wide EUR-evaluated AUD score.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Same as PGS000201: problematic alcohol use / alcohol dependence measurement with DSM-5 criteria count (log-transformed), not a clean dependence diagnosis endpoint.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: ΔR²=0.00456, notably weaker than PGS000201 and far below h2 ceiling; suggests limited PRS contribution in that setting.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR-only training (UKB) and small eval n=1,251; basic covariates listed (age/sex/PCs).
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Small validation and weaker incremental signal; UKB-only development; endpoint is measurement/count phenotype.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Within its sibling pair, it is clearly weaker on ΔR² and validation support; unlikely to rank #1 in an external benchmark.

rationale: Across the shortlist, PGS002738 has the best endpoint fidelity to alcohol dependence (AUD diagnosis-level endpoint) and the strongest available discrimination proxy (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96). It is also developed from a multi-cohort context (MVP+UKB), which is a stronger transportability signal than the UKB-only problematic-use scores (PGS000201/PGS000202) whose ΔR² signals are modest. PGS002739 matches the endpoint but is AFR-evaluated and gene-based with very low variant count, which is a higher-risk profile for topping a typical external benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Maps to the broad target EFO (blood coagulation disease) but the reported/phenotyped endpoint is a UKB pan-trait construct: “Other coagulation defects” with a time-to-event (TTE) framing, which is less faithful to a generic disease-status benchmark than a direct diagnosis-style endpoint.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Has explicit PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC ~0.634; PGS-only R² ~0.058), which is a real positive vs candidates with missing AUC/R². However, the score uses only 1 variant, making the reported signal atypical and raising concern that performance is driven by a single locus that may not transfer robustly across cohorts/phenotyping definitions.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Evaluation includes multiple ancestries overall, but the selected validation ancestry is European; validation N is large. Still, this is from a high-throughput UKB framework paper, which historically generalizes less well than disease-focused models even when internal metrics look decent.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: High framework-risk (813-traits sparse UKB), TTE endpoint mismatch risk, and extreme sparsity (1 SNP) risk; these are classic external-benchmark underperformance flags despite clean-looking catalog metrics.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Mixed: strong on metric availability, but the combination of pan-trait framework + TTE + 1-variant sparsity is a substantial negative for hidden external benchmark rank.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Trait is a specific coagulation disorder subtype (congenital deficiency of vitamin K-dependent clotting factors), which is plausibly within the broader “blood coagulation disease” umbrella; endpoint is diagnosis-like (not horizon-packaged), so fidelity is acceptable though narrower than the target.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No AUROC/R² reported; only partial correlation (partial-r ~0.056). This is weaker and less directly comparable than PRS-only AUROC/R², but at least it is a PRS-isolated metric (partialled on covariates) rather than a covariate-inflated full-model AUROC.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: UKB portability framework archetype; EUR-majority evaluation with some SAS. Validation N is modest and not a differentiator vs its sibling (PGS001826).
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Framework/portability-study penalty and missing standard discrimination metrics; however, method is genome-wide shrinkage (LDpred2) with many variants, which is structurally more likely to transfer than very sparse models when endpoints are comparable.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Among the two near-clones from the same paper/endpoint/covariates, LDpred2 with 32k variants is the stronger structural bet for external benchmark performance.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Same endpoint as PGS002034 (congenital clotting factor deficiency), acceptable but narrower-than-target match; diagnosis-like rather than risk-packaged.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Same partial-r (~0.0562) as PGS002034—effectively indistinguishable on reported performance signal.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same publication family, same ancestry mix (EUR/SAS), same validation N; no advantage over PGS002034.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Framework/portability penalty plus much smaller variant count (45) than its sibling, which reduces captured polygenic signal and is a negative structural indicator when metrics are tied.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Given near-identical endpoint and metric evidence to PGS002034, the lower-coverage penalized regression (45 variants) is less likely to rank #1 externally than the LDpred2 genome-wide score.

rationale: PGS001033 has the only explicit PRS-only AUROC/R², but its pan-trait sparse UKB origin, time-to-event endpoint, and extreme 1-variant construction are strong external-benchmark risk signals. Between the two endpoint-matched siblings (PGS002034 vs PGS001826) with essentially identical partial-r and identical validation context, the LDpred2 genome-wide model with far more variants (PGS002034) has the better structural transfer signal and is the most likely to rank highest in a hidden external benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match: trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all basal cell carcinoma; no horizon/packaging signals.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No PRS-only metrics; only full-model AUROC=0.632 and pseudo-R2=0.0487 with basic covariates, plus per-SD OR=1.663 and top1% OR=3.61. Effect-size signal is strong and comparable within this sibling set.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL; independent evaluation size n=11,322 (moderate). Same publication family as most others, so validation context is consistent.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Main risk is reliance on full-model AUROC (not PRS-comparable) and small-variant GWAS-hits construction; otherwise low covariate leakage risk (age/sex/PCs/batch only).
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Strong within-family contender but slightly weaker than the best sibling on effect-size/tie-break metrics; likely near-top but not the top pick.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match across all phenotype fields (basal cell carcinoma).
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No PRS-only metrics; full-model AUROC=0.632 (same as best), pseudo-R2=0.0489 (highest among the MGI-evaluated siblings), per-SD OR=1.661 (essentially tied for best), and top1% OR=3.79 (strong). With identical covariates, these small but consistent edges are the best available signal.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL; evaluation n=11,322; same evaluation setting as the other MGI siblings, improving comparability.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same limitations as siblings: full-model metrics only and sparse P+T with 27 variants; however covariates are basic and consistent, so comparability risk is low within this set.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Best-supported likely #1 within this near-clone cluster: highest pseudo-R2, tied-best AUROC, and strong effect sizes under identical endpoint/covariates/ancestry context.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match basal cell carcinoma across fields.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model AUROC=0.630 and pseudo-R2=0.0456 (lower than top siblings). Per-SD OR=1.633 is weaker than 452/454; top1% OR=3.95 is high but can be tail-sensitive and less stable than per-SD OR for cross-benchmark ranking.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR-only; evaluation n=11,322 in same setting as 452/454/458, so comparable but metrics are slightly weaker.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same full-model-only limitation; otherwise low leakage covariates.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Likely mid-pack among the MGI siblings due to weaker per-SD OR and pseudo-R2 despite a strong top1% OR.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match basal cell carcinoma across fields.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model AUROC=0.628 and pseudo-R2=0.0457 (below 452/454). Per-SD OR=1.634 similar to 456; top1% OR=4.03 is highest, but with slightly worse overall discrimination metrics under identical covariates.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR-only; evaluation n=11,322; same setting as other MGI siblings.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same: full-model-only metrics; sparse P+T with 23 variants may under-capture polygenic signal.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Tail-risk looks strong (top1% OR), but overall metrics are weaker than 454; less likely to rank #1 in an external benchmark focused on general discrimination.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match basal cell carcinoma across fields.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model AUROC=0.617 and pseudo-R2=0.0322 are materially lower than the MGI-evaluated siblings; per-SD OR=1.535 is also weaker. Despite larger training/validation, the observable discrimination signal is worse.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR-only; much larger evaluation n=60,018, but from a different cohort (UKB) than the other siblings, reducing direct comparability and not compensating for weaker metrics.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same full-model-only limitation; otherwise basic covariates. Risk that this is a weaker sparse hits set despite larger N.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Lower likelihood of #1 given consistently weaker AUROC/pseudo-R2/per-SD OR versus the other direct-match candidates.

rationale: All candidates are direct endpoint matches with similarly clean (basic) covariates and EUR-only context, and none reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so ranking must rely on within-family comparable signals. PGS000454 has the best overall metric package among the most comparable siblings (highest pseudo-R2, tied-best AUROC, and strong per-SD/top-tail ORs under identical endpoint/covariates/validation setting), making it the most likely to rank highest in an external benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match: trait_reported and trait_efo are aortic stenosis; phenotyping is incident aortic stenosis (acceptable disease endpoint, though incident-only).
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only full-model discrimination is shown (C-index 0.87) plus HR=1.92; the high C-index is likely covariate-inflated given the very heavy clinical covariate set, but the per-SD HR is strong and is the most PRS-informative metric available here.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR-only dev/eval; very large evaluation sample (n=446,895) and multiple records, but no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported, limiting comparability.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Major comparability risk: covariates include multiple comorbidities/clinical factors (T2D, HTN, CAD, hyperlipidemia, BMI, smoking, renal failure), so the reported C-index is not a clean PRS signal; incident-only endpoint may under/over-estimate general disease status depending on benchmark definition.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Strong endpoint fidelity + strongest available PRS-proxy effect size (HR) among direct AS candidates; method is strong (LDpred2, genome-wide). Despite covariate inflation risk, the HR suggests robust PRS contribution, giving good odds of top external-benchmark rank.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match aortic stenosis with incident aortic stenosis phenotyping; good alignment.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No AUC/R2; HR=1.64 (moderate-strong) provides some PRS signal but weaker than PGS005252.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR dev/eval; large eval n=244,450 but only one record and limited metric detail.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Cleaner/basic covariates (age, age^2, sex, PCs) reduce metric inflation risk, but absence of PRS-only metrics still limits cross-model comparability; overall signal relies on HR alone.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Good endpoint and clean covariates, but weaker HR than PGS005252 and no other performance metrics; likely ranks below the strongest-effect direct AS score.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Trait_reported is mean pressure gradient (a measurement) though phenotyping_reported says incident aortic stenosis; partial mismatch/ambiguity versus a pure disease-risk score.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No AUC/R2; HR=1.53 (moderate) weaker than the other AS-labeled candidates.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR dev/eval; eval n=244,450 but minimal reporting (single record).
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Endpoint labeling suggests a measurement-focused construction; even if evaluated on incident AS, this increases uncertainty about benchmark alignment for disease-risk prediction.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Weaker effect size and less direct trait labeling than the AS-risk sibling (PGS005254); unlikely to be top-ranked in an external AS benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Trait_reported is peak aortic velocity (measurement) with phenotyping_reported incident aortic stenosis; similar partial mismatch/ambiguity as PGS005255.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No AUC/R2; HR=1.53 (moderate) similar to PGS005255 and weaker than AS-risk candidates.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR dev/eval; eval n=244,450; single record with limited metric detail.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Measurement-trait framing raises benchmark alignment risk for aortic stenosis disease prediction; otherwise covariates are basic.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Comparable to PGS005255 and likely below the direct AS-risk scores due to weaker HR and less direct endpoint framing.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Not a match: hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (different disease) with corresponding phenotyping; does not align to aortic stenosis.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Reports AUROC 0.8 and R2 0.048, but for a different endpoint; not usable for direct-match AS benchmarking.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR evaluation with large n=343,182, but irrelevant to target endpoint.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Explicit endpoint mismatch dominates; any apparent metric strength is non-transferable evidence in a direct-match selection task.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Very low likelihood to rank #1 for an aortic stenosis benchmark due to endpoint mismatch.

rationale: Among the direct aortic stenosis candidates, all lack PRS-only AUC/R2, so effect-size strength and structural signals dominate. PGS005252 has the strongest PRS-proxy effect size (HR=1.92 per SD) and a strong genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with direct incident AS phenotyping. Its full-model C-index is discounted due to heavy covariates, but the HR still indicates the largest standalone genetic signal in the shortlist, making it the most likely to top an external AS performance benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match on trait_reported/efo; phenotyping is explicit (prevalent AAA), which is acceptable for generic AAA risk but slightly less ideal than broader/incident-inclusive definitions.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No PRS-comparable AUC/R2 reported; has OR per SD=1.37 (moderate signal, not standout). Small 29-variant P+T structure limits polygenic capture versus genome-wide shrinkage competitors.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Has a reasonably sized EUR-selected validation record (n=46,564) and also mixed-ancestry evaluation overall, but the selected performance record lacks comparable discrimination metrics.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Sparse variant set + older P+T approach increases risk of underperformance in external benchmarks; missing AUC/R2 reduces confidence.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Moderate: disease-focused context helps, but limited SNP count and only moderate OR without PRS-only metrics makes it less likely to be top-ranked versus genome-wide disease-meta-analysis PRS-CS scores.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match AAA endpoint; disease-focused GWAS meta-analysis context with explicit AAA phenotype and basic demographic covariates.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only full-model C-index=0.882 reported; with covariates limited to age/age^2/sex, this is less likely to be heavily clinically inflated, but still not PRS-only. No OR/HR or PRS-only R2 to isolate PRS contribution.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR evaluation (n=7,517). Single performance record limits robustness evidence, but the study archetype is strongly disease-focused and multi-cohort.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Main risk is metric comparability (full-model only) and modest validation size; otherwise method (PRS-CS) and genome-wide variant count are strong structural signals.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: High: among direct-match options, this is the cleanest disease-focused, genome-wide shrinkage score; the very high full-model discrimination with only basic covariates is at least consistent with a strong underlying model and beats framework/portability candidates on archetype.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match AAA endpoint; same Nat Genet study family as PGS003973, so endpoint alignment is strong.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Reports AUROC=0.69 but covariates are unknown, making comparability unclear; despite same PRS-CS and variant count as PGS003973, the reported discrimination is much lower.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR evaluation (n=6,940) with 3 records, but no clear PRS-only metric and the headline AUROC is not compelling relative to sibling.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Unknown covariates + materially weaker reported AUROC than near-clone sibling suggests either a different evaluation setup or weaker model instantiation; higher risk of not ranking #1.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Moderate: same strong study/method backbone, but the weaker reported metric and unclear covariates reduce likelihood of topping the benchmark compared with PGS003973.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match AAA label, but comes from a UKB portability/framework-style sweep rather than a disease-focused AAA study.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only partial-r=0.0144 (very small). This is PRS-comparable but indicates weak signal; consistent with low heritability ceiling context.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Multi-ancestry evaluation overall with a EUR-selected record (n=19,545), but the framework archetype limits expectation of top benchmark performance.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Framework/portability penalty + weak metric signal; despite LDpred2 and many variants, the observed partial-r is not competitive.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Low: unlikely to outrank disease-focused PRS-CS meta-analysis candidates given weak reported PRS signal.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match AAA endpoint, but from a global biobank PRS lessons/framework paper rather than a single-disease optimized effort.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Provides PRS-comparable Nagelkerke R2 (covariates regressed out)=0.014661, similar magnitude to PGS002054; full-model AUROC=0.868 is not PRS-only and likely largely demographic-driven. R2 is below the provided h2_liability ceiling (~0.02), so plausible but modest.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Very large EUR evaluation (n=350,767) increases stability of the modest PRS-only R2 estimate, but size is a weak differentiator versus archetype/method/endpoint.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Framework penalty remains; PRS-only R2 is modest and does not suggest top-tier benchmark performance against a disease-focused meta-analysis PRS-CS score.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Moderate-Low: better metric transparency than many (has PRS-only R2), but the magnitude is small and framework origin makes #1 benchmark rank less likely than PGS003973.

rationale: All candidates are direct endpoint matches, so the decision turns on study archetype + structural method signals under limited PRS-only metrics. PGS003973 is from a disease-focused AAA GWAS meta-analysis and uses genome-wide PRS-CS with basic demographic covariates; this combination most consistently transfers well in external benchmarks. Competing framework/portability scores (PGS001784, PGS002054) report modest PRS-only signal, and the older sparse P+T score (PGS000753) has limited variant coverage and only moderate OR evidence. Between the Nat Genet siblings, PGS003973 has the stronger reported discrimination signal and cleaner covariate disclosure.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct DCM endpoint (phenotyping_reported: Dilated cardiomyopathy) and EUR eval; however trait_reported is MTAG which is acceptable but not as explicitly clinical as the newer study’s “Clinical dilated cardiomyopathy”.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only full-model AUROC/R² shown (AUROC 0.71; R² 0.05) with basic covariates; lacks PRS-only metrics, so AUROC is not directly comparable as PRS performance. OR per SD 1.76 is strong supportive signal.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Large EUR validation (n=347,585) is supportive but is a weak differentiator; single record only.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Main risk is metric comparability: full-model AUROC likely partly covariate-driven; no incremental/PRS-only AUC/R² to isolate PRS contribution.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Good endpoint match and strong OR, but weaker benchmark-transfer signal than candidates that report explicit PRS-only AUC/delta-R² and are anchored to a clearly clinical endpoint.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct DCM endpoint (phenotyping_reported: Dilated cardiomyopathy) with EUR GWAS/EVAL; non-MTAG sibling of PGS004862.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only full-model AUROC/R² (AUROC 0.70; R² 0.048) with basic covariates; OR 1.56 is still strong but weaker than PGS004862/PGS004951/PGS004949.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Large EUR validation (n=347,585), single record.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same comparability risk as PGS004862 plus weaker effect-size signal.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Within its sibling pair it looks dominated by PGS004862 (slightly better AUROC/R² and materially higher OR), so unlikely to be #1 overall.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Strong direct match: phenotyping_reported is explicitly “Clinical dilated cardiomyopathy”; trait_reported is MTAG but still aligned. EUR evaluation (100%) supports typical benchmark transfer to EUR settings.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Has explicit PRS-only metric (Univariate PRS-only AUC 0.67, CI 0.65–0.69) plus delta PRS/residual liability-scale R² 0.101 and Nagelkerke delta 0.076—cleaner PRS-isolated signal than full-model AUROC. OR per SD 1.93 is the strongest in the shortlist. PRS-only R² (0.101) is below the provided h2_liability ceiling (~0.17), passing sanity.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Validation n=7,761 is smaller, but the presence of PRS-only metrics and strong effect size provides higher-quality validation evidence than large-N full-model-only reports.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Smaller validation sample increases uncertainty; GWAS is mixed EUR/MAE which can slightly shift optimization away from pure EUR, but evaluation is EUR and PRS-only metrics mitigate interpretability risk.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Best combination of endpoint fidelity + PRS-isolated performance reporting + strongest OR; these are the most benchmark-predictive signals in this shortlist.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Phenotyping_reported is “Non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy” (subtype) rather than generic DCM; still close but not perfectly aligned to broad DCM benchmark endpoints. Evaluation is MAE (100%), which may mismatch a EUR-heavy benchmark.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Reports PRS-only AUC 0.68 (CI 0.66–0.69) and delta liability-scale R² 0.095; OR 1.91 is very strong. However, evaluation ancestry/endpoint subtype reduce direct comparability to a generic DCM benchmark.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Large validation (n=326,106) is supportive; PRS-only metrics present.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Primary risks are endpoint specificity (non-ischemic subtype) and evaluation in MAE-only, which can depress rank in a EUR benchmark or create transport mismatch.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Strong PRS-only metrics and OR, but likely ranks below PGS004951 due to subtype endpoint and non-EUR evaluation context for typical external benchmarks.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Non-ischemic DCM subtype endpoint; evaluation MAE-only. Less direct match than generic/clinical DCM in EUR.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: PRS-only AUC 0.66 (CI 0.63–0.68) and delta liability-scale R² 0.076; OR 1.73 strong but weaker than PGS004951/PGS004949.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Moderate validation size (n=96,016) with PRS-only metrics.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Subtype endpoint + MAE-only evaluation are the main transfer risks; metrics are also weaker than the closest sibling (PGS004949).
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Unlikely #1 given weaker PRS-only metrics and less benchmark-aligned endpoint/ancestry context.

rationale: Across the shortlist, PGS004951 has the strongest benchmark-relevant evidence package: (1) highest endpoint fidelity via an explicitly clinical DCM phenotype, (2) the cleanest PRS-isolated performance reporting (PRS-only AUC plus delta R²) rather than relying on full-model AUROC, and (3) the strongest per-SD effect size (OR 1.93). Although its validation n is smaller, the PRS-only metrics and effect size are more predictive of external benchmark rank than large-N full-model-only AUROC from the older sibling pair.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Strong direct match: trait_reported and phenotyping_reported are both Alcohol-associated liver cirrhosis; aligns cleanly to target alcoholic liver cirrhosis without subtype/time-horizon packaging.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Weak-to-moderate and somewhat ambiguous: reports R²=0.029 (listed as “Proportion of variance explained” and also as full_model_r2), plus a strong stratification OR (top vs bottom deciles) 4.4 (wide CI). No PRS-only AUROC/R² explicitly, so comparability is limited; R² magnitude is plausible under the provided heritability ceiling (h2_liability ~0.11).
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Moderate: explicit EUR evaluation with n=3,360 and basic covariates (age, sex, PCs). Disease-focused heavy-drinker context may be closer to an enriched-risk setting than a general-population benchmark, but still endpoint-faithful.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Main risks are (i) small variant count (20; C+T style) potentially under-capturing polygenic signal, and (ii) performance reporting not clearly PRS-only. However, covariates are clean (no biomarker/clinical leakage).
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Good endpoint fidelity + clean covariates + disease-focused design are positive for external benchmark transfer; metric evidence is not as directly comparable as a PRS-only AUROC/R², but overall looks more benchmark-aligned than a pan-trait UKB framework score or a 3-variant legacy score.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Concept-level match (alcohol-related cirrhosis) but phenotyping_reported is “Cirrhosis (males)”, introducing endpoint ambiguity/restriction relative to generic alcoholic liver cirrhosis.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Mixed/discounted: full-model AUROC 0.671 is not PRS-comparable; strong OR (top 20% vs bottom 20%) 6.18 suggests meaningful stratification, but without per-SD effect or PRS-only metric it’s harder to compare across studies and may reflect thresholding on a very small SNP set.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Limited: EUR eval n=1,390; covariates unknown (unclear comparability/possible augmentation). Single-cohort (MyCode) context suggests narrower transportability evidence.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: High risk of underpowered/overfit or architecture-mismatch due to extremely sparse 3-variant score; endpoint restriction (males) and unknown covariates reduce confidence in benchmark transfer.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Despite a large top-vs-bottom OR, the combination of male-only phenotype ambiguity, unknown covariates, and ultra-sparse construction is a weaker signal for ranking #1 in an external benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct label match (Alcoholic cirrhosis) and phenotyping_reported matches; however, it appears as part of a broad UKB-driven framework-style paper rather than a cirrhosis-focused development/validation effort.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model C-index 0.711 is not PRS-only; HR 1.18 (likely per SD) indicates weak-to-moderate standalone PRS signal. No PRS-only AUROC/R² to support strong benchmark performance.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Large evaluation n=135,300 with mostly EUR (plus some MAE), and covariates are basic (age time-scale, sex, batch, PCs), which is clean. But the evaluation is still largely within the same UKB ecosystem archetype.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Framework/single-biobank optimization risk: very large genome-wide model (183k variants, snpnet) can look strong internally yet transfer less well than disease-focused scores; modest HR suggests limited incremental genetic discrimination.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Big N and clean covariates help, but weak effect-size signal (HR 1.18) and framework-style origin reduce likelihood of being the top external-benchmark performer versus a disease-focused, endpoint-targeted score.

rationale: Across the shortlist, all candidates lack clean PRS-only AUROC/R², so endpoint fidelity + study archetype + covariate cleanliness and effect-size plausibility drive the decision. PGS004913 is the most endpoint-faithful and disease-focused (alcohol-associated cirrhosis among heavy drinkers) with clean basic covariates and a plausible variance-explained signal plus supportive stratification OR. PGS000704 has cleaner covariates and huge N but shows weak HR and carries a framework/single-biobank transfer penalty; PGS001777 is ultra-sparse with male-only phenotype ambiguity and unknown covariates, increasing external-benchmark risk.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match: trait_efo=breast carcinoma and phenotyping_reported=Breast cancer; no horizon/packaging/subtype restriction indicated.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No PRS-only metrics; only full-model AUROC/R² reported, so cross-study comparability is limited. Within this near-clone set (same eval context/covariates), it has the top full-model AUROC (0.6625) and top R² (0.0764) plus strongest per-SD effect sizes (OR 1.83, β 0.602), giving the best available discrimination signal among siblings.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same publication family and same validation setting as others (selected_validation_ancestry=European; eval includes EUR/SAS; n=48,968). Record_count identical, so validation breadth doesn’t differentiate; still a reasonably sized external-style evaluation within the five-biobank benchmarking context.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Covariates field is '0' (clean/no clinical augmentation), reducing risk of covariate-inflated performance, but also means the reported AUROC is still a full-model metric and not directly PRS-only. Training/dev appears UKB-only (n=12,483), so potential UKB-centric optimization; however this risk is shared across the shortlist.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Strongest tie-break profile in a tightly matched sibling cluster: ensemble/multi-score method (MultiPRS.CV) aligns with structural evidence that ensembling tends to outperform single-method scores, and it also leads the sibling set on AUROC/R² and OR. Most likely to rank #1 in an external benchmark among these candidates.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match (breast carcinoma / Breast cancer) with consistent phenotype labeling.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only full-model metrics; slightly lower AUROC (0.6598) and R² (0.0739) and slightly weaker OR (1.81) than the top sibling, suggesting marginally weaker PRS signal within this identical evaluation frame.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same validation ancestry mix and sample size as the rest; no differentiating external-validation advantage.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same shared risks: full-model-only reporting and UKB-only dev; covariates listed as 0 (clean).
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Good genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2.CV) but loses on the only available within-family performance/effect-size signals and lacks the ensemble advantage.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match (breast carcinoma / Breast cancer) with consistent phenotype labeling.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model AUROC/R² essentially tied with PGS004040 but fractionally lower; OR (1.81) also slightly lower than the top candidate. LDpred2-auto can be strong, but here it does not show an empirical edge in the provided evaluation record.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same validation context and size; no added robustness signal.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same shared risks: full-model-only metrics; UKB-only dev; covariates=0 (clean).
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Near-clone to LDpred2.CV in this evaluation and not the top performer; unlikely to outrank the ensemble sibling in a hidden benchmark given no superior metric/effect-size evidence.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match (breast carcinoma / Breast cancer) with consistent phenotype labeling.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Lowest AUROC (0.6553), lowest R² (0.0697), and weakest OR (1.77) in the shortlist, indicating weaker discriminative signal within the same evaluation frame.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same validation context/size; no compensating advantage.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same shared risks (full-model-only; UKB-only dev; covariates=0).
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Despite a strong method family (PRS-CS-auto), the observed within-family performance signals are consistently lower, making #1 benchmark rank less likely.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match (breast carcinoma / Breast cancer) with consistent phenotype labeling.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model AUROC/R² modestly above PRS-CS-auto but still clearly below the top three; OR (1.78) also below the leader. Variant count is also the lowest (869k), a mild negative structural signal versus other genome-wide scores here.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same validation context/size; no differentiating advantage.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same shared risks (full-model-only; UKB-only dev; covariates=0).
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Middle-lower empirical signal within identical evaluation; unlikely to beat the ensemble or top LDpred2 siblings in an external benchmark.

rationale: All candidates are endpoint-identical near-clones from the same study family with the same (full-model-only) metric type, covariate setting (0), and validation context, so small AUROC differences alone are weak. The most reliable differentiators available are (i) consistent within-family superiority across AUROC, R², and per-SD OR/β and (ii) the structural advantage of an ensemble/multi-score method. PGS004153 leads on all of these, making it the best-supported pick to rank highest in a hidden external benchmark among this shortlist.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match (coeliac disease) with coherent trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported; no subtype restriction. Strong endpoint fidelity for generic celiac disease benchmarking.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only full-model AUROC reported (0.879, tight CI). No PGS-only AUROC/R2, so discrimination is not directly comparable as PRS signal; could be partly covariate-driven (covariates unknown).
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Very large evaluation sample size (n=379,767) and EUR evaluation listed; however ancestry string includes NR (50%) which adds some metadata ambiguity. Still suggests substantial evaluation support.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Main risk is metric comparability: full-model AUROC with unknown covariates; also relatively small variant set (53) could under-capture polygenic signal depending on architecture.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Good endpoint fidelity and large evaluation support help, but lack of PRS-only metrics makes it harder to justify as top performer versus a candidate with explicit PGS-only AUC/R2.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Trait label is broader (malabsorption/coeliac disease) but still explicitly includes coeliac disease; phenotyping_reported matches that combined endpoint. Slight endpoint impurity versus pure celiac diagnosis, but still close.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Strongest PRS-comparable evidence in the shortlist: PGS-only AUROC 0.8287 (CI given) and PGS-only R2 0.1422; full-model AUROC 0.8335. Reported PRS-only R2 is below the provided liability h2 ceiling (0.2305), so passes sanity check.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Evaluation in EUR (selected) with additional non-EUR representation in the study (AFR/SAS listed), suggesting some breadth; validation n=67,425 is moderate but adequate and metrics are explicitly PRS-only.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Comes from a pan-trait UKB framework paper ("across 813 traits"), which is a known external-transfer risk; endpoint is a combined phenotype (malabsorption/coeliac) rather than a clean disease-only definition.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Despite framework penalty, it is the only candidate with clean PRS-only AUC and R2 plus basic covariates, giving the clearest signal for likely benchmark ranking; sanity-check-consistent R2 strengthens credibility.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match (coeliac disease) with clean phenotyping_reported; strong endpoint fidelity.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Reports AUROC=0.9 but appears to be full-model/classification AUROC without explicit PGS-only labeling; no PRS-only AUC/R2 provided, so cross-model comparability is weak.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR-only dev/eval and disease-focused publication context; validation n=2,476 is small/moderate and could be optimistic depending on design.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Key risk is over-interpreting a non-PRS-only AUROC; limited validation size and older/smaller training set reduce confidence in top external benchmark performance.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Disease-focused and endpoint-faithful, but missing PRS-only metrics makes it hard to justify beating the candidate with explicit PGS-only AUC/R2 in a hidden benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Endpoint is explicitly restricted to HLA-DQ2.5 carriers (subgroup), not generic celiac disease; this is a meaningful endpoint mismatch for a general celiac benchmark.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model AUROC 0.73 (CI provided) with no PRS-only metrics; modest discrimination and not directly comparable.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR evaluation; validation n=1,237 is small and subgroup-specific.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Subgroup-only (HLA-positive) design is the dominant risk; likely to underperform or be non-comparable in a general-population benchmark.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Low: endpoint restriction plus modest AUROC and small validation make it unlikely to rank #1 in a generic external benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Same subgroup restriction as PGS000042 (coeliac disease in HLA-DQ2.5 carriers), so not a direct general celiac endpoint match.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model AUROC 0.718 (CI provided), no PRS-only metrics; slightly weaker than PGS000042.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR evaluation; validation n=1,237 small and subgroup-specific.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same major endpoint mismatch (HLA-carrier-only) plus modest discrimination.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Low: unlikely to top a general celiac disease benchmark given subgroup endpoint and weaker AUROC.

rationale: Across the shortlist, PGS001301 is the only candidate providing clearly PRS-comparable performance (PGS-only AUROC and PGS-only R2) with basic covariates and a heritability-sane R2, which is the strongest available signal for likely external benchmark ranking. The main counterweight is its pan-trait UKB framework origin and slightly broader combined endpoint, but the competing direct-endpoint candidates largely lack PRS-only metrics (and two are subgroup-only), making their apparent AUROCs less reliable for predicting benchmark rank.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match: trait_reported/efo/phenotyping all coronary artery disease with no horizon/packaging qualifiers; endpoint fidelity is clean.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No PRS-only AUC/R2 reported; relies on effect sizes. OR per SD ~2.14 and HR ~1.75 are very strong discrimination signals among this shortlist (stronger than sibling scores and older scores here).
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Large evaluation (n=308,264) with explicitly multi-ancestry EVAL distribution; selected validation ancestry shown as European but overall breadth suggests robustness/transportability evidence beyond EUR-only.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Main risk is lack of PRS-comparable AUC/R2 and reliance on effect sizes; otherwise covariates are basic (age/sex/PCs) with low leakage risk.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Strong: disease-focused CAD paper family, genome-wide shrinkage (LDpred2), high variant count, and strongest OR/HR among near-clone siblings; multi-ancestry evaluation context supports external benchmark transfer.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct CAD match with clean phenotyping and basic covariates; essentially same endpoint family as PGS003725.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only HR reported (~1.73), strong but slightly weaker than PGS003725 and lacks the additional strong OR evidence.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Similarly large validation (n=308,264) with multi-ancestry EVAL; fewer performance records than PGS003725 (not very meaningful).
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same main limitation: missing PRS-only AUC/R2; otherwise low covariate leakage risk.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Good but slightly behind the strongest sibling due to weaker effect-size signal and less corroborating metric variety.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct CAD match; clean endpoint and basic covariates.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: HR (~1.67) is still strong but clearly weaker than PGS003725/PGS003726; variant count also lower than those siblings.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Large validation (n=308,264) with multi-ancestry EVAL; training cohort list is narrower (CARDIoGRAMplusC4D, UKB) which is a mild transportability weakness vs broader siblings.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Missing PRS-only AUC/R2; otherwise low leakage risk.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Moderate: same study family but appears to be a weaker sibling (lower HR, fewer variants, narrower training context).

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct CAD match; phenotyping is CAD and covariates are basic (age/sex/PCs plus possible technical covariates).
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only OR (~1.64) reported; respectable but materially weaker than PGS003725’s OR/HR signals. No PRS-only AUC/R2.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Large validation (n=343,676) and multi-ancestry GWAS context; however this is a broad 'common diseases across ancestries' framework-style paper, which is a negative generalization signal when a disease-focused alternative exists.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Framework/pan-disease archetype risk (scores not optimized per disease as strongly as disease-focused CAD work); metrics remain effect-size-only.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Moderate-to-low: despite size and LDpred, the framework-study penalty plus weaker effect size makes it less likely to top an external CAD benchmark than the Nat Med CAD-focused LDpred2 sibling with stronger OR/HR.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Mostly direct but phenotyping explicitly 'Coronary artery disease (prevalent)' which is a mild endpoint mismatch vs generic CAD risk; still acceptable but less ideal than non-qualified CAD endpoints.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Reports full-model AUROC 0.89, but this is not PRS-only and is likely largely covariate-driven; OR (~1.6) is weaker than PGS003725 and similar to PGS002244.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Validation sample size is small (n=3,309) relative to others; many records but record_count is not predictive.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: High risk of overinterpreting full-model AUROC; older metaGRS construction and small training n=3,000 also raise robustness concerns versus newer genome-wide shrinkage scores.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Low: apparent AUC advantage is non-comparable; weaker effect size and much smaller validation make it unlikely to rank #1 in a hidden external benchmark against the newer disease-focused LDpred2 scores.

rationale: All candidates are direct CAD matches and most lack PRS-only AUC/R2, so the most reliable differentiators are (i) endpoint cleanliness, (ii) strength of PRS-linked effect sizes, and (iii) disease-focused study/transportability context. PGS003725 is a clean-endpoint LDpred2 genome-wide score from a CAD-focused multi-ancestry study family and shows the strongest effect-size evidence (notably OR~2.14 and HR~1.75) among the near-clone siblings, making it the most likely to rank highest in an external CAD benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct EFO match to arthritis with broad/unspecified phenotype label (Arthritis (nos)); acceptable for a generic arthritis target but endpoint is vague and likely heterogeneous.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Has PRS-comparable metrics: PGS-only AUROC 0.539 and PGS-only R2 0.00291 (below the provided h2_liability ceiling; modest but interpretable). Full-model AUROC ~0.67 with tiny incremental AUROC (0.003) indicates most discrimination is covariate-driven.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: UKB-based development with EUR dev; evaluation includes multiple ancestries but selected validation record is EUR; validation n~24.9k is moderate. Multiple records exist but all within the same framework family.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Strong framework-paper risk (pan-trait sparse snpnet across 813 traits) and sparse variant count (~1k) consistent with weaker external transfer despite clean reporting.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Moderate: best among candidates for having explicit PRS-only metrics on an arthritis endpoint, but framework/sparsity and low PRS-only signal limit likelihood of topping an external benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: EFO maps to arthritis; phenotype is ICD10 M13 'Other arthritis'—a narrower/administrative subtype rather than generic arthritis, but still reasonably aligned to the umbrella target.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No AUROC/R2 reported; only OR per SD ~1.26 suggests weak-to-moderate PRS discrimination signal (below ~1.3 threshold for clearly moderate).
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR-only dev/eval in UKB; validation n~56k is decent but does not compensate for missing comparable metrics and single-biobank context.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Covariates unknown; method is a meta/ensemble-style 'RFDiseasemetaPRS' which is structurally promising, but lack of transparent PRS-only performance makes comparability uncertain.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Moderate-low: potentially better structure than sparse framework scores, but the weak OR and missing PRS-comparable metrics reduce confidence it would rank #1 externally.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Same endpoint as PGS004547 (ICD10 M13 Other arthritis); reasonable but not perfectly generic arthritis.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No AUROC/R2; OR per SD ~1.20 indicates weak PRS signal.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR-only UKB dev/eval; validation n~56k. Single record, limited robustness evidence.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Unknown covariates; despite LDpred2 being a strong method family, the observed effect size is weak and there is no PRS-only metric to support top performance.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Low: weaker effect-size evidence than its sibling (PGS004547) and no compensating validation/metric advantages.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Endpoint is juvenile idiopathic arthritis (different disease entity than generic adult 'arthritis'); this is a clear endpoint mismatch for the target trait.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Reports full-model AUROC 0.738 and OR ~2.09, which look strong, but they apply to a different endpoint and cannot be assumed to transfer to generic arthritis.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR-only with small validation (n~940) and modest training size; multi-cohort dev is a plus but limited by endpoint mismatch and small eval.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: High risk of non-transfer due to pediatric-onset specific phenotype; performance likely not representative for generic arthritis benchmarking.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Low: despite strong within-endpoint metrics, mismatch makes it unlikely to rank #1 for a generic arthritis benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Osteoarthritis is a specific arthritis subtype; partial match to generic arthritis but not an exact umbrella endpoint.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Has PRS-comparable metrics but weaker than PGS001135: PGS-only AUROC 0.522 and PGS-only R2 0.00109. Full-model AUROC ~0.67 with very small incremental AUROC (0.0013) again suggests covariate-driven discrimination.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same UKB pan-trait snpnet framework family; validation n~67k (largest among the snpnet pair) but validation size is a weak differentiator.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Framework/sparse-model transfer risk similar to PGS001135; additionally endpoint is narrower (OA) than generic arthritis target.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Low-moderate: weaker PRS-only signal and less direct endpoint than PGS001135, so less likely to top an external generic-arthritis benchmark.

rationale: Across the shortlist, PGS001135 is the only candidate with a direct arthritis endpoint (EFO=arthritis) plus explicit PRS-comparable performance (PGS-only AUROC/R2). The two 2024 M13 'Other arthritis' models have more modern/stronger method labels but provide only modest-to-weak ORs and no AUROC/R2, making them harder to justify as likely external-benchmark #1. PGS001290 is subtype-mismatched (osteoarthritis) and has weaker PRS-only metrics. PGS000114 has strong metrics but is a clear endpoint mismatch (juvenile idiopathic arthritis). Framework-origin risk keeps confidence from being high, but within the available evidence PGS001135 has the strongest benchmark-rank signal.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match: trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all ankylosing spondylitis (non-TTE).
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only partial correlation reported (partial-r=0.0919, EUR eval). This is PRS-comparable but weaker/less standard than explicit PGS-only AUROC/R²; still indicates non-trivial signal.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Portability-style evaluation with EUR primary plus some non-EUR groups; selected validation ancestry European; eval n=18,262 (moderate).
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Framework/portability paper (UKB-derived applied across ancestry groups) can be less externally robust than disease-focused multi-cohort studies; however covariates are basic (age/sex/PCs etc.) and endpoint is clean.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Good structural method (LDpred2, genome-wide shrinkage; 22k variants) and clean endpoint, but lacks strong comparable metrics (no PGS-only AUROC/R²) which reduces rank confidence versus candidates with explicit PRS-only metrics.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match ankylosing spondylitis; phenotype is straightforward case/control style (not TTE).
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Has explicit PRS-comparable metrics: PGS-only AUROC=0.7265 and PGS-only R²=0.0988 (below heritability ceiling; plausible). Also reports full-model AUROC=0.7433 with incremental AUROC=0.1299.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Large UKB-based evaluation (selected EUR; eval n=67,425) with multi-ancestry evaluation records listed; covariates are basic (age/sex/array/PCs).
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Pan-trait UKB framework ("across 813 traits") and extremely sparse model (10 variants) raises external-transfer risk despite clean metrics; may underperform more disease-optimized genome-wide scores in hidden benchmarks.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Strongest direct PRS-only metric evidence in the shortlist for the exact endpoint; despite framework penalty, the combination of explicit PGS-only AUROC/R² and clean covariates is a strong predictor of benchmark ranking.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Partial mismatch: time-to-event (TTE) ankylosing spondylitis rather than generic disease status; still same disease concept but endpoint form differs.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Explicit PRS-comparable metrics slightly higher than PGS001267: PGS-only AUROC=0.7346, PGS-only R²=0.1023 (plausible vs heritability ceiling). Full-model AUROC=0.7488.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same evaluation setting as sibling (UKB; selected EUR; eval n=67,425; basic covariates).
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same pan-trait sparse framework and 10-variant sparsity risk; plus TTE endpoint can reduce comparability to typical case/control benchmark endpoints.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Near-clone of PGS001267 with marginally better metrics but weaker endpoint fidelity for a generic ankylosing spondylitis benchmark; likely ranks just behind the non-TTE sibling if the benchmark uses standard case/control.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match ankylosing spondylitis.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only partial correlation reported (partial-r=0.0797), weaker than PGS002089 and far less informative than explicit PGS-only AUROC/R².
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same portability paper context as PGS002089; EUR-selected eval; n=18,262.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Framework/portability context and missing standard metrics; method is penalized regression with 85 variants (not clearly superior here).
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Dominated by PGS002089 within the same study family (lower partial-r) and by PGS001267/PGS001268 on metric completeness; unlikely #1.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match ankylosing spondylitis, but anchored to Taiwanese/EAS context; may not match a EUR-oriented benchmark setting.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only full-model AUROC=0.7886 reported; no PGS-only AUROC/R², and covariates are unknown, so the AUROC is not reliably attributable to PRS.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EAS-only evaluation with small n=1,298; limited robustness signal.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Non-comparable metric (full-model only) + unknown covariates + small eval + ancestry specificity increases risk of overranking.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Despite high AUROC, evidence is not PRS-comparable and transportability is uncertain; low likelihood to top a general hidden benchmark.
