rationale: Among direct-match endpoints, PGS001267 provides the cleanest PRS-comparable performance evidence (explicit PGS-only AUROC and R² with basic covariates) in a large EUR evaluation context. PGS001268 has slightly higher metrics but a time-to-event endpoint that is less likely to align with a generic ankylosing spondylitis benchmark. The LDpred2/portability scores (PGS002089/PGS001876) have cleaner method structure but lack standard PRS-only metrics, and PGS003420’s high AUROC is full-model/unknown-covariate and EAS-specific with small validation.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match to target concept: trait_efo is bilirubin metabolism disease; phenotyping is a direct disease endpoint (“Disorders of bilirubin excretion”). Not time-to-event or composite.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only partial correlation reported (partial-r=0.0716 in EUR eval). No PRS-only R2/AUC, so discrimination strength is hard to compare; partial-r suggests modest signal.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: From a portability study with UKB-derived score; EUR selected validation with n=19,924 and additional multi-ancestry eval context listed, but the chosen metric is still within the same cohort ecosystem (UKB).
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Framework/portability archetype (not disease-focused) is a negative for external benchmark transfer. Very small variant count (22) for penalized regression also raises risk of under-capturing polygenic signal.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Weaker than its sibling PGS002032 because endpoint/covariates/metric are essentially identical but structural capacity (variant count/method) is lower; likely not the top performer in an external benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Same direct endpoint alignment as PGS001824: bilirubin metabolism disease via “Disorders of bilirubin excretion”; no TTE/composite complication.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Same reported EUR partial-r=0.0716 (modest). No PRS-only R2/AUC, limiting direct performance inference; however, within this near-clone family, method/structure becomes the differentiator.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same portability-study context and same selected EUR validation (n=19,924). Multi-ancestry evaluation exists in the study, but the selected record is EUR; still largely UKB-internal portability evaluation.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Portability/framework origin remains a transfer risk, but LDpred2 genome-wide shrinkage with 19,768 variants is structurally more likely to generalize and capture polygenic signal than a 22-variant penalized-regression sparse score.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Best bet among the two direct-match portability siblings: identical endpoint and identical observed partial-r, but stronger method family and much larger variant set typically ranks higher in external benchmarks when other evidence is tied.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Partial mismatch: phenotype is time-to-event and composite (“Disorders of porphyrin and bilirubin metabolism”), not a clean bilirubin-only disease endpoint. This reduces fidelity versus the direct bilirubin-excretion endpoints.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Reports very high AUC/R2 (PGS-only AUROC 0.88697; PGS R2 0.21843), but these are out of line with the provided local h2_obs ceiling (~0.0889) for bilirubin, suggesting non-comparability (different scale/endpoint, composite/TTE, or metric context). High full-model AUROC likely not interpretable as pure PRS advantage here.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Larger EUR validation (n=67,425) than the portability siblings, but comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework (“across 813 traits”), which historically transfers less well despite clean-looking metrics.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Two major risks: (1) pan-trait sparse framework archetype and (2) endpoint/metric non-comparability (TTE + composite; apparent R2 exceeding heritability sanity check). These make the impressive metrics unreliable for predicting benchmark rank on the target trait.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Despite headline AUC, the combination of endpoint mismatch and heritability-sanity failure makes it less likely to rank #1 on a bilirubin-metabolism-disease benchmark than the cleaner direct-match bilirubin-excretion scores.

rationale: PGS001824 and PGS002032 are the only clean direct matches to the target endpoint; they share the same study family, covariates, validation setting, and identical partial-r, so structural/modeling differences dominate. PGS002032 uses LDpred2 with a much larger variant set (19,768 vs 22), which is more likely to capture polygenic signal and generalize in an external benchmark. PGS000924’s stronger reported AUC/R2 is discounted due to time-to-event composite endpoint mismatch and an R2 that exceeds the provided heritability sanity ceiling, indicating non-comparable performance reporting for this target.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match at disease-concept level (major depressive disorder / depression). Phenotyping is generic “Depression” (less specific than “lifetime MDD” but still aligned to target depressive disorder).
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No AUC/R2 reported; has OR per SD = 1.26 (moderate-to-weak PRS signal). Effect-size evidence is usable but not strong versus peers with R2.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR-only evaluation with n=39,444 and basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/technical) suggests reasonably comparable evaluation, but lacks multiple records/replications.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Cross-disease comparison paper archetype (“across 24 common diseases”) can behave more like a framework/benchmarking context than a disease-optimized PRS; missing PRS-comparable metrics increases uncertainty.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Moderate: clean covariates and direct endpoint help, but weaker quantitative signal (OR 1.26) and non-disease-optimized study framing reduce likelihood of topping an external benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match (MDD) with EHR-based case definition implied by title; phenotyping_reported is “Major Depressive Disorder” (aligned).
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Reports Nagelkerke pseudo-R2 = 0.022, but appears to be full-model/unspecified covariate context (covariates unknown), so comparability to PRS-only is limited; still provides some quantitative signal.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR evaluation n=34,703; training cohorts listed (23andMe/PGC/UKB) suggests broad disease-focused GWAS inputs rather than single-biobank only, which is supportive for transfer.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Unknown covariates is a confidence penalty; EHR/PheWAS framing may involve phenotype heterogeneity and potential ascertainment differences versus benchmark endpoints.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Moderate: multi-cohort training signal is good, but unclear covariate/metric comparability and only modest R2 reduce confidence it beats the best sibling cluster.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match (lifetime MDD) and phenotyping_reported “Major depressive disorder” is coherent with target depressive disorder.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model R2 = 0.0254 (not explicitly PRS-only). Within its near-clone family, this is slightly lower than PGS003578 and higher than PGS003576, giving it mid-pack signal.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same study family with 10 records and multi-ancestry evaluation overall; selected validation ancestry European with n=42,250. Repeated-record structure suggests more robust evaluation than single-record candidates.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: PRSice-2 (thresholding) is structurally weaker than genome-wide shrinkage methods for highly polygenic traits, but here the key comparison is within the same publication family where endpoint/setting are similar.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Moderate: strong family-level robustness, but not the top-performing sibling on the only available metric.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match (lifetime MDD) with coherent phenotyping_reported “Major depressive disorder”; fits depressive disorder target well.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Highest reported full-model R2 among the three near-clone siblings (0.0257 vs 0.0254 and 0.0241). While not PRS-only, it is the best available within a tightly matched design cluster, making it the strongest metric signal in the shortlist.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same robust multi-record (record_count=10) study family with multi-ancestry evaluation context; selected European validation n=42,250. This combination (coherent cluster + multiple records) is a positive robustness cue versus single-record entries.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Preprint and PRSice-2 thresholding are mild negatives; however, risks are shared across its sibling cluster and are outweighed by being the top sibling on reported performance under essentially identical endpoint/covariate structure.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: High relative to shortlist: best-in-family metric within the most corroborated (multi-record) direct-match cluster, making it most likely to rank #1 in an external benchmark among these candidates.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match (lifetime MDD) with coherent phenotyping_reported; aligned to target.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model R2 = 0.0241, lowest among the near-clone siblings; despite higher variant count, the observed metric signal is weaker within the same method/publication context.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same multi-record, multi-ancestry evaluation family; European validation n=42,250 supports robustness but does not differentiate from siblings.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same shared risks as siblings (PRSice-2; preprint); additionally, the lower R2 suggests less effective tuning/threshold choice for this score variant.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Moderate-to-low within shortlist: likely outperformed by its closest sibling (PGS003578) given near-identical context but weaker reported performance.

rationale: All candidates are direct matches, so the decision hinges on the most benchmark-relevant evidence under comparable design. The PGS00357x trio forms the strongest corroborated cluster (same endpoint family, same covariates, same validation setting, multiple performance records). Within that near-clone cluster, PGS003578 has the best reported R2 (0.0257) under essentially identical conditions, making it the most likely to rank highest in an external benchmark among the provided shortlist.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Strong direct match: CKD stage 3+ with explicit eGFR<45 definition (stage 3b+), which is within the chronic kidney disease umbrella and clinically concrete.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only full-model AUROC=0.78 is reported (not PGS-only); however OR per SD=1.47 suggests moderately strong PRS signal relative to others here.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Disease-focused CKD paper with explicit multi-ancestry evaluation listed; selected record is EUR with n=11,813 (not huge, but not trivial).
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Reported AUROC likely covariate-inflated due to heavy clinical covariates (HTN, diabetes, BMI, meds, smoking/alcohol, etc.), reducing comparability; method is P+T (structurally weaker than PRS-CS for polygenic traits).
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Despite covariate inflation, it has the best combination of endpoint specificity + relatively strong effect size + disease-focused cross-ancestry intent; likely to transfer well in external benchmarks compared with weaker-effect generic/framework-style CKD scores.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct CKD stage 3+ match, but phenotype is vague (“Chronic kidney disease”) without an explicit eGFR/ICD definition in the visible fields.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model AUROC=0.90 and R²=0.10 are not labeled PGS-only; AUROC is very likely dominated by covariates and/or cohort-specific modeling. OR=1.41 is moderate and not clearly better than the top candidate.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Large evaluation n=67,819 in African American/Afro-Caribbean context; strong within-ancestry evidence but narrower transportability if the hidden benchmark is not AFR-focused.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Non-EUR-only GWAS/EVAL (AFR-only) is a portability risk for a generic benchmark; very high AUROC without incremental/PGS-only metrics is a comparability red flag.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Could rank #1 only if the hidden benchmark is specifically AFR/Black American CKD; otherwise likely underperforms EUR-trained multi-ancestry-intended scores in generic benchmarks.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Label matches CKD, but comes from a paper centered on T2D proteomic markers/comorbidities; endpoint likely EHR-derived CKD and less clearly disease-focused for CKD prediction.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No AUC/R²; OR=1.35 indicates moderate PRS signal but weaker than PGS002237’s OR.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Moderate validation n=48,603 with mixed EUR/MAE evaluation stated, but only 2 records and unclear external-cohort diversity beyond UKB-style settings.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Study archetype suggests CKD is secondary/comorbidity endpoint; higher risk of non-optimized CKD score relative to CKD-focused work.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Absent PRS-comparable metrics and weaker effect size make it less likely to top an external benchmark versus a CKD-focused score with stronger OR.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Partial mismatch: incident CKD cases without diabetes (restricted subgroup) and time-to-event framing; not the generic CKD endpoint.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only full-model C-index=0.78 (not PGS-only); HR=1.30 suggests modest-to-moderate PRS signal, weaker than top candidates.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Validation n=11,645; development appears EHR/primary-care network oriented, which can help realism but here endpoint restriction reduces generality.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Restriction to non-diabetic incident CKD reduces applicability to broad CKD benchmarks; full-model metric includes a clinical risk score, inflating discrimination and reducing PRS comparability.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Endpoint restriction + clinical-risk-score packaging makes it unlikely to rank #1 in a generic CKD PRS benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct CKD label match but from a broad cross-disease comparison paper; phenotype definition not specified here (likely heterogeneous).
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No AUC/R²; OR=1.15 indicates weak PRS signal versus the rest.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR evaluation with n=39,444 is decent, but evidence suggests this is not an optimized CKD score.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Framework/benchmarking archetype and weak effect size are strong negatives for external top-rank performance.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Low OR strongly suggests it will not be the top performer in a hidden benchmark.

rationale: Across the shortlist, PGS002237 has the strongest endpoint fidelity (explicit CKD stage 3+ definition) and the strongest effect-size signal (OR=1.47) in a clearly CKD-focused study with multi-ancestry evaluation intent. Competing candidates either have weaker PRS signal (PGS002757, PGS004889, PGS005113) or are likely to be benchmark-ancestry dependent with potentially covariate-inflated headline AUROC (PGS005090). Given missing PGS-only metrics across all candidates, the best-supported bet for highest external-benchmark rank is PGS002237.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match to target concept (atopic eczema/atopic dermatitis) with phenotyping as incident atopic dermatitis; suitable for generic eczema risk though incident-only is a mild narrowing.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No PRS-comparable AUC/R2 reported; only HR (high vs low PRS)=1.249 suggests moderate separation but not especially strong and not per-SD, limiting comparability.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Large EUR evaluation (n=337,910) supports stability; GWAS ancestry mostly EUR with some diversity but eval is EUR-only, so transfer beyond EUR is unproven.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Comes from a cross-disease comparison paper (framework-like archetype) rather than a disease-focused PRS optimization; covariates include socioeconomic/behavioral factors (not severe leakage, but makes effect-size context less PRS-isolated).
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Strong structural method (PRS-CS, genome-wide ~1.09M variants) and huge eval are positives; however lack of PRS-only metrics and framework-style origin reduce confidence versus a disease-focused, well-specified training pipeline.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct incident atopic dermatitis endpoint, but framed specifically as elderly-onset incidence in an air-pollution interaction study; narrower deployment phenotype than generic atopic eczema.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only HR (high vs low PRS)=1.153 indicates weak-to-moderate signal; sparse 23-SNP GWS score structurally limits achievable discrimination for a polygenic endpoint.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Large EUR evaluation (n=337,910) is supportive; training cohorts listed (EB/FinnGen/UKB) suggest multi-cohort sourcing, but the score itself is very sparse.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Exposure-centered study archetype (air pollution + genetic risk) increases risk that the PRS is an auxiliary construct rather than the best-performing standalone PRS; sparse SNP set is a key downside.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Despite big validation, the combination of very low variant count and weaker HR makes it unlikely to top an external benchmark focused on PRS performance.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Partial mismatch: targets moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis (and appears cohort-specific), not general atopic eczema; phenotype text has a typo but clearly severity-restricted.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Reports very high full-model AUROC=0.93 and R2=0.49, which are implausible as PRS-driven given eczema heritability ceiling (~0.13 liability) and likely reflect non-comparable modeling; no PRS-only metrics provided.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Small validation (n=676) and mixed/unclear ancestry labeling (MAE) reduce reliability for external benchmark transfer.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: High risk of metric inflation/misinterpretation (full-model metrics, potential overfitting, severity endpoint, small N); covariates include parental ethnicity which may partially proxy ancestry/structure.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: The headline AUROC is not credible as a PRS-quality signal in this context; overall evidence suggests low likelihood of ranking #1 in a hidden external benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Endpoint mismatch: paradoxical eczema in biologic-treated psoriasis patients is treatment/condition-specific and not representative of general atopic eczema risk.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model AUROC=0.567 is low; OR=1.89 reported but pertains to paradoxical eczema context, not general eczema; metrics not PRS-only.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Moderate sample (n=3,212) but in a restricted clinical subpopulation; EUR-only.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Strong selection bias and treatment-induced phenotype; limited covariates (PCs 1-2) but endpoint restriction dominates risk.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Unlikely to transfer to a generic atopic eczema benchmark due to endpoint mismatch despite a seemingly strong OR.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Endpoint mismatch similar to sibling: paradoxical eczema in biologic-treated psoriasis; additionally trait label broadens to 'atopic eczema or atopic disease', increasing construct ambiguity.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model AUROC=0.585 (slightly higher than PGS003486 but still low); OR=1.83 in the restricted paradoxical-eczema setting; not PRS-only.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same restricted EUR clinical cohort (n=3,212).
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Treatment/subpopulation endpoint plus broader trait definition increases non-benchmark comparability risk.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Slightly better AUROC than sibling but still unlikely to rank highly for a general atopic eczema benchmark because the endpoint is not aligned.

rationale: Among the shortlist, PGS002755 has the cleanest direct endpoint alignment (incident atopic dermatitis) without the severe treatment/subpopulation restriction seen in PGS003486/PGS003459 and without the severity-restricted/small-N/inflated-metric concerns of PGS001773. Between the two large-UKB-evaluated incident-AD options (PGS002755 vs PGS004587), PGS002755 has much stronger structural properties (PRS-CS, genome-wide ~1.09M variants) and a higher HR signal, making it the most likely to rank #1 in an external benchmark focused on PRS performance.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match to angina pectoris concept, but endpoint is UKB self/doctor-diagnosed “Vascular/heart problems diagnosed by doctor Angina”, which is broader/less code-anchored than a phecode/ICD definition.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Has explicit PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.5868; PGS-only R2=0.0130) and incremental AUROC=0.0098. PRS-only R2 is below local h2_obs ceilings (~0.009–0.014) but close enough to warrant mild caution about scale/definition differences; overall PRS signal is modest.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: European selected validation with large n=49,472; multi-ancestry eval exists in metadata but selected record is EUR. Single-biobank framework context limits expectation of robust external transfer.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Pan-trait UKB sparse framework (813 traits) + sparse SNP set (1,852) increases risk of weaker out-of-sample generalization despite clean covariates (age/sex/PCs/array). Full-model AUROC (0.807) is largely covariate-driven given small incremental AUROC.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Within the UKB-snpnet sibling set, it has the best PRS-only AUROC/R2 and largest validation n, so it is the strongest of that family; however, framework-origin and non-code endpoint reduce likelihood of topping an external benchmark versus a disease/EHR-anchored score with strong effect-size evidence.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match but explicitly time-to-event (TTE) angina pectoris; this is a mild endpoint mismatch if the benchmark is generic case/control angina status.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: PRS-only AUROC=0.5823 and R2=0.0123; incremental AUROC=0.0080. Slightly weaker than PGS001262 on PRS-only metrics.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR selected validation n=24,905 (smaller than PGS001262). Same UKB-only framework context.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same pan-trait sparse framework risk; TTE framing adds additional comparability risk across benchmarks.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Likely ranks below PGS001262 among the snpnet siblings due to weaker PRS-only metrics and added TTE mismatch.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match but very generic “Angina” label; phenotyping_reported is also generic, offering less endpoint fidelity than phecode/ICD anchoring.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: PRS-only AUROC=0.5811 and R2=0.0119; incremental AUROC=0.0078—weakest of the three snpnet siblings.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR selected validation n=24,905; same framework context.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same pan-trait sparse framework risk; generic endpoint wording increases phenotype heterogeneity risk.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Lowest expected rank among the snpnet trio given weakest PRS-only metrics and least specific endpoint.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match with a code-anchored clinical definition: Angina pectoris (PheCode 411.3). This is typically higher endpoint fidelity/portability than UKB questionnaire-style definitions.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No PRS-only AUROC/R2 reported; only full-model C-index=0.7669 plus per-SD OR=1.487 (1.41–1.56). The OR provides meaningful PRS-discrimination evidence (moderate-to-strong) even without PRS-only AUC, and is more directly PRS-informative than a covariate-boosted full-model metric.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Validation n=30,750 with EUR selected record; development in MVP with multi-ancestry GWAS mix reported. Comparative-method paper context suggests externally oriented evaluation rather than a pan-trait sweep.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Comparability risk from missing PRS-only metrics (cannot directly compare to snpnet PRS-only AUROC). Full-model C-index may include covariate contribution (age/sex/PCs), but covariates are basic (age, sex, 20 PCs) so inflation risk is limited.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Strong endpoint fidelity (phecode) + genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred) + near-1.5 OR signal collectively point to better external-benchmark performance than sparse UKB framework scores with modest PRS-only AUROC (~0.58). Slightly edges its sibling (PGS005052) on C-index.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Same high-fidelity phecode endpoint: Angina pectoris (PheCode 411.3).
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No PRS-only AUROC/R2; full-model C-index=0.7662 and OR=1.491 (1.42–1.57). OR is essentially tied with PGS005048 (slightly higher point estimate), while C-index is slightly lower.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same validation setting and n=30,750; same MVP development context.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same missing PRS-only metric limitation; basic covariates mitigate inflation concerns.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Near-clone of PGS005048; expected benchmark rank is very similar. With no PRS-only metrics to separate them, the tiny C-index difference is weak but is the only available within-family discriminator.

rationale: Across the shortlist, the MVP LDpred phecode-anchored models (PGS005048/PGS005052) have stronger endpoint fidelity and a stronger PRS-specific signal via per-SD OR (~1.49) than the UKB pan-trait sparse snpnet models whose PRS-only AUROC is only ~0.58 with small incremental AUROC. Between the two MVP near-clones, PGS005048 has a marginally higher reported full-model C-index, making it the best-supported pick given the visible evidence.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Partial: asthma but explicitly pediatric asthma; this age-restricted endpoint is a mismatch risk for a generic asthma benchmark.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Weak PRS-comparable signal: only full-model AUROC=0.66 and R²=0.04 shown; no PGS-only AUROC/R². OR per SD=1.57 is strong supportive evidence, but comparability is limited without PRS-only metrics and with unknown covariates.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Large validation n=391,820 and multi-ancestry evaluation listed (20% each broad group), which is supportive for robustness; however selected validation ancestry shown as European and covariates are unknown, reducing interpretability.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Key risks are endpoint restriction (pediatric) and metric comparability (full-model only, unknown covariates). Training sample size is small (n=4,498) but not decisive.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Mixed: strong OR and broad evaluation suggest potential, but pediatric-only endpoint and lack of PRS-only metrics make it less likely to top a generic asthma benchmark versus strong adult/general-asthma PRS with clean PRS-only R².

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Good: generic asthma endpoint (trait/phenotyping both asthma) aligns directly with target.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Strongest PRS-comparable metric in shortlist: covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R²=0.048844 (interpretable as PRS-only signal) plus AUROC=0.659 (likely full-model). R² is below liability h² ceiling (sanity OK).
candidate_audits.validation_signal: European-only evaluation (n=7,128) is modest and narrower than some others; still provides a clean single-record metric package with explicit basic covariates.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Framework-paper origin (global biobank lessons) is a mild penalty versus disease-focused studies, but method is PRS-CS-auto (strong genome-wide shrinkage) and the PRS-only R² is clearly reported, lowering selection risk.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: High: direct endpoint + best available PRS-only/covariates-regressed-out R² among candidates is a strong predictor of external benchmark rank, despite smaller validation N.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Good: generic asthma endpoint aligns directly with target.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Moderate: covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R²=0.035168 (PRS-only signal) and AUROC=0.64. Both are weaker than PGS001782 on the key PRS-comparable R².
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Large validation n=351,578 and multi-ancestry evaluation distribution listed; supportive for robustness, though selected validation ancestry is European. Covariates are more complex (age² and interactions) but still demographic/PC-style.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same framework-paper penalty as sibling; more covariate complexity can make full-model AUROC less comparable, but the PRS-only R² is still usable.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Moderate-high: strong validation breadth/size, but lower PRS-only R² than PGS001782 makes it less likely to rank #1 in a PRS-performance benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Good: asthma diagnosed by doctor is a direct match (if anything, slightly more specific/ascertained).
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Mixed: reports PGS-only AUROC=0.64568 and PGS R² (no covariates)=0.05973 (strong), but the selected classification AUROC shown (0.66621) is full-model. The PGS-only R² is the key positive signal and is plausible vs h² ceiling.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Validation n=19,857 (EUR) is moderate; evaluation includes multiple ancestries but development is UKB-only.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Pan-trait sparse UKB framework (snpnet across 813 traits) is a notable generalization risk; sparse 6,139-variant model may underperform genome-wide shrinkage scores out of sample even if internal metrics look good.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Moderate: strong reported PGS-only R², but substantial framework/single-biobank sparse-model penalty reduces likelihood of being the hidden benchmark top performer versus a genome-wide shrinkage score with cleaner cross-cohort construction.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Good: generic asthma endpoint aligns directly with target.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Limited comparability: only partial correlation (partial-r=0.1184) reported; no PRS-only R²/AUROC. Partial-r suggests some signal but is harder to compare across candidates than explicit PRS-only R².
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Validation n=19,551 (EUR) with multi-ancestry evaluation distribution listed; derived/applied within UKB portability context rather than clearly independent external cohorts.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Portability-framework/same-cohort derivation-application context is a generalization risk; metric type (partial-r) is less standard for benchmark comparisons.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Moderate-low: despite strong method (LDpred2) and large UKB training, the portability-framework context plus nonstandard metric makes it less likely to be the top benchmark performer than the candidate with the clearest PRS-only R² evidence.

rationale: Across the shortlist, PGS001782 has the cleanest direct asthma endpoint and the strongest explicitly PRS-comparable performance signal (covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R²=0.048844) with basic covariates, making it the most reliable predictor of top rank in an external PRS benchmark. Alternatives either (i) restrict the endpoint (pediatric asthma), (ii) come from sparse/pan-trait UKB frameworks with higher generalization risk, or (iii) lack similarly comparable PRS-only metrics.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match: trait/efo cervical carcinoma; phenotyping is incident cervical cancer (acceptable for generic disease risk, slight incident-only specificity).
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No PRS-only AUC/R2; reports time-to-event discrimination (C-index 0.613) plus HR per SD 1.33 (moderate). Full-model metric is modest and likely not PRS-isolated.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR-only but large external eval (n=128,113) and multi-cohort development listed (EB, FinnGen, KP, UKB) suggests disease-focused GWAS meta-analysis context rather than a generic framework sweep.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Training n=4,295 suggests limited case count; only one performance record; covariates include age+smoking (mild). Metric comparability limited (C-index, not PRS-only).
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Strong structural signal from genome-wide shrinkage (LDpred) with very large variant count (~2.9M) and disease-focused meta-analysis framing; despite modest reported C-index, this archetype often transfers better than sparse GWAS-hit scores when PRS-only metrics are absent.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match with incident cervical cancer; concept alignment is clean.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Reports AUROC ~0.745 / C-index ~0.75 but these are full-model metrics with a heavy covariate set; HR per SD 1.22 is weak-moderate. No PRS-only metric, so the high AUROC is discounted.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Large EUR evaluation (n=211,795). Training listed as TwinGene; appears to be a cross-cancer evaluation/portability-style score rather than a disease-optimized construction.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Very sparse (10 SNPs, genome-wide significant only) and covariate-heavy evaluation (parity, oral contraceptive use, pack-years, PCs, array) makes the reported AUROC less informative for standalone PRS ranking.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Despite large validation and high full-model AUROC, the combination of sparse construction + covariate-heavy model + cross-cancer evaluation framing is a common pattern that underperforms disease-focused genome-wide PRS in external benchmarks.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match with incident cervical cancer; same endpoint family as PGS000073.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Same full-model AUROC ~0.745 / C-index ~0.749 with similarly heavy covariates; HR per SD 1.21 is weak-moderate. Reported R²=0.437 is almost certainly full-model/overall and not PRS-only, so not comparable.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Large EUR evaluation (n=211,795). Essentially a near-clone/derivative of PGS000073 (inverse weights), so not expected to materially improve external PRS-only performance.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Sparse 10-variant score; covariate-heavy evaluation; derivative weighting raises additional uncertainty vs the original.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Near-clone of a sparse GWAS-hit score with no PRS-only metrics; unlikely to beat a disease-focused genome-wide shrinkage model in a hidden benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match cervical cancer, but ancestry context is EAS-only (GWAS+EVAL), which may mismatch an unspecified benchmark ancestry mix.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only full-model C-index 0.566 and HR 1.2 (weak). No PRS-only metrics.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Moderate EAS validation size (n=57,359) and BBJ-derived loci; coherent within EAS but limited evidence for broader transportability.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: 15-SNP GWAS-hit style score; lower discrimination; non-EUR-only evaluation is a consistent external-benchmark risk when benchmark is not explicitly EAS.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Good if the hidden benchmark is strictly EAS, but otherwise likely to rank below strong EUR-developed genome-wide models; overall signal is weak.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match cervical cancer; endpoint wording is generic disease status (acceptable).
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model AUROC 0.563 and R² 0.00158 indicate very weak signal; no effect sizes reported.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR evaluation (n=144,374) but performance is poor; training cohorts not listed, suggesting less clear disease-focused development.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Low discrimination despite more variants than GWAS-hit scores; likely not competitive in external benchmark.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Weak reported performance with no compensating structural/validation advantages; unlikely to rank #1.

rationale: Across candidates, none provides PRS-only AUC/R2, so selection should lean on endpoint fidelity plus structural/study-archetype signals rather than covariate-inflated full-model AUROC. PGS003428 is the only genome-wide shrinkage, very-high-variant-count score from a cervical-phenotype GWAS meta-analysis context with mild covariates and moderate HR evidence, which is the most plausible profile to transfer well and rank highest in a hidden external benchmark compared with the sparse 10–15 SNP cross-cancer/framework-style alternatives and the clearly weak-performing lassosum model.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct but slightly broadened endpoint ("Cholelithiasis and cholecystitis") rather than pure cholelithiasis; still clinically adjacent and plausibly overlapping with target. Phenotyping field matches the combined endpoint.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Provides PRS-comparable partial correlation (partial-r=0.098, EUR eval). No PRS-only AUC/R2; partial-r is a moderate signal and hard to compare to AUC/R2 across studies.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: From UKB portability study; EUR validation record selected with n=19,908 and multiple ancestry eval records exist (record_count=8), which supports robustness reporting but remains within the same cohort ecosystem.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Framework/portability archetype ("Portability of 245 polygenic scores...") is a known negative for external benchmark ranking versus disease-focused models. Endpoint is composite (adds cholecystitis).
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Despite strong method (LDpred2, genome-wide) and decent partial-r, the portability-framework origin and composite endpoint reduce likelihood of ranking #1 against more disease-focused/direct ICD10 K80 models.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Same combined endpoint as PGS002072 (cholelithiasis + cholecystitis), so slightly less specific than target but still close.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Partial-r=0.0948 (EUR eval), slightly weaker than PGS002072; no PRS-only AUC/R2.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same portability study family and same EUR validation size (n=19,908) with multiple ancestry records (record_count=8).
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same portability/framework penalty; additionally uses a much smaller SNP set (2,059) which can under-capture polygenic signal versus genome-wide shrinkage siblings.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Within its near-clone family it is dominated by PGS002072 on both method/coverage and partial-r, so unlikely to be the top benchmark performer.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Exact direct match to target: ICD10 K80 cholelithiasis; phenotyping explicitly K80.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Reports OR per SD = 1.2986 (moderate). No AUC/R2/PGS-only metrics, so discrimination evidence is limited but the OR is still informative and suggests non-trivial PRS signal.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Single reported validation record (record_count=1) in EUR with relatively large n=56,192; however, lack of multiple independent cohorts/ancestries in the visible fields limits robustness inference.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Covariates listed as Unknown (adds uncertainty about comparability). Method is an integrated/metaPRS approach (RFDiseasemetaPRS) which can be strong structurally, but could also reflect risk-factor integration/packaging; with missing covariate/metric detail this is a moderate transparency risk.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Strong endpoint fidelity plus a structurally advantaged multi-score/metaPRS-style method and the strongest effect-size signal among the direct K80 siblings makes it the best bet to rank highest, despite missing AUC/R2.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Exact direct match to target: ICD10 K80 cholelithiasis; phenotyping explicitly K80.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: OR per SD = 1.2194 (weak-to-moderate), clearly lower than PGS004546; no AUC/R2.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same study family and same EUR-only single record (n=56,192; record_count=1).
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Unknown covariates; otherwise similar transparency limitations as PGS004546 but with weaker effect-size evidence.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Within the same endpoint/study family, the lower OR suggests it will underperform PGS004546 in an external benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match on disease concept (cholelithiasis) but phenotyping is time-to-event (TTE), which is a mild endpoint mismatch for generic disease-status benchmarking unless the benchmark is also TTE.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Has explicit PRS-only metrics: PGS-only AUROC=0.623 and PGS R2 (no covariates)=0.0281. R2 exceeds the provided h2_obs (~0.0214), suggesting scale/definition mismatch or optimistic/non-comparable reporting; incremental AUROC=0.043 indicates PRS adds some signal but not huge.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR validation n=24,905 with multiple ancestry records (record_count=5). However, it is from a pan-trait sparse-PRS framework (813 traits) which historically transfers less well.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Framework penalty (pan-trait sparse snpnet) plus TTE endpoint. The heritability-ceiling inconsistency for R2 is a red flag for comparability/interpretation.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Even with explicit PRS-only AUROC/R2, the framework archetype + TTE mismatch + metric sanity-check concern reduce likelihood of being the top external benchmark performer versus direct K80 disease-focused siblings.

rationale: PGS004546 has the cleanest endpoint fidelity (ICD10 K80 cholelithiasis) and, among the direct-match K80 siblings from the same study family, shows the stronger per-SD effect size (OR 1.2986 vs 1.2194). The main competitors with explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS001174) and genome-wide methods (PGS002072/PGS001861) come from known framework/portability archetypes and/or have endpoint mismatches (TTE or composite cholecystitis+cholelithiasis), which lowers their expected rank in a hidden external benchmark focused on cholelithiasis.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match: trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all align to COPD without subtype/horizon packaging; endpoint looks like a straightforward disease status definition.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Strongest PRS-comparable signal in the shortlist: covariates-regressed-out (PRS-only comparable) Nagelkerke R2=0.0381, near the provided h2_liability ceiling (~0.0388) and thus plausible/high. Full-model AUROC=0.74 is secondary but consistent with nontrivial PRS contribution.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR-only evaluation (n=7,128) is modest and smaller than some alternatives, but still an external-style evaluation context within a multi-biobank framework; metric type (covariates-regressed-out R2) is high-value evidence despite smaller N.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Framework/global-biobank archetype (not disease-specific) is a generalization risk, and small eval N increases uncertainty. However covariates are basic (sex, age, PCs) with low leakage risk, and the PRS-only metric is explicitly isolated.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Best chance to rank #1 because it combines (i) clean endpoint match, (ii) genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS-auto) with very large variant count, and (iii) the highest PRS-comparable R2 in the set, close to the heritability ceiling—strong transfer signal relative to sparse UKB framework scores and the weaker sibling PRS-CS model.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct COPD match on all phenotype fields; no horizon/subtype packaging indicated.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: PRS-comparable R2=0.0163 is materially lower than PGS001783. Full-model AUROC=0.715 is not directly comparable for PRS ranking and is also lower than PGS001783’s full-model AUROC.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Very large EUR evaluation (n=337,168) increases stability of the estimate, but validation size is a weak differentiator when PRS-only signal is clearly lower.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: More complex covariate set (age2 and interaction terms) remains mostly demographic (not biomarker-heavy) but makes full-model AUROC even less interpretable; still a framework/global-biobank score rather than disease-focused.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Despite huge eval N, the substantially weaker PRS-only R2 versus PGS001783 is a strong negative for hidden-benchmark top rank; likely to trail the stronger sibling.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Near-direct match but phenotyping_reported is broader ('Chronic obstructive airways disease/copd'), suggesting a slightly noisier/broader endpoint than pure COPD.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Very weak PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC no-covars ~0.540; PGS R2 ~0.00235). Full-model AUROC ~0.731 is largely covariate-driven given tiny incremental AUROC (~0.003).
candidate_audits.validation_signal: UKB pan-trait framework (snpnet) with standardized covariates; evaluation includes multiple ancestries but selected record is EUR. Validation n=67,425 is decent but does not compensate for weak PRS-only signal.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Sparse model (482 variants) from the '813 traits' framework is a known generalization-risk archetype; endpoint breadth adds additional dilution risk.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Low likelihood of #1: PRS-only performance is far below the best candidates and consistent with underperforming sparse framework scores in external benchmarks.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Algorithmically-defined COPD; still mapped to COPD but endpoint is explicitly algorithmic/AD-coded, which can shift case definition versus generic COPD.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: PRS-only metrics remain very weak (PGS AUROC ~0.539; PGS R2 ~0.00236) with tiny incremental AUROC (~0.00289).
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same UKB pan-trait framework context; smaller validation n=24,905 than sibling models.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Sparse framework score with algorithmic endpoint increases portability risk; metrics indicate minimal standalone PRS contribution.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Unlikely to rank near top given weak PRS-only signal and framework+sparse construction.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Time-to-event 'other COPD' endpoint is a partial mismatch versus generic COPD status; adds horizon/endpoint-structure differences that can reduce comparability.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Best of the snpnet trio but still weak PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC ~0.547; PGS R2 ~0.00314). Incremental AUROC (~0.00368) remains tiny.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: UKB framework context; validation n=67,425 similar to PGS001332, but endpoint is TTE/other COPD which may not align with benchmark case-control COPD.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Sparse framework + TTE endpoint increases mismatch/transport risk; modestly higher PRS-only AUROC among snpnet siblings is not enough to compete with PRS-CS models.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Still unlikely to beat the PRS-CS candidates; endpoint mismatch further reduces probability of #1.

rationale: Across the shortlist, PGS001783 has the strongest PRS-comparable performance evidence (covariates-regressed-out R2=0.0381, near the provided heritability ceiling) while maintaining a clean direct COPD endpoint and using a genome-wide shrinkage method with very large variant coverage. The main uncertainty is its smaller EUR evaluation N, but the magnitude and type of PRS-only metric signal outweigh validation-size advantages of weaker siblings and the consistently low PRS-only signal of the sparse snpnet framework scores.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Strong direct match: trait_efo=dementia and phenotyping_reported=incident all-cause dementia aligns well with target_trait dementia (broad/umbrella).
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only full-model AUROC (0.761) plus HR=1.25; no PGS-only AUC/R2, so discrimination evidence is only moderately informative. Covariates include APOE ε2/ε4 dosage, which can inflate/shift full-model performance away from standalone PRS comparability.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Moderate: evaluation includes multiple ancestries overall, but selected validation ancestry is European with n≈2,032 (not large). Multi-ancestry presence is supportive but not decisive given small per-ancestry eval and lack of PRS-only metrics.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Key risk is comparability: APOE genotype included as covariate makes the reported AUROC less reflective of PRS contribution; also integrative/ensemble construction may be harder to reproduce/transfer if tuned on limited DEV n=2,039.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Good endpoint fidelity and strong structural method (integrative ensemble, genome-wide scale), but benchmark rank signal is weakened by APOE-adjusted full-model metric and limited clean PRS-only performance evidence.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Partial match: trait_reported Alzheimer’s disease but phenotyping_reported is incident all-cause dementia (broadly relevant to target).
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Weak-to-moderate: only HR (top third vs bottom third)=1.36; no PRS-only AUC/R2 and no full-model AUROC. Small SNP set (23) suggests limited polygenic capture unless architecture is highly concentrated.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Supportive size (n≈12,978) EUR-only evaluation, but validation size is a weak differentiator without stronger PRS-comparable metrics.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Sparse genome-wide-significant-only score risks under-capturing polygenic signal; limited covariate adjustment (age, sex) is clean but doesn’t compensate for weak metric evidence.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Some endpoint relevance via dementia incidence and moderate HR, but overall likely to under-rank more modern/stronger-architecture dementia scores.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Partial match: Alzheimer’s disease label, but phenotyping_reported=incident dementia (broad, close to target).
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Strongest effect-size signal in shortlist: HR (high vs low quintile)=1.51 with tight CI, suggesting meaningful stratification even without AUC/R2. Variant count (39) still sparse but better than 23/57-hit sets.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Very strong external signal by scale: n≈458,181 EUR evaluation. While validation N alone is weak, combined with a strong HR it increases trust that the signal is stable rather than idiosyncratic.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Covariates are extensive (many lifestyle/clinical factors), which can complicate comparability of any full-model metrics—but the reported HR is for PRS contrast and remains interpretable as PRS signal. Still, AD-labeled construction may not perfectly map to all-cause dementia benchmark definitions.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Best overall combination of close endpoint (incident dementia), strongest PRS-linked effect size, and very large evaluation context; likely to transfer well and rank highly in an external benchmark despite AD vs all-cause labeling.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Strong direct match: all-cause dementia endpoint matches target dementia well.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Reports high full-model AUROC (~0.819) and pseudo-R2 (~0.034) but these are not explicitly PGS-only; with only basic covariates (age/sex/PCs) the AUROC is less likely to be biomarker-inflated, yet still not directly comparable as PRS performance. Pseudo-R2 magnitude is plausible vs liability h2 ceiling, but its definition is model-based and not clearly PRS-only.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Moderate: UKB-only development with n≈67,428 evaluation EUR; single-record evidence (record_count=1) limits robustness readout across cohorts.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Single-biobank (UKB) setting raises overfitting/transport risk relative to multi-cohort disease-focused evidence; also the identical AUROC and AUPRC values look like a reporting artifact, reducing trust in metric granularity.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Direct endpoint and decent structural/method novelty, but benchmark rank signal is capped by single-biobank dependence and lack of clean PRS-only metrics.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Partial match: Alzheimer’s disease label; phenotyping_reported=incident dementia is close to target.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Weak: HR=1.09 (near-null) suggests limited discriminative power; no AUC/R2.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Small evaluation (n≈2,052) EUR; offers little robustness evidence.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: C+T with 57 variants plus weak HR indicates likely low benchmark performance; little to offset.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Low likelihood to rank #1 given weak effect-size signal and limited validation context.

rationale: Across the shortlist, the most benchmark-relevant differentiator is PRS-linked signal strength under an endpoint close to the target. PGS001775 pairs an incident dementia endpoint with the strongest reported PRS effect size (HR=1.51 high vs low quintile) and an unusually large European evaluation sample, which together provide the most credible indication of robust, transferable ranking performance. Direct all-cause dementia candidates (PGS005170, PGS004281) rely mainly on full-model AUROC without PRS-only metrics; PGS005170 additionally adjusts for APOE genotype, weakening comparability to standalone PRS benchmarks, while PGS004281 is UKB-only with limited robustness evidence.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match: phenotyping_reported and trait_reported are explicit Dupuytren’s disease/contracture of palmar fascia; trait_efo aligns.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only partial correlation reported (partial-r=0.0797, EUR eval). This is PRS-comparable but weaker/less interpretable than explicit PGS-only AUROC/R²; still slightly higher than its sibling PGS001880.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same UKB portability framework with EUR-derived training and multi-ancestry evaluation available; selected record is European with n=18,971 (moderate). Multi-ancestry eval breadth is a mild robustness positive, but still within the same-cohort portability archetype.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Framework/portability study archetype and lack of standard PRS metrics (AUROC/R²) increase uncertainty; however covariates are basic (age/sex/PCs etc.), limiting leakage concerns.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Within the near-clone pair from the same paper/endpoint/covariates, it has the best observed PRS signal (higher partial-r) and uses genome-wide shrinkage (LDpred2) with very large variant count, which tends to transfer better than sparse alternatives when other factors are equal.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match to Dupuytren’s disease with identical endpoint wording and mapping to the target trait.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Partial correlation only (partial-r=0.0783), essentially tied but slightly lower than PGS002092; no AUROC/R² to strengthen ranking confidence.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same validation context as PGS002092 (EUR selected, n=18,971; multi-ancestry eval records exist). No advantage over its sibling on validation design.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same portability-framework and missing PRS-comparable AUROC/R² risks; method is penalized regression with far fewer variants, which can under-capture polygenic signal relative to genome-wide shrinkage in comparable settings.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Given near-identical study/endpoint/covariates, the slightly weaker partial-r and less genome-wide model structure reduce likelihood of being the top benchmark performer versus PGS002092.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match (Dupuytren’s contracture) with coherent phenotype labeling; no obvious endpoint mismatch.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Reports explicit PGS-only AUROC=0.6646 and PGS R²(no covariates)=0.0247, which is strong, directly comparable evidence. Full-model AUROC is higher but appropriately discounted; incremental AUROC is modest.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR-only evaluation with larger n=67,425, but from a pan-trait sparse-PRS framework; validation is still within UKB context rather than clearly independent external cohorts.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: High-throughput pan-trait framework plus extremely sparse model (11 variants) is a major generalization risk signal despite clean metric reporting; such sparse UKB framework scores often underperform in external benchmarks.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Good PRS-only metrics are a positive, but the combination of pan-trait framework origin and ultra-sparse architecture is a strong negative for hidden external benchmark ranking versus a genome-wide shrinkage score from a portability/transfer-focused evaluation.

rationale: All three are direct endpoint matches, so ranking turns on transferable PRS signal and structural robustness. PGS001254 has the cleanest PRS-only AUROC/R², but it is an ultra-sparse (11-variant) pan-trait framework score—an archetype that often drops in independent benchmarks. Between the two near-clone portability-study siblings, PGS002092 has slightly stronger observed PRS signal (higher partial-r) and a genome-wide shrinkage construction with far broader variant coverage, making it the most likely to rank #1 in an external performance benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match to target (trait_efo cirrhosis of liver; phenotyping_reported Cirrhosis) with no subtype restriction indicated.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No PRS-only metric; only full-model AUROC=0.68 plus per-SD OR=1.42 (moderate PRS signal). Full-model AUROC is not directly comparable across candidates, but covariates are basic (age/sex/PCs), so the AUROC is less likely to be heavily clinically inflated.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Very large EUR evaluation (n≈1.15M) and multi-cohort development list suggests externally oriented, disease-focused architecture work rather than a single-cohort portability artifact; EUR-only evaluation matches the provided heritability context (EUR).
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Main risk is comparability: only full-model AUROC reported (no incremental/PGS-only AUC/R2), so true standalone PRS lift is uncertain. Otherwise low leakage risk given basic covariates and coherent endpoint.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Strong overall: best combination of exact endpoint alignment, genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with very large variant count, and moderate per-SD OR in a large EUR evaluation context—features that tend to transfer well to external benchmarks when PRS-only metrics are absent.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match (cirrhosis) with coherent phenotyping_reported Cirrhosis; no explicit subtype restriction.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No AUC/R2; effect size OR per SD=1.32 (weaker than PGS004621). Reports OR top20% vs bottom20%=2.26, but tail-contrast ORs are less comparable across studies than per-SD effects.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Evaluation includes EUR plus AFR/NR mix, but selected_validation_ancestry is European; validation n≈30k is modest. Method is 12 genome-wide significant variants, which can under-capture polygenic signal versus genome-wide shrinkage approaches.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Sparse SNP set increases risk of underperformance in a benchmark expecting genome-wide PRS; multi-ancestry evaluation is not clearly leveraged (and may dilute interpretability) without clear per-ancestry PRS metrics.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Moderate-to-weak: endpoint is fine, but weaker per-SD OR and very sparse construction reduce likelihood of ranking #1 versus a genome-wide PRS-CS score.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Partial mismatch: targets alcoholic cirrhosis (trait_efo alcoholic liver cirrhosis; phenotyping_reported Alcoholic cirrhosis) rather than generic cirrhosis of liver.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model C-index=0.711 and HR per SD=1.18 (weak PRS signal). Full-model metric not PRS-only and time-to-event framing further reduces comparability.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Large evaluation n≈135k, but development is UKB-only (single-biobank archetype) which is a weaker transportability signal than multi-cohort disease-focused development.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Subtype restriction + time-to-event endpoint + weak HR suggest lower benchmark transfer for generic cirrhosis; single-biobank development increases overfitting/portability risk.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Weak for the target benchmark due to endpoint mismatch and weak per-SD effect despite a seemingly higher full-model C-index.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Conceptually mixed: trait_reported Cirrhosis but phenotyping_reported is incident cirrhosis in NAFLD at-risk individuals (restricted population) and publication focuses on alcohol-related cirrhosis loci—endpoint likely not generic cirrhosis.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only full-model C-index=0.677; no PRS-only metrics or per-SD OR/HR reported in the provided fields, limiting inference about PRS contribution.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Evaluation ancestry not reported; validation n≈107k is decent but not decisive. Training n≈4.6k is small and score uses 9 variants, suggesting limited polygenic capture.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Restricted at-risk cohort endpoint and sparse variant set raise risk of poor generalization to a generic cirrhosis benchmark; missing ancestry details lower confidence.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Weak-to-moderate at best; endpoint restrictions and sparse construction make #1 benchmark rank unlikely.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Mismatch: alcohol-related cirrhosis and phenotyping_reported 'Cirrhosis (males)' indicates subgroup restriction; not a generic cirrhosis endpoint.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model AUROC=0.671 (not PRS-only). Tail OR top20% vs bottom20%=6.18 is large but likely reflects subgrouping/ascertainment and is not directly comparable; per-SD beta provided but not easily comparable across studies without scale context.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Small evaluation (n≈1,390) and covariates unknown; limited evidence for robust external transfer.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Subgroup restriction (males, alcohol-related) plus small validation and unknown covariates create high risk of non-transfer to a generic cirrhosis benchmark.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Low likelihood of ranking #1 given endpoint mismatch and weak transportability evidence.

rationale: Among direct/near-direct matches, PGS004621 has the cleanest generic cirrhosis endpoint alignment plus the strongest structural signals for external performance (PRS-CS genome-wide shrinkage with ~1.09M variants) and a stronger per-SD effect size (OR=1.42) than the other generic-cirrhosis option (PGS000726 OR=1.32). Competing candidates are either subtype/restricted-population endpoints (alcohol-related, NAFLD at-risk, males-only) or very sparse SNP sets with weaker effect-size evidence, making them less likely to top a hidden external benchmark for generic cirrhosis of liver.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match on trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported (atrial fibrillation). However, evaluation appears embedded in a clinical risk-wrapper context (CHARGE-AF included in covariates), which weakens interpretability of reported discrimination as PRS-driven.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only full-model C-index reported (0.8718) plus HR per SD ~1.67. The very high C-index is likely dominated by age/clinical risk calculator components; absence of PGS-only AUC/R2 or incremental metrics limits PRS-comparable signal. HR is supportive (>=1.5) but not isolated from the risk-wrapper context.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR-only evaluation (n=52,757) is decent and from a large disease-focused meta-analysis context, but the validation evidence is not cleanly PRS-only due to covariate packaging.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: High comparability risk: explicit inclusion of CHARGE-AF (named clinical calculator) is a strong negative for benchmarking standalone PRS performance; full-model metric likely inflated and not transferable as a PRS ranking signal.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Despite strong study archetype and HR, the CHARGE-AF packaging makes the headline metric non-comparable; likely to under-rank versus cleaner AF PRS in an external PRS benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct AF endpoint alignment across fields. No horizon/incident-only packaging indicated; looks like standard case-control style evaluation.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Reports full-model AUROC 0.74 and pseudo-R2 0.14 with basic covariates (age/sex/PCs). However, pseudo-R2=0.14 for a P+T score is suspiciously high as a PRS-quality signal (likely model/scale/case-control pseudo-R2 and not PRS-only), and no PRS-only metric is provided. OR per SD ~1.94 is strong.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Evaluation is EAS-only (n=24,147). If the hidden benchmark is EUR-leaning (common), this ancestry mismatch can materially reduce rank; if benchmark is multi-ancestry, EAS-only still limits robustness.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Method is sparse (P+T) and evaluation ancestry differs from many common benchmark settings; pseudo-R2 interpretability risk. Still relatively clean covariate set (no named clinical calculator).
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Strong OR helps, but EAS-only evaluation plus P+T method and questionable pseudo-R2 comparability reduce likelihood of being #1 in a generic external benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct AF endpoint (minor capitalization difference only). Covariates are basic (age, sex) with no explicit risk-calculator packaging.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model AUROC 0.78 (tight CI) and OR per SD ~1.82 (strong). No PRS-only AUC/R2, but effect size magnitude is a solid PRS-quality proxy and covariates are light, making AUROC more interpretable than covariate-heavy models.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EVAL listed as MAE (100%) with a selected_validation_ancestry string spanning multiple groups; metadata is somewhat inconsistent, but overall suggests broader cross-population intent than the older single-biobank scores. Validation n=37,161 is moderate.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Some ambiguity in ancestry fields (MAE vs multi-ancestry string) and only full-model AUROC reported; still, no obvious clinical leakage covariates and method (PRS-CSx) is structurally strong for transfer.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Best combination of (i) clean endpoint, (ii) strong effect size, (iii) light covariates, and (iv) strong cross-ancestry shrinkage method—signals most consistent with top external-benchmark performance among this shortlist.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct AF endpoint alignment. Comes from a broad common-diseases framework-style paper rather than an AF-focused meta-analysis, which is a mild negative versus disease-focused AF studies.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Has PRS-comparable signal: pgs_only_r2=0.029, which is plausible and below the EUR h2_obs ceiling (~0.020–0.031 range depending on estimate; close enough to be believable given scale differences). Full-model AUROC 0.77 with basic covariates. However, R2 is modest.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Large validation (n=288,978) and includes multiple ancestries in eval distribution, but selected record is EUR. Size is supportive but not decisive.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Framework/pan-disease archetype risk: these scores often underperform disease-focused, modern multi-cohort AF PRS in external benchmarks. Older LDpred implementation may lag newer cross-ancestry shrinkage approaches.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Good because it reports a PRS-only R2 (rare here), but likely not the top performer versus newer AF-focused PRS with stronger per-SD effect sizes and modern methods.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Phenotyping is 'Incident atrial fibrillation' (still a direct match but slightly narrower than generic AF). Otherwise aligned.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only full-model C-index 0.751 and HR per SD ~1.62 (strong). No PRS-only AUC/R2; metric is modest and not clearly PRS-isolated.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR-focused evaluation with small validation n=10,561; adequate but weaker evidence than others.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Time-to-event/incident-only framing plus limited metric isolation; older LDpred score and smaller validation reduce confidence in top-rank performance.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Unlikely to beat the stronger modern disease-focused candidates; lacks PRS-only metrics and has narrower endpoint framing.

rationale: Across the shortlist, most candidates lack PRS-only AUC/R2, so the most reliable differentiators become endpoint fidelity, covariate cleanliness (avoid risk-wrapper leakage), effect-size strength, and method structure. PGS005168 is penalized heavily because CHARGE-AF packaging makes its very high C-index non-comparable. PGS002814 has strong OR but is EAS-only evaluation and uses P+T with a potentially non-comparable pseudo-R2. The older LDpred scores (PGS000016/PGS000331) have weaker structural signals and/or narrower endpoints, despite PGS000016 reporting a modest PRS-only R2. PGS005313 best balances a direct AF endpoint, light covariates, strong OR (~1.82), and a strong cross-ancestry shrinkage method (PRS-CSx), making it the most likely to rank #1 in an external benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match (Diverticular disease) with coherent phenotyping_reported. Not horizon-specific, not a proxy endpoint.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only full-model AUROC reported (0.76) with covariates including family history (likely inflates/obscures PRS-only contribution). No PGS-only AUROC/R2 or incremental metric, so PRS signal strength is hard to compare.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: European selected validation record; modest n=7,696. Ancestry string suggests some multi-ancestry evaluation exists, but the selected record is EUR and there is no PRS-only metric to leverage across records.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: High comparability risk because family history is included in the model covariates and the only visible discrimination metric is full-model AUROC; could rank well on covariate-augmented prediction but not on PRS-only benchmark.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Despite strong method/variant count (SBayesR, ~1.08M), the lack of PRS-comparable metrics plus family-history covariate inflation makes it less reliably top-ranked in an external PRS-performance benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct ICD10-aligned endpoint (K57 diverticular disease of intestine), good match to target trait concept.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Provides per-SD(?) OR=1.321, a moderate PRS signal; no AUROC/R2 reported, so discrimination can’t be directly benchmark-compared but OR magnitude is still informative.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR development and EUR evaluation; large validation n=56,192 (weak signal but supports stability). Single record only.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Covariates unknown (uncertainty), but no explicit heavy clinical covariates disclosed; method is an integrated/metaPRS approach (RFDiseasemetaPRS) which can be strong structurally, though details are opaque here.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Within the 2024 Commun Biol sibling family, this has slightly stronger effect-size evidence than the LDpred2 sibling; likely to outperform older sparse UKB framework scores, and has cleaner PRS-relevant signal than the family-history-boosted AUROC candidate.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct ICD10-aligned endpoint (K57 diverticular disease of intestine), good match.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: OR=1.312 (moderate), slightly weaker than PGS004544; no AUROC/R2.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR dev/eval; large validation n=56,192; single record.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Covariates unknown; otherwise similar risk profile to PGS004544. As a near-clone sibling, small OR disadvantage is the main differentiator.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Likely close to PGS004544 but marginally lower expected benchmark rank given slightly weaker effect-size signal with otherwise indistinguishable metadata.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Time-to-event diverticular disease of intestine; still related but less aligned to generic disease-status target than straightforward case/control diagnosis endpoints.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Has explicit PRS-only metrics: PGS-only AUROC=0.591 and PGS R2=0.01777 (plausible vs local h2_liability ~0.0174; near-ceiling but not impossible). Incremental AUROC over covariates is small (0.01733), indicating modest standalone lift.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Framework-style UKB pan-trait sparse score; EUR selected validation with multi-ancestry listed overall. Validation n=24,905.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Framework penalty (pan-trait sparse snpnet) and TTE endpoint reduce expected external benchmark transfer despite having clean PRS-only metrics.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Good comparability due to PRS-only metrics, but expected to underperform disease-focused 2024 direct-endpoint models in external benchmarks; PRS-only AUROC is modest.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Composite label (diverticular disease/diverticulitis) is close but slightly broader than target; still acceptable direct match.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: PRS-only AUROC=0.552 and PGS R2=0.00372 (weak). Incremental AUROC 0.00841 also weak.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: UKB framework sparse snpnet; EUR selected validation; n=67,425.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Framework penalty plus clearly weak PRS-only signal.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Unlikely to rank #1 given low PRS-only performance and framework origin.

rationale: PGS004544 and PGS004474 are the strongest direct-match, disease-endpoint-aligned 2024 candidates with moderate effect-size evidence and large EUR evaluation, and they avoid the explicit family-history covariate inflation problem seen in PGS004614 (which only reports a full-model AUROC). Between the two near-clone Commun Biol siblings, PGS004544 has the slightly stronger OR signal (1.321 vs 1.312) with otherwise indistinguishable endpoint/ancestry/validation context, making it the best-supported pick for highest external benchmark rank.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Strong direct label match (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all follicular lymphoma). No explicit endpoint contradiction.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only a full-model AUROC reported (0.61, CI 0.59–0.63); no PRS-only AUROC/R2 or incremental metrics, so PRS-specific signal is uncertain and the AUROC may be covariate-driven.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR evaluation, but very small validation sample (n=197). Multi-cohort context listed, but training is N/A and the small eval makes the metric noisy/less reliable for ranking.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Genome-wide significant variants with only 6 SNPs is structurally sparse; could work if architecture is oligogenic, but generally risks under-capturing polygenic signal. Unknown covariates add uncertainty.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Good endpoint fidelity but weak PRS-specific metric evidence and very small eval; likely not the top external-benchmark performer versus genome-wide shrinkage siblings with cleaner PRS effect-size reporting.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Partial mismatch: trait_reported/phenotyping_reported are 'Nodular lymphoma' while trait_efo maps to follicular lymphoma. Likely related/overlapping labeling, but endpoint fidelity is weaker than explicit follicular lymphoma.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model AUROC 0.538 and Nagelkerke R2 0.00349 (not clearly PRS-only). Effect size OR per SD 1.149 (CI 1.021–1.294) suggests weak-to-modest PRS discrimination.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR GWAS/DEV/EVAL with basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs1-4). Validation n=3,256 provides more stable estimates than very small studies.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Pan-repository style (Cancer PRSweb) rather than a single disease-focused consortium build; endpoint naming ambiguity. Method (lassosum) is reasonable, but performance signals are modest.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Among the PRSweb siblings, slightly better AUROC/R2 than PGS000643, but overall signal remains modest and endpoint mismatch risk persists.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Same partial mismatch as PGS000644: 'Nodular lymphoma' reported/phenotyped with trait_efo follicular lymphoma; weaker endpoint fidelity than explicit follicular lymphoma.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model AUROC 0.532 and Nagelkerke R2 0.00282 (not clearly PRS-only). OR per SD 1.133 (CI 1.005–1.277) is weak; despite a strong top-1% vs rest OR, the per-SD effect suggests limited overall discrimination.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same evaluation setting as PGS000644 (EUR; n=3,256; basic covariates), so metrics are comparably stable.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same PRSweb/framework-style risk and endpoint ambiguity; although PRS-CS is structurally strong, the observed performance/effect-size signals here are slightly weaker than the lassosum sibling.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Likely ranks below PGS000644 given slightly weaker AUROC/R2 and similar endpoint/validation context.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Trait_reported/trait_efo say follicular lymphoma, but phenotyping_reported is 'Chronic lymphocytic leukemia'—an explicit endpoint contradiction that strongly undermines endpoint fidelity for the target.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No AUROC/R2; only an OR 1.07 (CI 0.98–1.17), which is essentially null/very weak PRS signal.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Large EUR validation sample (n=20,134), but it validates the wrong/contradictory phenotype per the phenotyping field, so size does not rescue comparability.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Severe phenotype incoherence plus very weak effect size; likely catalog/endpoint contamination for this target use.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Low likelihood of ranking well in an external benchmark for follicular lymphoma due to endpoint contradiction and near-null effect size.

rationale: PGS003455 is effectively disqualified by explicit phenotype contradiction (phenotyping_reported is a different disease) and near-null OR. Between the remaining candidates, PGS002304 has the cleanest follicular-lymphoma endpoint but provides only a full-model AUROC from a very small evaluation (n=197) and is an extremely sparse 6-variant score, making its apparent AUROC advantage unreliable for PRS ranking.
