The PRSweb siblings (PGS000644/PGS000643) have some endpoint-label ambiguity, but they are evaluated in a more standard setting with basic covariates and a larger, more stable validation (n=3,256). Among them, PGS000644 shows slightly stronger discrimination (AUROC 0.538 vs 0.532; higher pseudo-R2; slightly higher per-SD OR), giving it the best overall benchmark-rank signal in this shortlist.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match: trait_efo is Hashimoto's thyroiditis and phenotyping_reported is lymphocytic thyroiditis (near-synonymous/clinical description consistent with Hashimoto’s).
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No PRS-only AUC/R2; only full-model AUROC=0.6297 (not PRS-comparable). Effect size OR per SD=1.55 is strong and suggests meaningful standalone PRS signal despite missing PRS-only metrics.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same study family and same eval setting as siblings; multi-ancestry evaluation listed (AA/AFR-Caribbean, Hispanic/LatAm, European) with n=94,651, which is supportive but not strongly differentiating within this near-clone set.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Covariates are unknown, so full-model AUROC could be covariate-inflated; however this risk applies similarly across the shortlist. No explicit risk-wrapper/biomarker-heavy packaging is disclosed.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Within a same-endpoint, same-publication near-clone cluster lacking PRS-only metrics, the strongest per-SD OR is a better discriminator than small full-model AUROC differences; this candidate has the best OR signal and adequate genome-wide method/variant count.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match on trait_efo and phenotyping_reported (lymphocytic thyroiditis) consistent with the target disease concept.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only full-model AUROC=0.6387 (slightly highest), but not PRS-comparable. Reported OR=1.037 is very weak, implying minimal PRS discrimination; this conflicts with the idea that it would truly be best-performing externally.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same evaluation ancestry set and n=94,651 as others; provides no unique external-robustness advantage.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Unknown covariates make the full-model AUROC hard to interpret; with such a weak OR, the AUROC advantage is likely covariate-driven rather than PRS-driven.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Despite the highest full-model AUROC, the very weak OR and sparse 55-variant P+T construction reduce likelihood of ranking #1 on a PRS-performance benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match: Hashimoto’s thyroiditis mapping with lymphocytic thyroiditis phenotyping.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only full-model AUROC=0.6054 (lowest). OR=1.42 is moderate, weaker than PGS005271 but stronger than PGS005270; PRSCS with ~1.085M variants is structurally strong.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same eval ancestry set and n=94,651; no differentiating validation design signal versus siblings.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Unknown covariates; full-model AUROC discounted. Otherwise similar risks to the other PRSCS sibling.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Competes mainly with PGS005271 as a PRSCS genome-wide score; lower OR and lower full-model AUROC together suggest it is less likely to top the external benchmark than PGS005271.

rationale: All three are endpoint-faithful near-clones from the same study family with the same evaluation context and no PRS-only AUC/R2, so full-model AUROC differences are weak evidence. The most informative differentiator here is per-SD effect size: PGS005271 reports the strongest OR (1.55), consistent with better standalone PRS discrimination than PGS005272 (OR 1.42) and far better than PGS005270 (OR 1.037). Given similar covariate uncertainty across candidates, PGS005271 has the best benchmark-rank signal.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match: trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all align to disorders of iron metabolism (target iron metabolism disease). No horizon/packaging or proxy phenotype indicated.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only PRS-comparable signal shown is partial correlation (partial-r)=0.1355 (EUR selected record). Slightly higher than sibling; no AUC/R2/OR-per-SD to strengthen discrimination evidence. Magnitude is plausible vs h2_obs~0.067 as a weak-to-moderate signal but not directly comparable to R2.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same study family and same validation setup as sibling (UKB-derived portability paper; EUR selected validation; n=19,883; basic covariates). Multi-ancestry evaluation exists in metadata but selected record is EUR; overall validation evidence is adequate but not externally independent (same-cohort portability archetype).
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Framework/portability archetype (UKB-derived across many traits) is a generalization risk vs disease-focused multi-cohort models (none available here). Metrics are limited to partial-r, increasing uncertainty. Covariates are basic (low leakage risk).
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Within near-clone siblings with identical endpoint/covariates/setting, the higher partial-r plus genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) and much larger variant count (6713 vs 654) provide the strongest available structural+empirical edge for likely top benchmark rank.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match: trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all align to disorders of iron metabolism (target iron metabolism disease).
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Partial correlation (partial-r)=0.1307 (EUR selected record), slightly lower than PGS002031; no AUC/R2/OR-per-SD. Sparse-ish model (654 variants) provides less polygenic capture signal given otherwise identical context.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same validation context as PGS002031 (EUR selected; n=19,883; same portability paper; basic covariates). No differentiating external-validation advantage.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same portability/framework risk and limited metric reporting as sibling. Penalized regression here yields a much sparser score; if architecture is polygenic, this is a downside for transfer/performance.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Given identical endpoint and evaluation design, the slightly weaker partial-r and substantially lower variant count make it less likely to rank #1 than PGS002031 in an external benchmark.

rationale: Both candidates are near-clones from the same UKB portability study with identical endpoint alignment, covariates, training cohort, and validation size; neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 or effect sizes, so differentiation relies on the small but consistent partial-r advantage plus structural signals. PGS002031 has higher partial-r (0.1355 vs 0.1307), uses LDpred2 genome-wide shrinkage, and includes far more variants (6713 vs 654), making it the more likely top performer in a hidden external benchmark under otherwise matched conditions.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match to target (juvenile idiopathic arthritis) across trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported; not restricted to a subtype, so best aligned to a generic JIA benchmark endpoint.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only full-model AUROC reported (0.738) with basic covariates (sex, PCs1-10); no PGS-only AUROC/R2, so discrimination evidence is discounted. Per-SD OR=2.085 is strong supportive PRS signal.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR-only dev/eval; validation n=940 is modest. Same disease-focused study family/cohorts as others (B58C/UKBS/WTCCC), so transport context is coherent but not broad.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Main risk is reliance on full-model AUROC (not PRS-only) and smaller validation; otherwise low leakage risk given basic covariates and clean endpoint.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Strongest endpoint fidelity for a generic JIA benchmark; effect size is strong and likely to transfer better than subtype-specific scores when benchmark cases are mixed-subtype.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Subtype endpoint (oligoarticular JIA) rather than umbrella JIA; good clinical specificity but mismatched if benchmark defines overall JIA.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model AUROC=0.80 with basic covariates; no PGS-only metrics. OR=1.93 is strong. Metric advantage over PGS000114 is hard to interpret cross-endpoint (subtype vs overall).
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR-only dev/eval; validation n=3,157 is larger, but validation size is a weak differentiator and endpoint mismatch dominates.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Primary risk is endpoint mismatch to umbrella JIA; otherwise similar low covariate leakage risk.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Could rank well only if hidden benchmark is specifically oligoarticular JIA; otherwise likely penalized versus an umbrella-JIA score.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Subtype endpoint (RF-negative polyarticular JIA); not a direct umbrella-JIA endpoint.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model AUROC=0.76; OR=1.51 is borderline-strong/moderate compared with others here. No PGS-only metrics.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR-only dev/eval; validation n=3,089. Same study family/cohorts.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Endpoint mismatch plus weaker effect-size signal relative to other candidates; full-model AUROC not PRS-comparable.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Less likely to top an overall-JIA benchmark given subtype restriction and comparatively weaker OR.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Subtype endpoint (enthesitis-related JIA); not umbrella JIA.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Very high full-model AUROC=0.93 and OR=3.09, but both are for a specific subtype and AUROC is full-model (not PRS-only), so cross-endpoint comparability is weak.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR-only dev/eval; validation n=594 is smallest. Same study family/cohorts.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Highest risk of apparent metric inflation/over-optimism for benchmark purposes due to subtype restriction and small validation; full-model AUROC is especially non-comparable here.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Despite striking within-subtype performance, most likely to underperform an umbrella-JIA benchmark because the benchmark case mix will dilute subtype-specific signal.

rationale: All candidates come from the same disease-focused study family with similar ancestry and covariates, and none reports PRS-only AUROC/R2, so endpoint fidelity becomes the main differentiator. PGS000114 is the only umbrella juvenile idiopathic arthritis score (direct match to the target), making it the most likely to rank highest in an external benchmark defined on overall JIA rather than a specific subtype; it also has a strong per-SD OR supportive of meaningful PRS signal.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match: trait_efo is nicotine dependence and phenotyping_reported is Tobacco use disorder (same disease concept as target in this shortlist). No horizon/packaging or proxy phenotype indicated.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Has a PRS-comparable metric (partial correlation) with higher estimate (partial-r=0.0741, CI 0.0601–0.0881) than the sibling candidate; no AUC/R2 reported for either, so partial-r is the main comparable signal here.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same publication family and same validation sample size (n=19,400) with selected_validation_ancestry=European; also evaluated across multiple ancestries in the same cohort framework, which is at least supportive for portability context (though still within-UKB).
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Framework/portability-paper origin (UKB-derived scores applied within UKB ancestry groups) raises external-transfer optimism risk; however covariates are basic (sex, age, birth date, deprivation index, PCs) and comparable, and risks are symmetric vs the sibling.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Within a near-clone pair (same endpoint, cohorts, covariates, validation setting), the higher PRS-comparable signal plus genome-wide shrinkage with very large variant count (LDpred2; 847,691 variants) is the strongest indicator it will rank higher in an external benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match on the same fields as PGS002037 (nicotine dependence / Tobacco use disorder). Endpoint fidelity is essentially identical within this shortlist.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Lower PRS-comparable metric than its sibling (partial-r=0.0557, CI 0.0416–0.0697), suggesting weaker standalone genetic signal in the comparable evaluation record.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same validation context as PGS002037 (same paper, n=19,400, selected_validation_ancestry=European; multi-ancestry evaluation within UKB). No unique validation advantage.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same portability-framework and within-cohort evaluation risks as PGS002037; method is penalized regression with a much sparser variant set (13,838), which can under-capture polygenic signal when compared to genome-wide shrinkage in otherwise identical settings.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Given identical endpoint/covariates/publication family, the lower partial-r and much smaller variant set point to a lower likelihood of topping the hidden benchmark versus PGS002037.

rationale: Both candidates are near-clones from the same portability study with the same endpoint and validation setting, so the decision hinges on the most PRS-comparable performance signal and structural capture of polygenic signal. PGS002037 shows a materially higher partial correlation in the selected European validation record and uses a genome-wide LDpred2 construction with far more variants, making it the more likely #1 performer in an external benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match: trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all gout; no horizon/subtype packaging indicated.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only full-model metrics shown (AUROC 0.694; R² 0.089) plus strong per-SD effect sizes (OR~2.05). Full-model comparability is limited, but within its sibling set it is the top AUROC/R² and top OR.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Large evaluation (n~90k) with selected European validation; eval ancestry includes EUR with some SAS in the broader distribution, suggesting some robustness checks within the study family.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Covariates listed as '0' (clean, PRS-forward), but also means full-model AUROC is closer to PRS signal than covariate-boosted; still lacks explicit PGS-only AUROC/R². Training n is small (6,704) but not decisive.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Best-supported within a coherent same-publication cluster: ensemble/multi-PRS structure + strongest observed discrimination/effect size among near-clones with identical endpoint/setting makes it the most likely to rank #1 externally.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct gout match by all fields; no obvious endpoint mismatch.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Reports only incremental R² (0.081) with covariates included; no AUROC and no PRS-only metric/effect size, making cross-candidate comparability weaker than the UKBB sibling set.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Single validation record, EUR-only eval (n~9.5k). Training in AllofUs (n~37.9k) is not a reliable advantage by itself.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Heavier basic covariates (age/sex/PC1-10) and incremental metric definition reduce interpretability versus candidates with cleaner/no-covariate reporting; limited replication breadth (record_count=1).
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Despite modern method label and larger training, the metric package is less directly comparable and less corroborated than the multi-biobank benchmarking-family candidates; less likely to top a hidden external benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct gout match; same endpoint family as PGS004160.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model AUROC 0.685; R² 0.080; OR~2.00. Strong, but consistently below PGS004160 on AUROC/R²/OR within the same design.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same large eval context as PGS004160 (n~90k; EUR selected; broader EUR/SAS distribution).
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Covariates '0' (clean) and same small training n; main risk is simply being a weaker sibling on observed metrics.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: High likelihood of strong external performance, but dominated by the ensemble sibling that shows uniformly better discrimination in the same setting.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct gout match; same endpoint family as PGS004160.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model AUROC 0.678; R² 0.073; OR~1.93—again strong but clearly the weakest of the three UKBB benchmarking siblings on all reported signals.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same large eval context as the other UKBB benchmarking siblings (n~90k; EUR selected).
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Clean covariate field but lower discrimination; fewer variants than the other two siblings, consistent with weaker capture of polygenic signal.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Unlikely to beat the stronger siblings in an external benchmark given same endpoint/study context but weaker observed performance.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct gout match; no explicit endpoint mismatch.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Very high full-model AUROC (~0.798) but with age/sex/PC covariates and no PRS-only/incremental metric; pseudo-R² is modest (~0.040). With only 80 variants, the AUROC is likely dominated by non-PRS signal and/or case-mix, making it a weak PRS-quality indicator.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Single validation record (n~67k) EUR-only; no multi-record corroboration here.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Key risk is metric non-comparability: covariate-boosted AUROC without PRS-only isolation plus extremely low variant count increases the chance the apparent advantage will not transfer to a PRS-focused external benchmark.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: The AUROC outlier is not trustworthy as PRS evidence given covariate inclusion and lack of PRS-only metrics; more likely to underperform the best-supported genome-wide/ensemble sibling in a hidden benchmark.

rationale: All candidates are endpoint-faithful for gout, so the decision turns on which has the most benchmark-relevant, transferable performance signal. PGS004160 sits in a coherent same-publication sibling cluster with identical endpoint/validation context and shows the strongest discrimination/effect-size signals among those near-clones, while also having a favorable structural cue (MultiPRS/ensemble). Competing candidates either have weaker within-family metrics (PGS004047/PGS004018), less comparable incremental-only reporting (PGS004768), or an implausibly high covariate-inflated AUROC with tiny variant count and no PRS-only isolation (PGS004265).

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match: ICD10 J33 nasal polyp; trait_efo and phenotyping_reported both align to nasal cavity polyp with no horizon/subtype packaging indicated.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No PRS-comparable AUC/R2 reported; relies on effect size only. OR=1.60 per SD is a strong discriminative signal (stronger than sibling’s OR) and plausibly within the trait’s modest heritability ceiling (no contradiction visible).
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR-only development and evaluation; same training (UKB, n=174,489) and same validation size (n=56,192) as sibling, so validation context does not differentiate except via observed effect size.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Method is an integrated/metaPRS (RFDiseasemetaPRS) which can be robust but may embed risk-factor integration; covariates are unknown, so some risk of non-genetic augmentation/packaging, though no explicit heavy clinical covariates are shown. Missing AUC/R2 lowers confidence.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Within a near-clone pair (same endpoint, cohorts, ancestry, variant count, publication), the materially higher OR is the clearest available performance signal and is likely to translate to higher external benchmark ranking than the LDpred2 sibling absent contrary PRS-only metrics.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match: ICD10 J33 nasal polyp; trait_efo and phenotyping_reported align cleanly to nasal cavity polyp.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No PRS-comparable AUC/R2 reported; effect size OR=1.35 per SD indicates moderate signal but weaker than sibling, suggesting lower standalone PRS discrimination in comparable settings.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same EUR-only dev/eval, same UKB training size and same validation size as sibling; no independent advantage in transportability or validation design is visible.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: LDpred2 is a strong genome-wide shrinkage method, but in this shortlist the empirical signal available is weaker (lower OR) and covariates are still unknown; missing PRS-only metrics keeps uncertainty high.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Despite a method-family advantage in principle, the only observed discriminative evidence (OR) is meaningfully lower than the sibling in an otherwise matched setting, which is a negative rank signal for the hidden benchmark.

rationale: Both candidates are endpoint-identical near-clones (J33 nasal polyp), same publication family, same variant count, same EUR-only UKB dev/eval context, and both lack PRS-only AUC/R2. With metrics missing, the strongest differentiator is the reported per-SD OR: PGS004535 (OR=1.60) is materially stronger than PGS004465 (OR=1.35), which is the most benchmark-relevant signal available here and outweighs the method-label preference for LDpred2.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Good concept match to glaucoma via POAG, but phenotyping is explicitly self-reported POAG, which is a weaker endpoint-fidelity signal than clinically ascertained/biobank-coded POAG used in other candidates.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No PRS-comparable metric (no PGS-only AUC/R2). Full-model AUROC=0.748 is not directly comparable as PRS performance; OR per SD=1.74 is strong supportive signal of PRS discrimination.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Very large evaluation n=407,667 and multi-ancestry evaluation listing suggests robustness, but the selected metric is still full-model and endpoint is self-report, so validation strength is partly blunted for benchmark transfer.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Risk of covariate-driven AUROC interpretation (age/sex/ancestry covariates present) and self-report misclassification; otherwise covariates are basic (no heavy clinical leakage).
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Strong OR and huge eval are positives, but lack of PRS-only metrics plus self-reported endpoint makes it less reliably top-ranked than a comparable-endpoint model with explicit PRS-only R2.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct POAG endpoint (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both POAG). Trait_efo is broader (glaucoma) but overall endpoint fidelity is strong for glaucoma target.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Has PRS-comparable signal: Nagelkerke R2 (covariates regressed out)=0.03209, which is below the provided liability h2 ceiling (~0.0556) and thus sanity-consistent; full-model AUROC=0.777 is secondary.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Large European validation (selected_validation_ancestry European) with n=347,396; evaluation ancestry string indicates broader evaluation contexts exist, but the selected record is EUR and large.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Covariates include age/sex interactions and 20 PCs (still basic/demographic-genetic adjustment). Main risk is that this is from a global-biobank framework paper (not disease-focused), but method is strong (PRS-CS-auto) and metrics isolate PRS contribution.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Best combination in shortlist of (i) clean POAG endpoint, (ii) explicit PRS-only/covariates-regressed-out R2 with heritability-consistent magnitude, and (iii) large validation—strongest predictor set for external benchmark rank.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct POAG endpoint (open-angle glaucoma / POAG) and coherent phenotyping_reported POAG; good match to glaucoma target via dominant subtype framing.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: PRS-comparable R2 (covariates regressed out)=0.031479, very close to PGS001792 but slightly lower; full-model AUROC=0.749 is secondary.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: European-only evaluation with small n=7,128, which makes the reported metrics less stable/less indicative of top benchmark performance than the larger sibling.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same framework-paper origin risk as PGS001792; otherwise covariates are basic (sex, age, 20 PCs). Small validation is the main risk.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Near-clone to PGS001792 on method/endpoint/PRS-only R2 but with far weaker validation support; likely ranks below PGS001792 in an external benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Trait_reported is broad glaucoma but phenotyping_reported is POAG, which is still a strong direct match for glaucoma risk; endpoint fidelity is acceptable.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only full-model AUROC=0.80 reported; no PRS-only AUC/R2/effect size, so the apparent advantage could be driven by covariates (notably includes family history).
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Moderate/small validation n=1,795 with mixed evaluation ancestries; limited evidence for robust external benchmark transfer.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Family history covariate is explicit clinical augmentation, making AUROC non-comparable for PRS ranking; C+T with 2,673 variants is structurally weaker than genome-wide shrinkage alternatives here.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Despite high full-model AUROC, the combination of family-history covariate inflation + lack of PRS-only metrics + older sparse method lowers likelihood of #1 benchmark rank.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Broad glaucoma endpoint (phenotyping_reported glaucoma) is a direct match to target glaucoma; good conceptual alignment.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No AUC/R2; reports OR per SD=1.68 (strong), but without PRS-only discrimination metrics it is harder to benchmark against the PRS-only R2 evidence in PGS001792/PGS001797.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Single evaluation record, EUR-only, n=39,444—reasonable but not as compelling as the large EUR validation with PRS-only R2 in PGS001792.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Pan-disease comparative paper context (across 24 diseases) is not necessarily disease-optimized; covariates are basic and acceptable. Main risk is limited performance reporting (no PRS-only metrics).
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Strong OR suggests decent PRS, but missing PRS-comparable R2/AUC and less benchmark-relevant evidence than PGS001792 makes #1 rank less likely.

rationale: Across the shortlist, PGS001792 has the strongest benchmark-relevant evidence package: a direct POAG endpoint (good glaucoma match), an explicit PRS-comparable metric (covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2=0.03209) that is sanity-consistent with the provided heritability ceiling, and a very large European validation sample. Competing candidates either lack PRS-comparable metrics (PGS004944/PGS000137/PGS002761) or are near-clones with much weaker validation support (PGS001797). The main uncertainty is the framework-paper origin, hence Moderate confidence.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match: trait_reported and phenotyping_reported are both Hodgkin's disease; trait_efo maps to Hodgkins lymphoma. No endpoint mismatch signals.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Best-looking discrimination among the PRSweb siblings: full-model AUROC 0.62 (basic covariates only) and per-SD OR 1.476 (CI excludes 1), suggesting moderate PRS signal even though PGS-only AUC/R2 are not provided.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: European-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL with a single evaluation record (n=775). Same validation context as its sibling scores, so relative comparisons are fair within this cluster.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Main risk is reliance on full-model AUROC (not PRS-only) and small evaluation N; however covariates are basic (age/sex/batch/PCs), limiting covariate-inflation concerns. Sparse 20-variant P+T could under-capture polygenic signal, but effect size is the strongest in the cluster.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Strongest within a coherent same-endpoint, same-covariate, same-ancestry sibling set; highest AUROC and highest per-SD OR in that set are the most reliable tie-breakers for likely external benchmark rank.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match (Hodgkin's disease / Hodgkins lymphoma) with consistent phenotyping_reported.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Weaker than PGS000639: full-model AUROC 0.601 and per-SD OR 1.377 (still >1 but smaller). No PRS-only metrics.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same PRSweb evaluation setting as PGS000639 (EUR; n=775), so differences likely reflect model strength rather than validation artifacts.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same limitations as the family (full-model metric only; small eval N). GWAS-hits 16-variant construction may miss additional signal; nothing in metrics suggests it beats the best sibling.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Within-family mid performer; lacks any advantage (endpoint, covariates, ancestry, or effect size) over the top sibling, so less likely to rank #1 externally.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match with consistent Hodgkin's disease phenotyping.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Lower full-model AUROC (0.574) and weaker per-SD OR (1.30) than the sparse siblings; despite genome-wide PRS-CS variant count, observed signal here is modest.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same EUR-only PRSweb evaluation (n=775), enabling fair within-cluster comparison.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Genome-wide method/huge variant count does not translate into better observed discrimination in this setting; could indicate over-shrinkage or limited GWAS power for this endpoint in the source pipeline.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Given materially weaker observed AUROC/OR than the best sibling under identical evaluation conditions, unlikely to top an external benchmark versus the stronger-performing sibling.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match with consistent Hodgkin's disease phenotyping.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Lowest full-model AUROC among PRSweb siblings (0.569) and per-SD OR ~1.292; no PRS-only metrics.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same EUR-only PRSweb evaluation (n=775).
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Like PGS000637, genome-wide lassosum does not show strong signal here; nothing suggests superior external performance relative to the best sibling.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Bottom of the coherent sibling cluster on both AUROC and OR; low likelihood of ranking #1 in a hidden benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Endpoint fidelity is poor/contradictory: trait_reported is Hodgkin lymphoma, but phenotyping_reported is Chronic lymphocytic leukemia, indicating likely catalog/metadata contamination or a non-matching endpoint.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Per-SD OR 1.02 (near-null) provides weak PRS signal; no AUC/R2 reported.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Large evaluation sample size (n=20,134; EUR) but with unclear covariates and multiple records; size does not rescue endpoint incoherence or near-null effect size.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: High risk of being the wrong phenotype (explicit mismatch in phenotyping_reported) and/or a score not predictive for the target; unknown covariates add uncertainty.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Despite large N, the combination of endpoint mismatch and near-null OR makes it very unlikely to rank highly in an external Hodgkin lymphoma PRS benchmark.

rationale: All four PRSweb candidates are clean direct matches with identical ancestry/covariates/validation context, so the most reliable differentiators are the observed effect size and (within-family) full-model AUROC. PGS000639 has the highest AUROC (0.62) and strongest per-SD OR (1.476) among the coherent sibling set, making it the best-supported pick for likely top external benchmark performance. PGS003449 is penalized heavily due to explicit phenotyping mismatch and near-null OR.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match to target trait: myocardial infarction; consistent across trait_reported (PheCode 411.2), trait_efo, and phenotyping_reported.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No PRS-only AUC/R2; only full-model C-index/AUC-like metric reported (0.7848) with basic covariates. Effect size OR per SD=1.578 is the strongest among shortlist, suggesting comparatively stronger PRS signal within this near-clone set.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same evaluation setting as others (European selected record; n=30,379; record_count=3). Multi-ancestry GWAS/eval context is identical across candidates, so validation does not differentiate.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Main risk is metric comparability: full-model C-index is not PRS-only and likely partly covariate-driven; however covariates are light (age/sex/PCs) and consistent across candidates, reducing differential risk within the shortlist.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Within an otherwise indistinguishable sibling cluster (same endpoint, cohorts, covariates, eval size/ancestry), the best-supported rank signal comes from stronger per-SD OR and marginally higher full-model C-index; both favor PGS005039.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct MI match (same PheCode 411.2 / EFO / phenotyping).
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model C-index 0.7834 (slightly below top); OR=1.541 is moderate-strong but weaker than PGS005039/PGS005045.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same validation design/size/ancestry as the rest; no differentiating external-validation breadth visible.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same limitation: lacks PRS-only metrics; full-model metric may be covariate-influenced, though covariates are basic.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Given near-identical metadata, slightly weaker OR and slightly lower C-index reduce likelihood of being top performer versus the best sibling.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct MI match (same PheCode 411.2 / EFO / phenotyping).
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model C-index 0.7839; OR=1.554 (second-best). Method is PRS-CS (genome-wide shrinkage) but within-family empirical signals (OR/C-index) are slightly below PGS005039.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same evaluation context (European selected record; n=30,379) and same multi-ancestry description; does not differentiate.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same PRS-only metric absence; otherwise comparable and clean (basic covariates).
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Strong contender; however, within this tight cluster the slightly lower OR and slightly lower C-index than PGS005039 weakly predict a lower benchmark rank.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct MI match (same PheCode 411.2 / EFO / phenotyping).
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model C-index 0.7836; OR=1.546. Both are mid-pack among the five.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same validation setting/size/ancestry; no added robustness evidence versus siblings.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same comparability limitation (full-model only), but covariates are basic and consistent.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: With no structural or validation advantages and slightly weaker effect size/metric than the top sibling, less likely to rank #1.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct MI match (same PheCode 411.2 / EFO / phenotyping).
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Lowest full-model C-index (0.7831) and lowest OR (1.53) in the shortlist; no PRS-only metrics to offset.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same validation context as others; does not compensate for weaker performance signals.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same full-model-only limitation; additionally, being the weakest sibling on available signals increases risk of underperforming in external benchmark.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Lowest likelihood of ranking #1 given it is consistently bottom on the only differentiating performance proxies available.

rationale: All five candidates are near-clones on endpoint fidelity, covariates, cohort context, and validation setting, and none reports PRS-only AUC/R2. In this tie-break scenario, the strongest available PRS-relevant signal is per-SD effect size (OR), with small full-model C-index differences as secondary within-family support. PGS005039 has the highest OR (1.578) and the highest reported C-index (0.7848), making it the most likely to rank #1 in an external benchmark among this shortlist.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match: trait_reported and phenotyping_reported are both hip osteoarthritis (not a proxy like replacement; not horizon/incident-only packaging).
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No AUC/R2 reported, but has a reasonably strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.38, 95% CI 1.31–1.46), suggesting moderate PRS discrimination; genome-wide PRS-CS with ~1.05M variants is structurally strong.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR-only evaluation with decent n=39,444; covariates are basic (age, sex, PCs, technical), so effect size is relatively comparable and not obviously clinically inflated.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Main risk is missing PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUC/R2), so ranking relies on effect size + structural signals; otherwise low leakage risk given covariates.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Strong overall: best combination of clean endpoint fidelity + genome-wide shrinkage method + moderate OR under clean covariates; likely to transfer better than sparse GW-significant score and better-supported than newer UKB-only ICD-code siblings with weaker OR.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Partial mismatch: phenotyping_reported is total hip replacement (treatment/proxy) rather than hip osteoarthritis diagnosis; can shift case mix and severity.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Reports only full-model AUROC=0.66 (age, sex), which is not PRS-only; variants_number=44 (GW-significant) is structurally sparse for a complex trait, so PRS signal may be limited despite multi-cohort framing.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR eval n=14,926; multi-cohort development listed, which is supportive for external orientation, but the endpoint proxy reduces comparability to the target trait benchmark.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Proxy/treatment endpoint is the key risk; full-model AUROC may be largely covariate-driven and not comparable across candidates.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Moderate: multi-cohort disease-focused context helps, but THR proxy + very sparse SNP set makes it less likely to top an external benchmark for hip OA diagnosis.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Good concept match via hip OA EFO; phenotyping is ICD-style M16 coxarthrosis (hip arthrosis), which is close to hip OA but not identical wording.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only effect size shown (OR≈1.296), weaker than PGS002763; LDpred2 genome-wide (~1.06M variants) is structurally strong.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR eval n=56,192, but covariates are unknown, reducing interpretability/comparability of the reported OR.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Risk-factor integration publication context plus unknown covariates raises concern about comparability/possible packaging; also appears UKB-only development, which can be more internally optimized.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Moderate: strong method/variant count, but weaker OR and less transparent covariates than PGS002763 reduce likelihood of ranking #1.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Same endpoint family as PGS004478 (M16 coxarthrosis) and similarly close to hip OA.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Effect size is weaker (OR≈1.216) despite same large variant count; method is an integrated/metaPRS approach but does not show stronger empirical signal here.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR eval n=56,192; covariates unknown (same limitation).
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same concerns as sibling: unknown covariates and integration framing; additionally, weaker OR suggests lower standalone PRS discrimination.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Lower: within the near-clone pair, this looks empirically weaker than PGS004478 and clearly weaker than PGS002763.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match label, but phenotyping_reported is incident hip osteoarthritis (time-to-event framing), which can differ from prevalent/case-control benchmarks.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Reports full-model C-index=0.60 (not PRS-only) and HR=1.4 per SD (moderate). Method (megaprs.auto) with ~774k variants is reasonably strong, but the visible training sample (n=404; 1000G) is a red flag for how the score was derived/parameterized in this record.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Very large EUR eval n=412,090, but that is a weak differentiator; covariates are PCs only (clean), yet the metric is still not PRS-only and is in a survival/incidence setting.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Framework/absolute-incidence paper context plus incident-only endpoint and odd training metadata (1000G, n=404) increase risk that this is not the best standalone disease PRS for external benchmarking.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Moderate-to-low: despite huge validation and decent HR, the incident/survival packaging and metadata oddities make it less likely to be the top external-benchmark performer versus a clean disease PRS-CS case-control style score.

rationale: Across the shortlist, PGS002763 has the cleanest endpoint match (hip OA diagnosis rather than replacement proxy or incident-only packaging), uses a strong genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with ~1M variants, and shows a solid per-SD effect size (OR=1.38) under basic covariate adjustment. Competing genome-wide models (PGS004478/PGS004548) have weaker ORs and unknown covariates in an integration-study context, while the sparse THR proxy score (PGS002728) and the incident/survival framework-style score (PGS004882) carry larger endpoint/packaging risks for a hidden external benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct trait match (hypothyroidism) but phenotyping is explicitly incident hypothyroidism, which can be slightly less aligned to a generic disease-status benchmark than prevalent/combined case-control definitions. Endpoint is otherwise coherent.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only a full-model AUROC is reported (0.859, CI 0.821–0.897) with no PGS-only/incremental metric; given inclusion of strong near-outcome thyroid biomarkers (TSH, T4, anti-TPO), this AUROC is likely dominated by covariates and is not comparable as PRS signal.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Large EUR evaluation (n=441,692) and EUR-only context; however, the reported metric is tied to biomarker-heavy covariates, limiting interpretability for PRS-only benchmark ranking.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: High comparability/leakage risk from biomarker covariates tightly coupled to hypothyroidism diagnosis; missing PRS-only metrics increases uncertainty about true standalone PRS performance.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Despite strong study scale and modern method/variant count, the covariate-inflated full-model AUROC provides weak evidence for PRS benchmark performance; likely not the top external-benchmark performer if benchmark emphasizes PRS contribution.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match (Hypothyroidism) with generic phenotyping label; no explicit incident-only restriction stated, which is favorable for generic benchmark alignment.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Reports full-model AUROC=0.70 and OR per SD ~1.5 (1.41–1.60). The OR provides a more PRS-relevant signal than full-model AUROC here, and OR≈1.5 is comparatively strong within this shortlist.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR dev/eval but small evaluation sample (n=8,417) and only one performance record; covariates are unknown, reducing interpretability but not as problematic as explicit biomarker adjustment.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Framework/portability-style paper context and sparse model (6,127 variants, SnpNet) raise risk of weaker external generalization; unknown covariates add uncertainty.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Has the strongest explicit PRS-relevant effect-size signal (OR≈1.5) among candidates with clean endpoint wording, but framework/sparse-method origin is a meaningful downside versus disease-focused genome-wide shrinkage scores.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match (Hypothyroidism) with standard disease endpoint wording; good alignment for a generic hypothyroidism benchmark.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No AUC/R2; reports OR per SD 1.47 (1.43–1.52), a solid PRS-discrimination signal and close to the strongest in the set.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR evaluation with moderate n=39,444; covariates are basic (age, sex, PCs, technical), which makes the effect-size evidence more comparable to PRS-only performance expectations.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Training sample listed as N/A (summary-stat-based construction likely), and only one record; still, no explicit leakage covariates and method is genome-wide shrinkage (PRS-CS) with ~1.09M variants.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Combines strong structural properties (PRS-CS, genome-wide) with clean covariates and a strong OR; this is the most benchmark-plausible package for standalone PRS performance among the shortlist.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match (Hypothyroidism) with standard disease endpoint; good alignment.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only incremental/full-model R2 reported (0.0262) rather than PGS-only; modest and hard to compare across studies, but at least isolates improvement over covariates in its own setting.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Multi-ancestry evaluation design overall, but selected validation ancestry is European; n=43,505 and multiple records (4) is mildly supportive.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Incremental R2 is tied to a specific modeling comparison (“combined with BOLT-LMM”), reducing cross-study comparability; no OR/HR and no PGS-only metrics.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Methodologically strong (PolyFun-pred) and reasonable incremental R2, but weaker direct PRS-signal evidence than the OR-based candidates; likely mid-pack for external benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match (Hypothyroidism) with standard disease endpoint; good alignment.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Incremental R2 reported (0.0247), slightly below the sibling PolyFun-pred model; no PGS-only metrics or effect sizes.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same evaluation setup as PGS002653 (n=43,505; 4 records; selected EUR).
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same comparability limitations as PGS002653 (incremental R2 context-specific); lacks additional supportive effect-size evidence.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Near-clone to PGS002653 but with slightly weaker incremental R2; unlikely to outrank the stronger OR-based PRS-CS candidate in an external benchmark.

rationale: Across the shortlist, PGS002766 offers the best benchmark-facing evidence package: direct endpoint match, genome-wide shrinkage construction (PRS-CS with ~1.09M variants), clean/basic covariates (reducing leakage/comparability concerns), and a strong PRS-relevant effect size (OR per SD 1.47). PGS005218’s very high AUROC is discounted because it is a biomarker-heavy full model (TSH/T4/anti-TPO) with no PGS-only metric, making it weak evidence for PRS benchmark ranking. PGS004935 has a slightly higher OR (~1.5) but comes from a portability/framework context with a sparse model and small evaluation, increasing risk of poorer external benchmark performance.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match to hypertension; phenotyping is prevalent hypertension (acceptable for generic hypertension risk, though not incident-only).
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No PRS-only AUC/R2; only full-model AUROC=0.764 plus strong per-SD effect size OR=2.1, which is unusually strong supportive evidence of PRS discrimination even without PRS-only metrics. Full-model AUROC likely partly covariate-driven (BMI, smoking, etc.), so OR is the key signal here.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Disease-focused multi-cohort context (BioMe/MVP/UKB) with multi-ancestry validation listed and large eval n=39,035; suggests robustness beyond a single-biobank framework.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Comparability risk from covariate-heavy model (BMI, smoking, site, race/ethnicity) and reliance on full-model AUROC; however, covariates are not obviously outcome-proximal biomarkers/treatment variables, and the strong OR mitigates missing PRS-only metrics.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Strong: disease-focused multi-ethnic study family + multi-score aggregation style (PRSsum) + very strong OR signal; likely to transfer well and outperform UKB framework/portability scores whose apparent strength is mostly from reported AUC formats rather than stronger underlying PRS.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match; prevalent hypertension endpoint aligns similarly to PGS004236.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only full-model AUROC=0.763 (near-identical to PGS004236) but no reported PRS effect size (OR/HR) and no PRS-only metrics; weaker discriminative evidence than its sibling.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same evaluation setting and n=39,035 as PGS004236; multi-cohort disease-focused context but slightly less supported (training cohorts omit MVP vs sibling).
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same covariate-driven AUROC comparability concern as PGS004236, but without an effect-size anchor the PRS contribution is harder to trust.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Moderate: same strong study family, but lacks the extra PRS-strength evidence (OR) that would predict higher external benchmark rank versus its sibling.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct hypertension endpoint; acceptable alignment.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Has PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.629, PGS R2=0.0649) which are comparable and below heritability ceiling; however, these are modest and come from a pan-trait sparse framework context. Full-model AUROC=0.7189 with incremental AUROC=0.044 suggests limited added value from PRS.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: UKB-based development (single-biobank framework archetype) with evaluation reported as European for the selected record; less indicative of external robustness than a disease-focused multi-cohort study.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Framework penalty ("across 813 traits") and sparse L1 model generalization risk; despite clean PRS-only reporting, these models often underperform disease-focused alternatives in external benchmarks.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Moderate-low: good metric transparency but archetype risk and only modest PRS-only AUROC/R2 reduce likelihood of ranking #1 against a strong disease-focused multi-cohort candidate.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct hypertension label, but publication context is biomarker genetics rather than hypertension-focused model development/validation.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only full-model AUROC=0.623 (low) and no PRS-only metrics/effect sizes; weak signal for top benchmark performance.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR-only dev/eval in UKB with n=87,413; large n but single-biobank and not clearly disease-focused validation.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: High risk of being a secondary/auxiliary phenotype model from a non-disease-focused study; limited evidence that PRS itself is strong.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Low: weak discrimination evidence and weaker study archetype for hypertension PRS performance.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct hypertension endpoint; acceptable alignment.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only full-model AUROC=0.72 with unknown covariates (hard to interpret) and modest OR=1.42 (moderate PRS signal, not top-tier). No PRS-only metrics.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Portability-framework style paper; EUR-only eval with small n=8,417, offering limited robustness evidence.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Framework/portability archetype penalty plus unknown covariates; modest OR suggests it is unlikely to beat the strongest disease-focused multi-cohort score.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Moderate-low: despite decent full-model AUROC, the combination of framework context, small eval, unknown covariates, and only moderate OR reduces likelihood of #1 benchmark rank.

rationale: Across the shortlist, PGS004236 and PGS004234 are the strongest endpoint-faithful, disease-focused multi-cohort candidates. Between them, PGS004236 has the key extra discriminative evidence (strong OR=2.1) and a structurally favorable aggregation-style method (PRSsum), while the others are penalized by pan-trait/portability archetypes or weaker/less interpretable metrics. Missing PRS-only AUC/R2 keeps confidence from being high, but the study-family strength plus the large OR makes PGS004236 the most likely to rank #1 in an external benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct trait_efo match to kidney failure, but phenotyping is explicitly restricted to “Diabetic kidney failure in all”, which is narrower than generic kidney failure and may not align with a benchmark expecting broader kidney failure/ESKD definitions.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No PRS-only AUC/R2. Reports full-model C-index 0.779 plus HR per SD 1.19 (modest), suggesting limited standalone PRS discrimination; full-model metric likely partly covariate-driven (age/sex/PCs).
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Large EUR evaluation (n=135,300) in UKB context; supportive for internal robustness but still single-biobank and subtype-restricted.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Subtype restriction (diabetic kidney failure) is the main risk for external benchmark mismatch; reliance on full-model metric without PRS-only metrics adds comparability risk.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Moderate: exact label helps, but modest HR and subtype endpoint reduce likelihood of topping a generic kidney-failure benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Maps to kidney failure via N18 chronic renal failure; closer to kidney failure than CKD stage definitions, and not explicitly subtype-restricted.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No AUC/R2; only OR per SD ~1.40 (moderate). This is weaker than strong PRS signals but better than very small effects; still limited by lack of comparable discrimination metrics.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR-only eval (n=56,192) with unknown covariates; single record limits triangulation.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Unknown covariates and “risk factor metaPRS” construction may embed non-disease PRS components; could help or hurt transfer, but comparability is uncertain without incremental/PGS-only metrics.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Moderate: endpoint is plausible for kidney failure and OR is decent, but evidence is thin and packaging risk is non-trivial.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Same N18 chronic renal failure endpoint family as PGS004562; reasonable alignment to kidney failure.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only OR per SD ~1.17 (weak). No AUC/R2, so little evidence of strong standalone PRS performance.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same limited single-record EUR eval (n=56,192) with unknown covariates.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same unknown-covariate and study-design comparability risks as its sibling, but with clearly weaker effect-size signal.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Low: weak OR makes it unlikely to be top-ranked externally.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Not a direct kidney failure endpoint: CKD stage 3+ (eGFR <45) is earlier/broader than kidney failure. This is a meaningful endpoint mismatch versus a kidney-failure benchmark.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model AUROC 0.78 with extensive clinical covariates; not PRS-comparable. OR per SD 1.47 is relatively strong and suggests good PRS signal, but the endpoint mismatch limits relevance.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Multi-ancestry evaluation exists overall, but the selected record is EUR with small n=11,813; still, the broader evaluation footprint is a mild robustness positive.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Heavier covariate set inflates full-model AUROC; primary risk is endpoint mismatch (CKD vs kidney failure).
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Moderate-low: strong OR helps, but mismatch to kidney failure likely prevents #1 in a kidney-failure benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: CKD-focused and includes “CKD or dialysis” which partially overlaps kidney failure via dialysis, but still not a clean kidney-failure endpoint and mixes broader CKD with failure-level disease.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model AUROC ~0.592 and R² ~0.02 (likely PRS-only given covariates=0, but labeled as full-model fields). Effect size OR ~1.39 is moderate. Overall discrimination signal is not strong.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR/SAS evaluation (n=90,274) is reasonably large and somewhat more transport-informative than EUR-only, but still not clearly external multi-cohort disease-focused validation.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Endpoint ambiguity (CKD or dialysis) and relatively weak AUROC signal; also training sample is small (n=13,496), raising overfitting/instability concerns despite large eval.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Low-moderate: some dialysis overlap, but weak discrimination and endpoint mixing reduce odds of topping a kidney-failure benchmark.

rationale: Among the shortlist, the best direct-match endpoint to generic kidney failure without an explicit subtype restriction is the N18 chronic renal failure model. Between the two N18 siblings, PGS004562 has a materially stronger per-SD effect size (OR ~1.40 vs ~1.17), which is the most informative available PRS-quality signal given the absence of PRS-only AUC/R² across candidates. PGS000708 matches the label but is restricted to diabetic kidney failure and shows only a modest HR, while the CKD-based candidates (PGS002237, PGS004158) have meaningful endpoint mismatch to kidney failure despite some overlap (dialysis).

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match on trait_reported/trait_efo; phenotyping is familial late-onset AD (LOAD), which is still aligned but slightly narrower than generic population LOAD.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No AUC/R2; has strong OR per SD (OR=1.73, 95% CI 1.57–1.93), which is a meaningful PRS-strength signal among this shortlist.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Evaluated in AMR (Hispanic/Latin American) with n=3,324; useful robustness/transport signal but may underperform a EUR-evaluated score in a EUR-heavy hidden benchmark.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: GW-significant-only (21 variants) may miss polygenic signal; familial ascertainment could inflate effect sizes vs population-based benchmarks; nonetheless covariates are clean (age, sex).
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Strong effect-size evidence and clean covariates help, but AMR-only evaluation and familial endpoint make it a slightly riskier bet for a generic external benchmark than its EUR sibling.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match on trait_reported/trait_efo; phenotyping is familial late-onset AD (LOAD), aligned but somewhat specialized.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No AUC/R2; OR per SD is moderate (OR=1.29, 95% CI 1.21–1.37), weaker than PGS000054 and not clearly superior to other candidates with more polygenic construction.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR evaluation with n=4,792 and clean basic covariates (age, sex) gives good comparability for typical external benchmarks.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: GW-significant-only (21 variants) limits captured signal; familial ascertainment may reduce transferability; effect size suggests only modest discrimination.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Good comparability (EUR eval, clean covariates) but weaker OR makes it less likely to be top-ranked if the benchmark rewards stronger discrimination.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match with straightforward late-onset AD phenotyping; less specialized than the 'familial' endpoint variants.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Reports R²=0.191 but it appears to be a full-model/unspecified 'proportion of variance explained' with unknown covariates; magnitude is suspiciously high for a simple C+T score and not PRS-only comparable.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR evaluation n=3,810; GWAS ancestry is mixed/NR+EUR, but evaluation is EUR which matches common benchmark settings.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Unknown covariates + unusually high R² raises comparability/definition risk (possible scale mismatch or covariate-inflated metric); C+T with only 22 variants is effectively sparse and may not generalize as implied.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Despite good endpoint alignment, the metric is hard to trust and may not translate to PRS-only benchmark scoring; risk of being overrated by a non-comparable R².

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Trait label maps to late-onset AD but is explicitly pathway-restricted (synaptic function SNPs); phenotyping says late-onset AD, yet the construction is not a general PRS for the endpoint.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model AUROC=0.731 only; no PGS-only metric and covariates are unknown, so AUROC is not safely interpretable as PRS strength.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Very small evaluation (n=136) and development n=439; high variance/optimism risk.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Pathway-limited 8-variant score is unlikely to capture broad polygenic signal; small-sample evaluation and unknown covariates increase overfitting/metric inflation risk.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Low likelihood to rank #1 in an external benchmark due to restricted construction and weak/unstable validation evidence.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Trait_reported matches, but phenotyping_reported is a cognition-by-age interaction outcome (not AD case/control). This is an endpoint mismatch for late-onset AD risk benchmarking.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No AUC/R2/OR for AD; reports a cognition interaction effect metric that is not comparable to disease-risk discrimination.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Huge n=497,087, but for a non-matching endpoint; does not provide transferable PRS performance evidence for AD diagnosis.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Severe phenotype/endpoint mismatch dominates; large sample size does not rescue comparability.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Very unlikely to rank highly in a benchmark targeting late-onset AD case/control performance.

rationale: Across the direct-match candidates, none provides clean PRS-only AUC/R². The most informative comparable signal available is per-SD effect size under clean covariates. PGS000054 and PGS000053 are near-clones (same study family, same variant count, same covariates, same familial LOAD framing), and PGS000054 shows a materially stronger OR (1.73 vs 1.29), which is a strong discriminator when other design elements are similar. PGS000334 has good endpoint alignment but its very high, covariate-unknown R² is non-comparable/suspect; PGS004918 and PGS002289 have major generalizability/endpoint issues. The main drawback for PGS000054 is AMR-only evaluation, which lowers certainty for a EUR-heavy benchmark, hence Moderate confidence.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match: trait_reported and phenotyping_reported are explicitly knee osteoarthritis; EFO aligns (osteoarthritis, knee).
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No AUC/R2 reported; has per-SD(?) OR=1.35 (moderate discriminative signal) with CI, which is usable but less comparable than PRS-only R2/AUC.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR-only evaluation with reasonably large n=39,444; covariates are basic (age/sex/PCs/technical), suggesting minimal covariate inflation.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Main risk is missing PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUC/R2) and unclear training cohort details (N/A). Otherwise low leakage risk.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Genome-wide shrinkage (PRS-CS) with ~1.05M variants plus clean covariates and direct endpoint is a strong structural package; likely to transfer well versus sparse/framework alternatives.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Trait is knee osteoarthritis but phenotyping_reported is broader ('Clinical osteoarthritis'), reducing knee-specific fidelity versus knee-coded endpoints.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only full-model AUROC=0.66 reported (not PRS-only); includes BMI in covariates, so AUROC is not directly comparable as PRS performance evidence.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Disease-focused multi-cohort development list is supportive for external orientation; EUR eval n=14,926 is smaller than others here.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Endpoint broadening (clinical OA) and reliance on full-model AUROC with BMI increases comparability risk; small 24-variant GWS score may under-capture polygenic signal.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Multi-cohort disease study is a plus, but the combination of broad endpoint + small SNP set + only covariate-influenced AUROC weakens likelihood of ranking #1.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match via ICD-style knee OA code (M17 gonarthrosis) mapped to knee OA EFO; good knee-specific fidelity.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No AUC/R2; reports OR=1.3667 (moderate, slightly stronger than 1.35). Method is meta/ensemble-like (RFDiseasemetaPRS), a positive structural signal.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR dev/eval with large eval n=56,192; however covariates are unknown, reducing interpretability/comparability of the reported effect size context.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Unknown covariates and 'risk factor integration' publication theme raise risk that performance reflects packaging/augmentation rather than clean PRS-only signal (even if not explicitly shown here).
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Strong endpoint + ensemble-style method + large eval are promising, but uncertainty about covariate/packaging makes it less reliably benchmark-top than a cleaner PRS-only construction.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match via M17 gonarthrosis (knee OA) with aligned EFO; good knee-specific fidelity.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No AUC/R2; OR=1.3233 (moderate but weaker than PGS004549/PGS002767). LDpred2 genome-wide shrinkage is structurally strong.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR dev/eval; eval n=56,192; covariates unknown (same limitation as sibling).
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same covariate/packaging uncertainty as the Commun Biol integration study family; additionally weaker OR than its sibling reduces confidence.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Likely below PGS004549 within the same family due to weaker effect size; still plausible but not the top pick.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Knee OA concept match but phenotyping_reported is time-to-event (TTE) gonarthrosis; less aligned to generic case/control knee OA benchmarks.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Has PRS-comparable metrics: PGS-only AUROC=0.5566 and PGS-only R2=0.0068 (well below h2 ceiling, plausible but weak). Full-model AUROC=0.645 with incremental AUROC=0.0104 indicates limited PRS lift.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Pan-trait UKB framework (813 traits) archetype; EUR selected validation with large n=67,425, but framework scores often generalize worse than disease-focused scores.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Framework + sparse snpnet (4,525 variants) + TTE endpoint increases risk of underperformance in external benchmarks despite having explicit metrics.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Explicit PRS-only metrics are helpful but weak; given framework archetype and modest PRS-only signal, unlikely to rank #1 against strong genome-wide disease-targeted candidates.

rationale: PGS002767 has the cleanest direct knee-osteoarthritis endpoint labeling, uses a strong genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with ~1M variants, and is evaluated with basic demographic/PC/technical covariates (low comparability/leakage risk). While PGS004549 has a slightly higher OR and an ensemble-like method, its unknown covariates and risk-factor-integration context add uncertainty about how benchmark-comparable the signal is. The remaining candidates either broaden the endpoint (PGS002729) or are a pan-trait sparse/TTE framework score with weak PRS-only metrics (PGS001192).

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match: lung cancer / lung carcinoma; phenotyping is incident lung cancer (broad, not subtype- or age-restricted).
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only full-model discrimination reported (AUROC 0.846; C-index 0.849) plus modest HR per SD ~1.16; no PGS-only AUC/R2, and full-model likely heavily covariate-driven given extensive smoking/environment/family-history terms.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Large EUR evaluation (n=392,539) in a cross-cancer evaluation setting; transportability limited to EUR but robust sample size.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: High covariate complexity (family history, PM2.5, detailed smoking variables and interactions) makes the reported AUROC weakly informative about standalone PRS; genome-wide-significant-only (109 SNPs) may under-capture polygenic signal.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Strong endpoint match and huge eval N help, but lack of PRS-only metrics and covariate-inflated full-model AUROC reduce confidence that it will rank #1 on an external PRS-focused benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match: incident lung cancer; same endpoint framing as PGS000078.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Near-clone of PGS000078 with inverse weights; same full-model AUROC/C-index and similar HR (1.17). Reported R²=0.799 is almost certainly full-model/scale-mismatched for PRS comparison and not credible as PRS-only given lung cancer h2_liability ~0.15 ceiling.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same large EUR evaluation context (n=392,539) and similar covariate set; no added independent PRS-only validation evidence versus PGS000078.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Inverse-weight construction is a red flag for true PRS utility; same heavy covariate leakage concerns as PGS000078, plus the very high R² suggests non-comparable reporting.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Despite identical headline AUROC, the inverse-weight design and suspect R² reduce likelihood of top external-benchmark PRS performance versus other candidates.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match: incident lung cancer; case-control cohort context but still aligned to the target trait.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Uses LDpred2 with genome-wide coverage (1,143,554 variants), a strong structural signal when PRS-only metrics are absent across the shortlist. Full-model AUROC 0.893 is high but not PRS-only; OR per SD ~1.33 suggests moderate standalone PRS signal.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR evaluation but much smaller n (24,012) and single-record evidence; cohort is French-Canadian (still EUR-labeled) which may shift portability relative to broader EUR benchmarks.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Full-model AUROC likely boosted by smoking status and other covariates; smaller/single-cohort validation increases overfitting/optimism risk and reduces robustness evidence.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Best method/variant-count profile in the shortlist and a non-trivial OR signal make it the most plausible to rank highest on an external PRS-performance benchmark, despite smaller validation and covariate-inflated AUROC.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Partial mismatch: early-onset lung cancer (<50) rather than general lung cancer; this restriction can reduce relevance to a generic lung cancer benchmark.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model AUROC 0.811 with wide CI; no PRS-only metrics or effect sizes shown here. Method is sparse (clumped + LASSO) with 128 variants—structurally weaker than genome-wide shrinkage for broad polygenic capture.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Large evaluation (n=167,955) with mostly EUR; some AFR included in eval distribution but selected validation ancestry is European.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Endpoint restriction (early-onset) is the main risk for benchmark transfer; full-model AUROC not PRS-comparable.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Good study size, but endpoint mismatch and weaker structural PRS properties make top rank less likely.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Subtype mismatch: lung squamous cell carcinoma rather than overall lung cancer; not guaranteed to represent the umbrella endpoint in a generic benchmark.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model AUROC 0.778 and extremely small R² (0.000746) indicate weak signal as reported; P+T with 90 variants is structurally limited.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Large EUR evaluation (n=270,054) but single-record and subtype-specific.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Subtype restriction plus weak reported variance explained suggest low standalone PRS utility for broad lung cancer benchmarking.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Unlikely to rank #1 for a general lung cancer benchmark given subtype mismatch and weak metric signals.

rationale: All candidates lack clean PRS-only AUC/R2, so full-model AUROC is not a reliable cross-study comparator—especially for models with heavy smoking/family-history/environment covariates (PGS000078/PGS000789). Given similar endpoint alignment among the broad lung cancer models, the strongest remaining predictor of external PRS performance is structural PRS quality: PGS004860’s LDpred2 genome-wide construction (1.1M variants) plus a moderate per-SD OR signal makes it the most likely to deliver the best standalone PRS discrimination in a hidden external benchmark. Confidence is moderated by its smaller, single-cohort validation and covariate-inflated reported AUROC.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match to heart failure across trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported (Heart Failure). No horizon/packaging signals; looks like standard disease status modeling.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Has a PRS-comparable metric: Nagelkerke R2 (covariates regressed out)=0.006981, which is interpretable as PRS signal and is below the provided heritability ceiling (liability h2~0.12), so not obviously inflated. Full-model AUROC=0.75 is likely largely covariate-driven and is secondary.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Very large EUR evaluation (n=358,905) with basic covariates (age/sex interactions + PCs). Multi-biobank development context supports external-facing construction, though this is a global-biobank framework-style paper.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Framework/portability-style origin (“Global Biobank analyses…”) is a known penalty versus disease-focused HF-specific studies. Also evaluation is EUR-only despite multi-ancestry GWAS mix, so robustness outside EUR is not evidenced here.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Strongest direct PRS-only/PRS-comparable performance evidence in the shortlist (explicit covariates-regressed-out R2) plus clean endpoint and huge evaluation; despite framework penalty, this combination is most predictive of ranking well in an external benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match (heart failure) but phenotyping is explicitly “Prevalent heart failure,” which can be less transportable than generic/incident-inclusive definitions depending on benchmark design.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No PRS-only AUC/R2 reported; only full-model AUROC=0.72 and Brier skill score=0.065. Without isolated PRS contribution, the metric evidence is weaker for cross-model ranking.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Moderate validation size (n=40,989). Covariates are basic (age, sex, 5 PCs). Development appears disease-focused (HF genetic architecture paper; includes HERMES/GBMI/MVP etc.), which is a positive study-archetype signal.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Evaluation ancestry string is inconsistent (EVAL: MAE 100% but selected_validation_ancestry says European, African unspecified), adding uncertainty about the actual benchmark-relevant evaluation context. Prevalent-only endpoint may also misalign with some benchmarks.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Disease-focused study archetype is a plus, but lack of PRS-only metrics and endpoint prevalence framing reduce confidence it will outrank a candidate with explicit PRS-comparable R2.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct heart failure label, but comes from a broad biomarker genetics paper rather than a HF-focused PRS effort; endpoint fidelity is acceptable but study archetype is not disease-optimized.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only full-model C-index=0.635 and HR per SD=1.08 (weak effect-size signal). This suggests limited standalone PRS discrimination.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR-only dev/eval; decent validation size (n=135,300) but single-biobank (UKB) development, which often generalizes less well than multi-cohort disease-focused efforts.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Weak effect size (HR~1.08) is a strong negative for benchmark ranking; also older and not clearly optimized for HF prediction.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Low—metrics/effect size indicate weak PRS signal relative to other shortlist options.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Near-direct match: congestive heart failure (PheCode 428.1) is closely aligned to heart failure, but is a phecode-specific instantiation (still acceptable as a direct clinical diagnosis proxy).
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No PRS-only AUC/R2; reports full-model C-index ~0.754 and OR per SD=1.455 (moderate-to-strong effect-size evidence, but below the ≥1.5 ‘strong’ heuristic). Full-model C-index is not PRS-comparable and likely covariate-influenced.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Validation n=31,804 with basic covariates (age, sex, 20 PCs). Multi-ancestry eval split is listed, but selected_validation_ancestry shows European, creating some ambiguity about which record is being summarized.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Method-comparison paper (not necessarily optimized for best HF PRS, more benchmarking). Endpoint is CHF phecode (slight mismatch vs generic HF). Reliance on full-model C-index limits comparability.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Mid—effect size is meaningfully better than PGS000709, but absence of PRS-only metrics and slight endpoint/record ambiguity make it less benchmark-predictive than PGS001790.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Same endpoint family as PGS005083 (CHF phecode), similarly close to heart failure but not the exact generic HF label.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Similar full-model C-index (~0.754) and OR per SD=1.452, essentially a near-clone of PGS005083 with marginally weaker effect size.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same validation setting/size/covariates as PGS005083 (n=31,804; age/sex/20 PCs).
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same comparability limitations (full-model metric; benchmarking-paper context; slight endpoint mismatch). Also slightly weaker OR than PGS005083, so loses within-sibling tie-break.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Mid-to-low among the CHF siblings; unlikely to be #1 overall given lack of PRS-only metrics and slightly weaker effect size than PGS005083.
