candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Targets pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (a major subtype within pancreatic carcinoma) with incident PDAC endpoint; acceptable as a dominant-subtype match but not identical to umbrella pancreatic carcinoma.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Very high full-model AUROC 0.83 is likely driven by strong clinical packaging (diabetes onset categories, age at DM diagnosis, waist circumference, family history) rather than PRS; no PRS-only/incremental metrics provided, so PRS strength is not evidenced.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Validation ancestry not reported and sample size is modest (n~11,462); less transportability clarity than EUR-anchored large-cohort evaluations.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: High risk of covariate leakage/near-outcome prediction (diabetes timing/onset) inflating AUROC; curated 49-variant score may not outperform in PRS-only benchmarks despite headline AUROC.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Despite headline AUROC, likely not #1 in a PRS performance benchmark because the metric is non-comparable and heavily covariate-driven with unclear ancestry context.

rationale: Across the shortlist, all candidates lack clean PRS-only AUC/R², so the best-supported pick hinges on endpoint fidelity plus the most reliable external-validation context and interpretable PRS signal. PGS000083 is a direct incident pancreatic cancer score with very large EUR evaluation and a moderate HR per SD (~1.49) consistent with meaningful PRS discrimination. PGS000794 is flagged by its inverse-weight construction (high risk of degraded PRS), PGS002264’s AUROC is likely dominated by diabetes/clinical covariates with unclear ancestry, and PGS000663/PGS000725 show weaker discrimination and/or much weaker validation support.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match to osteoporosis with straightforward case/control-style phenotyping_reported="Osteoporosis"; good conceptual alignment.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Has explicit PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.5685; PGS-only R2=0.00688). Full-model AUROC is high but incremental AUROC is small (0.00477), indicating most discrimination is covariate-driven; PRS signal is modest but clearly quantified.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR development (UKB) with EUR-selected validation record; evaluation ancestry listed as mixed, but selected validation ancestry is European; validation n=24,905 is adequate and metrics are clearly reported.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Strong framework-paper risk: pan-trait sparse snpnet from "across 813 traits" UKB workflow tends to underperform disease-focused scores in external benchmarks. Sparse 316-variant model suggests limited polygenic capture for a complex disease.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Despite clean PRS-only metrics, the combination of pan-trait framework origin + very modest PRS-only performance makes it less likely to top an external benchmark when any more disease-optimized genome-wide score exists.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Near-direct match but endpoint is time-to-event and restricted to "osteoporosis without pathological fracture"; still within osteoporosis concept but less generic than the target.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Best PRS-comparable metrics in the shortlist: PGS-only AUROC=0.57595 and PGS-only R2=0.00945 (both higher than PGS001273). Incremental AUROC (0.00777) also higher, suggesting stronger PRS contribution (still modest overall).
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same UKB snpnet framework context as PGS001273 with EUR-selected validation record; validation n=24,905; metrics are explicit and comparable.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same major framework-paper penalty (pan-trait sparse UKB). Endpoint is TTE/subtype which may reduce transfer to a generic osteoporosis benchmark definition.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Within the snpnet framework siblings, this is the stronger one on PRS-only metrics and variant count (1270 vs 316), so it is the most plausible top performer among the framework options; still potentially beaten by a disease-focused genome-wide PRS if that PRS is truly standalone and well-validated.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Trait_reported is osteoporosis, but trait_efo includes "heel bone mineral density" alongside osteoporosis, introducing some endpoint/construct ambiguity versus a pure diagnosis endpoint.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No AUROC/R2 reported; only OR per SD=1.31 (moderate). This is supportive but less directly comparable than explicit PRS-only AUROC/R2 from other candidates.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR GWAS and EUR evaluation; validation n=39,444 is decent, but only one performance record and limited metric detail.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Endpoint mapping ambiguity (osteoporosis + heel BMD) and missing PRS-comparable discrimination metrics increase uncertainty; however method (PRS-CS, genome-wide shrinkage) is structurally strong.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Could transfer well due to PRS-CS genome-wide construction, but the moderate OR and lack of AUC/R2 make it harder to justify as most likely #1 versus a candidate with clearer disease endpoint and stronger/clearer signal.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match: phenotyping_reported="Osteoporosis" aligns cleanly with the target trait.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No AUROC/R2; reports OR per SD=1.328 (moderate, slightly higher than PGS002768). Method is an integrated/metaPRS approach with ~1.06M variants, a positive structural signal for capturing polygenic signal.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: DEV EUR (UKB) and EVAL EUR with relatively large validation n=56,192; however covariates are unknown, reducing comparability/interpretability of the reported effect size.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Potential risk of non-genetic risk-factor integration/packaging (title indicates integration of risk factor PRS with disease PRS). Even though the catalog entry is a PGS, the study framing raises concern that the reported effect size may reflect a composite or tuned integration rather than a clean standalone disease PRS; unknown covariates add uncertainty.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Strong endpoint fit + large-variant metaPRS structure + slightly stronger OR than alternatives gives plausible top-benchmark potential if it is a true standalone genetic score; but integration framing and missing metric detail lower certainty.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct-ish match but restricted to M81 (osteoporosis without pathological fracture), which is narrower than generic osteoporosis.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No AUROC/R2; OR per SD=1.3208 (moderate, slightly below PGS004565). Same large-variant metaPRS structure.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR dev/eval; validation n=56,192; covariates unknown.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same integration/packaging concern as PGS004565 plus narrower endpoint (M81) which may not align with a benchmark using broader osteoporosis definitions.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Very similar to PGS004565 but with slightly weaker OR and narrower endpoint, so less likely to rank #1 than its sibling.

rationale: Across the shortlist, the snpnet framework scores (PGS001273/PGS001274) provide explicit PRS-only AUROC/R2 but show only modest PRS signal and carry a strong pan-trait sparse-UKB framework penalty that often fails to top external benchmarks. PGS002768 has a strong method (PRS-CS) but weaker/less complete evidence (no AUC/R2; moderate OR; some endpoint ambiguity via heel BMD). Between the two Commun Biol metaPRS candidates, PGS004565 is the cleanest endpoint match (generic osteoporosis rather than M81-only) and has the strongest available effect-size signal (OR≈1.33) with a genome-wide/metaPRS structure and large EUR evaluation, making it the most likely to rank highest in a hidden external benchmark despite missing AUC/R2 and unknown covariates.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Near-direct match: PAD is a major, clinically coherent subset within the broader target label “peripheral vascular disease”; phenotyping is a clean clinical endpoint (incident PAD) without explicit restriction to a special subpopulation.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Strong PRS signal via effect size (HR per SD 1.66 with tight CI). Reported C-index 0.731 is full-model (age/sex/PCs) so not directly PRS-comparable, but covariates are light so it is less likely to be heavily inflated by clinical leakage.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Disease-focused multi-cohort development with very large evaluation (n~304k) and explicitly multi-ancestry evaluation; this is consistent with robustness/transportability rather than single-biobank internal optimization.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Main risk is metric comparability: lacks PGS-only AUC/R2 and relies on full-model C-index plus HR. Also incident-only endpoint may differ from some benchmarks that mix prevalent/incident, but this is a mild penalty given the disease-focused design.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: High: combines strong endpoint fidelity, genome-wide shrinkage (LDpred2) with very large variant count, and strong per-SD HR in a disease-focused multi-cohort setting—features that tend to rank well in external benchmarks versus framework/portability scores.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Exact label match to target (peripheral vascular disease, unspecified), but endpoint is vague/unspecified and appears as a UKB-derived portability-framework phenotype rather than a richly defined disease-focused endpoint.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Weak-to-modest PRS signal: partial-r 0.0175 (European selected record). This is PRS-comparable but small in magnitude, consistent with limited discriminative power.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Single-biobank (UKB) portability framework; evaluation exists across ancestries but the selected metric is EUR and the overall archetype is not disease-focused external validation.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Framework/portability penalty plus vague phenotype definition; small partial-r suggests low ceiling performance even if well-estimated.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Moderate-to-low: exact wording helps, but the combination of framework archetype and weak PRS-comparable metric usually underperforms a strong disease-focused PAD score in hidden external benchmarks.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Same as PGS002055: exact target label but vague/unspecified phenotype from the same UKB portability framework context.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Slightly weaker than PGS002055: partial-r 0.0151 (European selected record). Very sparse model (242 variants) also suggests limited polygenic capture.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same portability framework setting as PGS002055; no additional independent disease-focused validation signal.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Framework penalty + very sparse construction; small partial-r indicates weak standalone PRS contribution.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Low: near-clone of PGS002055 but with weaker metric and much lower variant count, making it less likely to top an external benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Partial match: PAD but explicitly restricted to individuals with type 2 diabetes (phenotyping_reported), which is a meaningful endpoint/population shift away from generic peripheral vascular disease.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Weak PRS signal: HR 1.13 per SD (small effect). No PRS-comparable AUC/R2 reported; small 19-SNP GWS score further suggests limited predictive power.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR-only evaluation with small validation sample (n~10.8k) and no clear training sample listed (N/A), reducing confidence in general benchmark transfer.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Strong restriction to T2D population plus heavy covariate set (many clinical/treatment variables) makes any downstream performance less comparable to PRS-only benchmarking; also very low variant count.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Low: restricted endpoint and weak effect size make it unlikely to rank #1 in a generic external benchmark for peripheral vascular disease.

rationale: PGS005217 has the strongest overall benchmark-rank signal: a clean disease endpoint (incident PAD), disease-focused multi-cohort design, genome-wide LDpred2 with very large variant count, and a strong per-SD HR (1.66). The exact-label UKB portability scores (PGS002055/PGS001843) provide PRS-comparable partial-r but the signal is small and the framework archetype plus vague phenotype lowers expected external-benchmark rank. PGS005158 is additionally penalized by its T2D-restricted endpoint and weak HR.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match: trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all Parkinson's disease. Generic disease status endpoint (not horizon-specific).
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only full-model metrics reported (AUROC=0.692; R²=0.054) so not PRS-only comparable; however includes a strong stratification effect (OR top 25% vs bottom 25% = 6.25) which supports meaningful PRS signal within this study family.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Disease-focused large meta-analysis family; evaluated in a small validation (n=999) but with basic covariates (PCs, age, sex). Evaluation ancestry listed as European (NR) despite broader EVAL mix in ancestry_distribution, so external comparability is acceptable but not maximally clear.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Main risk is metric comparability: full-model AUROC/R² likely covariate-influenced and not directly transferable as PRS-only performance. No heavy clinical covariates/packaging; method is C+T with many variants (1805), which is structurally stronger than GWAS-hit-only siblings here.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Strongest within the coherent Lancet Neurology sibling cluster: same endpoint/covariates/validation setting as PGS000902 but materially better discrimination and much richer variant set; likely to rank highest in an external benchmark among this shortlist.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match Parkinson's disease endpoint, aligned across fields.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only full-model AUROC reported (0.651, with CI). No PRS-only metrics or effect sizes; weaker than its sibling PGS000903 on the same evaluation context.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same disease-focused meta-analysis family and same validation size (n=999) with basic covariates (PCs, age, sex).
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Sparse GWAS-significant-only construction (90 variants) likely captures less polygenic signal than the C+T sibling; full-model AUROC not PRS-comparable.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: As a near-clone sibling, it is dominated by PGS000903 (higher AUROC and far more variants under similar covariates), so less likely to be #1.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Close but not perfect: phenotyping_reported is Incident Parkinson Disease (time-to-event framing) rather than generic case-control/status; still targets the same disease concept.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Reports HR (high vs low tertile)=1.72 (strong association signal), but no AUROC/R²; HR is not directly comparable to case-control AUROC and may reflect study-specific follow-up/hazard structure.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Very large evaluation sample (n=314,998) EUR with basic genetic covariates (array, 10 PCs). Training details are N/A, reducing interpretability of how the score was derived/optimized.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Endpoint/time-to-event and derivation opacity (samples_training N/A) increase uncertainty for external benchmark ranking; GWAS-hit-only with 44 SNPs may under-capture polygenic signal versus richer disease-meta-analysis scores.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Despite huge evaluation N and decent HR, the combination of incident-only framing and unclear training/derivation makes it less likely to beat the well-specified disease-meta-analysis family in a generic external PRS benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match Parkinson disease endpoint.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No AUROC/R²; only association p-value and a beta reported (scale unclear), offering weak cross-study comparability for ranking.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Small evaluation (n=786) EUR; basic covariates (age, sex, 2 PCs). Training details N/A.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Very small variant set (16) and limited performance reporting; likely underpowered/under-informative for external benchmark ranking.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Low: sparse model with weak comparable metrics and small validation, unlikely to outrank the better-supported meta-analysis-derived candidates.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match Parkinson's disease endpoint.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model AUROC=0.8 appears high but is paired with heavy non-genetic covariates including family history and multiple risk factors; without PRS-only/incremental metrics this AUROC is not strong evidence of PRS quality.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Moderate evaluation size (n=699) EUR; covariate set suggests a risk-factor integration model rather than clean PRS discrimination reporting.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: High comparability risk due to family history and multiple clinical/lifestyle covariates inflating full-model AUROC; PRS contribution cannot be isolated, making it unreliable for external PRS benchmark ranking.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Despite the headline AUROC, likely not #1 in a PRS-focused benchmark because the metric is probably covariate-driven and not comparable to cleaner PRS evaluations.

rationale: Across the shortlist, PGS000903 has the cleanest direct endpoint match within the strongest disease-focused study family and shows the best within-family performance signal versus its near-clone sibling (higher full-model AUROC plus strong risk stratification OR) while avoiding heavy clinical covariate packaging. Alternatives either have weaker sibling metrics (PGS000902), incident/time-to-event framing with unclear training (PGS003763), sparse/weakly reported evidence (PGS000123), or inflated full-model AUROC driven by family history and other risk factors (PGS001774).

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match: trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all align to prostate cancer/prostate carcinoma with no horizon/packaging qualifiers.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Best observed discrimination among shortlist siblings in the same evaluation context: full-model AUROC 0.7049 (CI tightly estimated) and highest reported OR per SD (~2.17). Note: metrics shown are full-model (no PGS-only/incremental), so differences are only meaningful as within-family tie-breaks.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same publication family and same validation setting as others (selected_validation_ancestry European; EVAL includes EUR+SAS; n=171,474). Record_count identical; validation size not differentiating but supports stability.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Covariates listed as 0 (clean, low leakage). Main risk is lack of PRS-only/incremental metrics, so AUROC may include baseline effects; however this limitation applies equally across all four candidates.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Within a near-clone set (same endpoint, cohorts, ancestry mix, covariate disclosure), the top-performing sibling by AUROC/OR is the strongest bet to rank #1 in an external benchmark; additionally MultiPRS ensemble structure is a positive structural signal versus single-method scores.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match to prostate cancer with consistent trait/phenotype fields; no endpoint mismatch signals.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Slightly weaker than the top sibling: full-model AUROC 0.7003 and OR per SD ~2.11. Differences are small and full-model, but still a within-family negative relative to PGS004155.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same validation ancestry/context and sample size as the rest (EUR-selected; EVAL EUR+SAS; n=171,474), so no advantage on robustness within this shortlist.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Covariates=0 (clean). Same key limitation: no PRS-only/incremental metrics, so cross-study comparability is limited.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Genome-wide shrinkage method is generally strong, but in this exact sibling cluster it is empirically behind the MultiPRS and does not have a compensating endpoint/validation advantage.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match to prostate cancer; phenotype alignment is equally strong as others.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model AUROC 0.6994 and OR per SD ~2.11—very close to PGS004139 but below the top candidate; no PRS-only metrics to argue otherwise.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same publication family and validation context (EUR-selected; EVAL EUR+SAS; n=171,474).
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Covariates=0 (clean). Same limitation: full-model-only reporting.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Competitive but not leading within the same-study near-clone set; lacks a clear structural or empirical edge over the top AUROC/OR sibling.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match to prostate cancer with consistent phenotype fields.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Weakest metrics in the shortlist: full-model AUROC 0.6962, lowest R² and OR per SD (~2.08).
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same validation context and size as others; no compensating validation breadth advantage.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Covariates=0 (clean) but otherwise dominated by weaker within-family performance.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Given identical endpoint/study context, the lowest-performing sibling is least likely to top an external benchmark.

rationale: All four candidates are endpoint-identical near-clones from the same publication family with the same (clean) covariate disclosure and the same validation context, and none reports PRS-only/incremental metrics. In this setting, the most reliable differentiator is within-family empirical performance: PGS004155 has the highest full-model AUROC and strongest effect-size signal, and its MultiPRS ensemble structure is an additional positive structural cue. The absence of PRS-only metrics keeps confidence at Moderate rather than High.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match: trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all align to carcinoma in situ of skin with no horizon/time-to-event packaging indicated.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Best apparent discrimination within this sibling set: full-model AUROC 0.569 (basic covariates only) and strongest effect size signals (OR per SD 1.401; top 1% vs rest OR 3.77). No PRS-only AUC/R2 reported, so rely more on effect sizes than small AUROC gaps.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same evaluation context as siblings (EUR; n=5,500; same covariates), so metrics are directly comparable within-shortlist; single validation record but consistent reporting.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Main risk is that only full-model metrics are provided (not PRS-only), limiting cross-study comparability; however covariates are basic (age/sex/PCs/batch) so inflation risk is modest and symmetric across candidates.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Within a near-clone family (same endpoint, cohorts, ancestry, covariates), the candidate with the strongest effect sizes and highest AUROC is the most likely to rank #1 externally; sparse 7-variant lassosum here appears to capture stronger signal than the other constructions for this endpoint.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match with identical phenotype labeling to the other candidates; no endpoint mismatch.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Intermediate performance: full-model AUROC 0.557; OR per SD 1.308; top 1% vs rest OR 2.45—consistently weaker than PGS000471 on all reported signals.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same EUR evaluation (n=5,500) and same basic covariates, enabling fair within-shortlist comparison; single record only.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same limitation of lacking PRS-only metrics; P+T with 5 variants may under-capture polygenic signal, but could be fine if architecture is sparse—still empirically weaker here.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Given identical study/endpoint context, its uniformly lower AUROC and ORs suggest it is unlikely to beat PGS000471 in an external benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match on all phenotype fields; no mismatch.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Weakest reported signals: full-model AUROC 0.524; OR per SD 1.09 (near-null); top 1% vs rest OR 1.48 with CI crossing/near 1—suggesting minimal PRS contribution despite genome-wide variant count.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same EUR evaluation (n=5,500) and same covariates; directly comparable within shortlist.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Despite method/variant-count appeal (PRS-CS, ~1.1M variants), the observed effect sizes indicate poor realized predictive signal in this setting; could reflect over-shrinkage, phenotype noise, or limited GWAS power, but benchmark transfer is still likely weak.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Low effect sizes and AUROC in the same evaluation framework strongly predict low external benchmark rank relative to its siblings.

rationale: All three candidates are endpoint-identical siblings (same publication family, EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL, same covariates, same validation size), so the most reliable differentiator is the within-family empirical signal. PGS000471 has the highest AUROC and clearly strongest effect sizes (OR per SD and top-1% OR), making it the most likely to rank highest in a hidden external benchmark. Confidence is moderate because PRS-only metrics are absent for all candidates, so we must infer PRS strength from effect sizes and a covariate-adjusted AUROC.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Trait label matches vitiligo, but phenotyping_reported is clearly mismatched ("Red hair"), creating endpoint incoherence despite the vitiligo fields.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No PRS-comparable AUC/R2; only a pseudo R² (~0.039) and a beta reported, which are hard to compare and not clearly PRS-only in a standard validation frame.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR eval with modest n=4,702, but endpoint ambiguity undermines interpretability of any validation.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: High risk of catalog/phenotype contamination given the red-hair phenotype; unknown covariates further reduce comparability.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Weak: endpoint incoherence plus lack of clean PRS-only metrics makes it unlikely to rank #1 in an external benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Close but not perfect: vitiligo is direct, but framed as time-to-event (TTE), which can be less comparable to generic case-control vitiligo benchmarks.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Has explicit PRS-comparable metrics: PGS-only AUROC 0.642 and PGS-only R² 0.016 (well below h2 ceiling, so plausible). Incremental AUROC reported, but full-model AUROC is not the key signal.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Large evaluation (n=67,425) with a European selected record; covariates are basic (age/sex/PCs/array), supporting comparability. However, it is from a pan-trait UKB sparse-score framework (snpnet across 813 traits), which historically generalizes less well.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Moderate: framework-origin + sparse model (77 variants) and TTE endpoint increase risk of weaker external transfer despite clean metric reporting.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Moderate: strongest on-paper PRS-only metrics in the shortlist, but penalized by framework archetype and TTE framing.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Trait label says vitiligo, but phenotyping_reported is a treatment-induced/therapy-context endpoint (anti-PD-L1 induced hypothyroidism in cancer patients), which is not a direct vitiligo disease endpoint.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No AUC/R2; only an HR per SD ~1.41 (moderate signal) plus a meta-analysis p-value, but the HR pertains to the therapy-specific endpoint context, limiting relevance.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR eval but small n=1,584; basic covariates (PCs) are fine, yet endpoint mismatch dominates.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: High: endpoint is explicitly non-target and context-restricted (cancer immunotherapy adverse event), so external benchmark on vitiligo risk is unlikely to favor it.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Weak: despite large training n, the endpoint mismatch makes top benchmark performance unlikely.

rationale: Among the three, PGS001536 is the only candidate with coherent vitiligo phenotyping (TTE vitiligo) and explicit PRS-comparable performance (PGS-only AUROC/R²) under basic covariates, making it the most defensible predictor of external benchmark rank. The other two have severe endpoint incoherence/mismatch (PGS000738: red-hair phenotype; PGS000760: therapy-induced hypothyroidism endpoint), which is typically fatal for benchmark performance on vitiligo.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match: trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all schizophrenia.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only full-model AUROC reported (0.64) with basic covariates; no PGS-only AUC/R2, so limited PRS-comparable signal. OR per SD ~1.7 is supportive.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR evaluation; moderate validation n=18,461; same study family as several siblings so context is consistent.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Full-model AUROC not directly comparable across candidates; otherwise low leakage risk (covariates are basic).
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Solid direct-match disease-focused sibling with supportive OR, but not the strongest within-family full-model AUROC and not the largest variant count.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match schizophrenia across all phenotype fields.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model AUROC 0.60 (basic covariates) and OR per SD ~1.69; weaker discrimination signal than other siblings; no PRS-only metrics.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR evaluation; n=33,694 (larger), but validation size is a weak differentiator within near-clones.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Low covariate leakage risk; main risk is simply weaker observed discrimination within the same design family.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Within a near-identical sibling set, the lower AUROC makes it less likely to be the top external performer.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match schizophrenia across all phenotype fields.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Highest reported full-model AUROC in the sibling cluster (0.74) with the same basic covariates; no PRS-only metrics/effect size, but the AUROC gap vs siblings is large enough to be meaningful within-family.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR evaluation; smaller n=9,569, but still a reasonable external sample and less important than the strong within-family metric/structure signals.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Potential that AUROC reflects case-mix differences, but covariates are comparable to siblings and no heavy clinical predictors are used.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Best within-family discrimination signal plus near-max genome-wide variant count among the PRS-CS siblings, making it the most likely to rank #1 in an external benchmark among this shortlist.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match schizophrenia across all phenotype fields.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model AUROC 0.60 and OR per SD ~1.48 (weaker effect-size signal than other siblings); no PRS-only metrics.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR evaluation; largest n=44,436, but this is a weak tie-break and does not offset weaker discrimination/effect size within the same study family.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Low leakage risk; main risk is weaker PRS signal suggested by lower OR and AUROC.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Despite large validation, the weaker within-family performance signals make top benchmark rank less likely.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Endpoint mismatch: phenotyping_reported is cognitive function, not schizophrenia diagnosis; despite trait_reported/efo being schizophrenia, this looks like a cross-trait application context rather than a direct disease endpoint evaluation.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Reports partial R² ~0.008 (not directly comparable to case-control discrimination for schizophrenia risk); no AUROC and metric is tied to cognition outcome modeling.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR evaluation; small n=2,524; many records (50) but record_count is not predictive and likely reflects multiple subgroup/analysis variants.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: High risk of metadata/endpoint incoherence for the target benchmark (schizophrenia risk prediction).
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Low likelihood to rank highly in a schizophrenia PRS benchmark due to explicit endpoint mismatch and non-comparable metric.

rationale: All four PRS-CS candidates (PGS000133/134/135/136) are near-clones from the same study with the same schizophrenia endpoint, EUR evaluation, and basic covariates, so within-family differences in reported discrimination and structural properties are the most informative. PGS000135 has the highest full-model AUROC (0.74 vs ~0.60–0.64) under comparable covariates and also has the largest variant count among the PRS-CS siblings, making it the strongest signal for top external benchmark performance. PGS002785 is deprioritized due to clear endpoint mismatch (cognition outcome) and non-comparable partial R².

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match to target via idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (a specific pulmonary fibrosis endpoint); phenotyping_reported is a direct diagnosis endpoint (not horizon-packaged).
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Has a PRS-comparable metric: Nagelkerke R2 (covariates regressed out) = 0.005929 (interpretable as PRS-only signal). Full-model AUROC=0.758 is not treated as PRS-only. PRS-only R2 is plausible vs provided h2_obs ceiling context (well below liability-scale h2; not an obvious reporting artifact).
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Very large EUR evaluation (n=347,350) and developed in a broad multi-biobank context, which tends to be more externally oriented than single-cohort development; evaluation ancestry matches selected record (EUR).
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Framework-style global biobank paper (not a single disease-consortium build), so some penalty vs disease-focused bespoke models; also no PRS-only AUROC reported. However covariates are basic (age/sex/PC-style) and the PRS-only R2 is explicitly provided, reducing comparability risk.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Best combination of endpoint fidelity + explicit PRS-only (covariates-regressed-out) performance metric + large external-style evaluation. Likely to transfer better than sparse pan-trait UKB score and better-supported than a 23-SNP GWS score with only quintile HR.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct IPF match; phenotyping is incident IPF (acceptable but slightly narrower than generic disease status for a generic 'pulmonary fibrosis' target).
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No PRS-only AUC/R2; only HR high-vs-low PRS quintile = 3.78, which is not directly comparable across studies and is sensitive to cutpoints and baseline hazard; lacks per-SD effect size.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Large EUR cohort (n=402,042), but appears embedded in an exposure-focused prospective analysis; less clear that the PRS was optimized/benchmarked as a standalone transferable predictor.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Method is genome-wide significant SNPs with only 23 variants—structurally likely to under-capture polygenic signal unless architecture is extremely oligogenic (not established here). Covariates include multiple epidemiologic factors (education, smoking, pack-years, BMI), making any implied model performance less PRS-comparable (though no AUC is reported anyway).
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Despite large N and strong-looking quintile HR, missing PRS-comparable metrics plus very small SNP set makes it less likely to rank #1 in an external benchmark than a genome-wide shrinkage score with explicit PRS-only R2.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match to pulmonary fibrosis (broader than IPF, which is fine for the target). Phenotyping_reported is a direct disease endpoint.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Reports PRS-only AUROC=0.6252 and PRS-only R2=0.0142, which are strong as standalone metrics within this shortlist. However the selected classification AUROC=0.8015 is full-model and not comparable; incremental AUROC is modest (0.01818), suggesting much of full-model discrimination is covariate-driven.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Validation n=24,905 (much smaller) and comes from a pan-trait UKB framework archetype; evaluation includes multiple ancestries overall but the selected record is EUR, and the framework setting is known to generalize less well than disease-focused builds.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Strong framework penalty: '813 traits in UK Biobank' snpnet sparse model with only 51 variants and single-biobank development—often underperforms in independent external benchmarks despite clean reporting. Smaller validation also increases uncertainty about stability.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Even with higher reported PRS-only R2 than PGS001791, the combination of pan-trait framework origin + very sparse model is a major negative for hidden external benchmark rank; likely to be outperformed by a genome-wide shrinkage multi-biobank score.

rationale: PGS001791 is the most benchmark-plausible winner because it pairs a direct pulmonary-fibrosis endpoint (IPF) with an explicitly PRS-comparable metric (covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2) and a large EUR evaluation in a multi-biobank context. PGS001030 has stronger reported PRS-only metrics but carries a substantial pan-trait sparse-UKB framework penalty that typically hurts external benchmark ranking. PGS004695 lacks PRS-comparable discrimination metrics and is a very small GWS-variant score reported mainly via quintile HR in an exposure-focused cohort, making top benchmark performance less likely.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match on trait_reported/trait_efo (rheumatoid arthritis) with phenotyping_reported = Seropositive RA (a clinically coherent RA subtype; acceptable for RA target though slightly narrower than all-RA).
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Best-looking reported discrimination within this sibling set: full-model AUROC 0.7469 (CI 0.713–0.781) and R² 0.1376 plus strong per-SD effect sizes (OR 2.46). However metrics appear to be full-model (PGS-only/incremental not provided), so cross-model comparability is limited; still useful as within-family evidence.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same publication family and evaluation context as others; selected_validation_ancestry European with large eval n=90,274. Multi-ancestry evaluation exists (EUR/SAS split shown) but selected record is EUR; overall validation support is solid and comparable to siblings.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Main risk is interpretability: covariates listed as 0 yet only full-model metrics are shown, so it’s unclear how much is PRS-only vs baseline; also phenotype is seropositive-only (possible attenuation if benchmark uses broader RA). Otherwise low leakage risk (no clinical risk calculator/biomarkers indicated).
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Strong: among near-clone candidates (same endpoint family, same cohorts, same eval size/ancestry context), it has the highest AUROC/R² and strongest OR, and it is an ensemble (MultiPRS) which is a positive structural signal when everything else is aligned.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Same direct RA match with phenotyping_reported = Seropositive RA; same slight subtype narrowing as others.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model AUROC 0.7283 and R² 0.1220; OR 2.37. Strong but consistently below PGS004163 on all reported metrics/effect sizes in the same setting.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same evaluation ancestry (EUR) and same large eval n=90,274; essentially identical validation context to the rest of the set.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same main risk: only full-model metrics; covariates field is 0 but PRS-only/incremental not shown. Otherwise low leakage concerns.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Moderate: LDpred2.CV is a strong single-score method, but within this tightly matched sibling family it is outperformed by the MultiPRS ensemble on the reported validation record.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct RA match; phenotyping_reported Seropositive RA (narrower than all-RA but coherent).
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model AUROC 0.7193 and R² 0.1129; OR 2.22. Weaker than PGS004163/PGS004049 on both discrimination and effect size.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same publication family and same eval context (EUR selected; n=90,274).
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same full-model-only metric limitation; otherwise low covariate leakage indicated.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Moderate-low: megaprs.CV is plausible, but reported performance is mid-pack among near-identical siblings, suggesting lower likelihood of topping an external benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct RA match; phenotyping_reported Seropositive RA.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Lowest R² in the set (0.0905) and low AUROC (0.7124) with OR 2.13; also auto-tuned variant may be less optimized than CV siblings here.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same EUR selected validation and n=90,274; comparable support.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same metric comparability limitation; otherwise low leakage indicated.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Low: consistently weakest reported performance among these near-clones, so unlikely to rank #1 externally.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct RA match; phenotyping_reported Seropositive RA.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model AUROC 0.7110 with R² 0.0994; OR 2.11. Similar to PGS004064 and below the top two; lassosum.CV doesn’t show an empirical edge here.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same EUR selected validation and n=90,274; comparable support.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same full-model-only metric limitation; otherwise low leakage indicated.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Low-moderate: performance is near the bottom of this matched sibling cluster, reducing likelihood of being the external top performer.

rationale: All candidates are near-clones from the same study family with the same seropositive-RA endpoint, similar ancestry context, and identical evaluation size, and none provides PRS-only/incremental metrics—so small AUROC differences are usually weak. Here, however, PGS004163 shows a consistent across-the-board advantage (highest AUROC, highest R², strongest OR) and also has a positive structural signal (MultiPRS ensemble), making it the most likely to rank #1 in an external benchmark among this shortlist.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match at the mapped level (trait_efo=retinal detachment) but reported/phenotyped endpoint is broader (“Retinal detachments and defects”), which is still close and plausibly inclusive of the target.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only partial correlation reported (partial-r=0.0276, CI 0.0135–0.0416); no PRS-only AUROC/R2. Partial-r is a weaker, less interpretable performance signal for cross-study ranking than explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same-cohort portability framework (UKB-derived, evaluated across multiple ancestries; selected record is European). Validation N ~19,445 is adequate but not a strong differentiator; multi-ancestry eval is a mild robustness positive.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Framework/portability archetype (UKB-to-UKB) raises risk of weaker external transfer vs disease-focused models; also metric sparsity (no AUROC/R2) lowers confidence. Covariates are basic/demographic+PCs (clean).
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Despite strong method/coverage (LDpred2, ~707k variants), the combination of (i) portability-framework origin and (ii) weak/indirect metric reporting makes it less likely to be the top performer in a hidden external benchmark than a direct endpoint model with explicit PRS-only metrics.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Same as PGS002040: close but slightly broader endpoint (“detachments and defects”) rather than the narrower target label; still a reasonable direct match.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only partial correlation (partial-r=0.0218, CI 0.0078–0.0359); weaker than PGS002040 and lacks PRS-only AUROC/R2.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same portability framework and validation context as PGS002040 (UKB; selected European record; N ~19,445).
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same framework/transfer risk and missing PRS-comparable metrics; additionally much smaller variant count (3,737) suggests less polygenic signal capture than the LDpred2 sibling.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Within the portability siblings, this looks dominated by PGS002040 (lower partial-r and far fewer variants), so unlikely to rank #1 overall.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Best endpoint fidelity: trait_reported and phenotyping_reported are exactly “Retinal detachment” (direct match to target).
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Has explicit PRS-only metrics: PGS AUROC (no covariates)=0.573 and PGS R2 (no covariates)=0.00663. These are interpretable and pass the heritability sanity check (R2 well below local h2_obs ~0.004–0.005; scale differences aside, nothing looks implausibly inflated). Incremental AUROC=0.0185 indicates non-trivial PRS contribution.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Pan-trait UKB framework (813 traits) but with clear European validation record and CIs reported; validation N ~24,905. Covariates are basic (age/sex/array/PCs).
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Framework penalty applies (pan-trait sparse snpnet), but here it is partially offset by having clean, PRS-only performance metrics and exact endpoint alignment. Variant count is small (321), consistent with sparse architecture and potential external fragility, but metrics suggest it captures measurable signal.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Among the shortlist, it has the strongest combination of endpoint fidelity + directly comparable PRS-only performance evidence; this is typically the best predictor of ranking well in an external benchmark when no disease-focused multi-cohort alternative is present.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Partial mismatch: time-to-event phenotype (“TTE retinal detachments and breaks”) and includes retinal breaks in addition to detachment; still related but less faithful to the generic target endpoint than PGS001137.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Explicit PRS-only metrics exist but weaker: PGS AUROC (no covariates)=0.542 and PGS R2 (no covariates)=0.00213; incremental AUROC=0.00606 is small. Overall PRS signal is clearly lower than PGS001137.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same pan-trait UKB framework family as PGS001137; European validation record; N ~24,905; basic covariates.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Added endpoint complexity (TTE + composite with breaks) increases comparability risk; weaker PRS-only metrics suggest lower true ranking potential.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Likely to rank below PGS001137 due to both weaker PRS-only performance and less direct endpoint fidelity.

rationale: PGS001137 is the most likely #1 in a hidden external benchmark because it combines the cleanest endpoint match (phenotyping_reported exactly retinal detachment) with the strongest directly comparable PRS-only performance evidence (PGS-only AUROC/R2 and a larger incremental AUROC than the other snpnet sibling). The portability/LDpred2 candidates have broader endpoints and lack PRS-comparable AUROC/R2, making their apparent strength harder to trust for benchmark ranking despite higher variant counts.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match to sarcoidosis (trait_efo sarcoidosis; phenotyping_reported Sarcoidosis). No horizon packaging; standard case/control-style UKB phenotype implied.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Has PRS-comparable metrics: PGS-only AUROC 0.6428 and PGS-only R2 0.0174 (below the h2_liability ceiling 0.107; plausible). Full-model AUROC 0.6486 adds little; incremental AUROC reported but not central. Overall moderate signal.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Single-biobank framework score ("across 813 traits"), evaluated in EUR (selected) with large n=67,425; multi-ancestry listed but selected record is EUR. Validation is internal/UKB-context rather than clearly external.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Framework/pan-trait sparse snpnet with very low variant count (12) is a portability risk; likely under-captures polygenic signal and tends to generalize worse than more disease-optimized genome-wide scores. Covariates are basic (low leakage).
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Good endpoint fidelity and clean PRS-only metrics help, but strong framework + extreme sparsity are negative for hidden external benchmark transfer; likely not top if a better-structured same-endpoint alternative exists.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Partial mismatch: time-to-event (TTE sarcoidosis) rather than generic disease status. Still same disease concept, but endpoint form can reduce comparability to typical external case/control benchmarks.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Slightly better PRS-only metrics than PGS000922 (PGS-only AUROC 0.6456; PGS-only R2 0.0180; plausible vs h2 ceiling). Full-model AUROC 0.6546 similarly modest. Net: marginally stronger than PGS000922 on metrics.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same pan-trait UKB snpnet framework and same EUR-selected validation context (n=67,425). Not clearly external; multi-ancestry listed but not the selected record.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same framework + sparsity risk (22 variants) plus added endpoint-form risk (TTE). Covariates basic (low leakage).
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Among the two snpnet siblings, this is the stronger one on PRS-only metrics, but TTE packaging and framework origin still make it less likely to rank #1 in an external benchmark than a more standard endpoint, genome-wide score.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Concept alignment is muddied: trait_efo is skin sarcoidosis while trait_reported/phenotyping_reported say Sarcoidosis. Treat as likely sarcoidosis phenotype but with some metadata/endpoint ambiguity penalty.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No PRS-only AUROC/R2; only partial correlation (partial-r=0.0199, CI 0.0059–0.0338). This is weak-to-moderate and harder to compare to AUROC-based candidates; still indicates nonzero signal.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: From a portability-focused UKB-derived study; evaluation spans multiple ancestries in the study design, but selected validation ancestry is EUR and validation n is smaller (19,670). Still, the paper’s focus on portability is mildly supportive for external transfer vs pan-trait sparse.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Portability-framework penalty (not disease-optimized) and endpoint/EFO ambiguity. Method is penalized regression with modest variant count (79), which may underperform genome-wide shrinkage for polygenic architectures.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Better structural/portability orientation than the pan-trait sparse snpnet scores, but limited comparable metrics and smaller/less-informative performance reporting reduce confidence it would top an external benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Same endpoint ambiguity as PGS001872 (trait_efo skin sarcoidosis vs reported/phenotyping Sarcoidosis), but otherwise aligned to sarcoidosis in the phenotype field.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only partial correlation reported (partial-r=0.0184, CI 0.0044–0.0324), slightly lower than PGS001872; no PRS-only AUROC/R2.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same portability-focused UKB-derived study context as PGS001872; EUR-selected validation with n=19,670. Portability framing is mildly supportive for external transfer, though still UKB-derived.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Portability-framework penalty and endpoint/EFO ambiguity remain. However, LDpred2 genome-wide shrinkage with very large variant count (403,417) is a strong structural signal for capturing polygenic signal and typically transfers better than very sparse models.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Despite slightly lower partial-r than PGS001872, the combination of genome-wide shrinkage + dense variant set is the strongest structural indicator in the shortlist for external benchmark performance, outweighing the small partial-r difference and the lack of AUROC.

rationale: All candidates are UKB-derived framework-style scores, so the decision hinges on which is most likely to generalize in an external benchmark. The snpnet models (PGS000922/PGS000923) have clean PRS-only AUROC/R2 but are extremely sparse pan-trait scores, a known negative for external transfer; PGS000923 also adds a time-to-event endpoint mismatch. Between the portability-paper candidates, PGS002084 uses LDpred2 with genome-wide coverage (403k variants), the strongest structural signal for capturing polygenic signal and portability, making it the most likely #1 in a hidden external benchmark despite only partial-r being reported and some endpoint/EFO ambiguity.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match: trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all align to squamous cell carcinoma; no horizon/packaging signals.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only full-model AUROC reported (0.599) plus pseudo-R2 (0.0304) and per-SD OR 1.491; covariates are basic (age/sex/batch/PCs), so full-model AUROC is at least somewhat interpretable. Slightly stronger AUROC and per-SD OR than the close PRSweb siblings.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Independent evaluation in EUR with n=8,473; modest size but consistent with the PRSweb evaluation setup.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: GWAS-hits sparse score (13 variants) limits polygenic capture; no PGS-only AUC/R2 so cross-study comparability is limited, but within-family comparison is feasible given similar covariates/endpoints.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Within the tight PRSweb cluster (same endpoint/covariates/ancestry), this has the best combined discrimination/effect-size package (highest AUROC and highest per-SD OR), making it the most likely to rank #1 in an external benchmark among these near-clones.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match on all phenotype fields for squamous cell carcinoma.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model AUROC 0.59 and per-SD OR 1.4; no PRS-only metrics and no additional supporting metrics. Slightly weaker than the best PRSweb sibling on both AUROC and OR.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR evaluation n=20,468 (larger), but validation size is a weak differentiator when metrics are similar and design is comparable.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Very sparse (10 variants) and essentially a near-clone of other sparse SCC scores; limited evidence beyond one AUROC/OR pair.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Looks like a weaker-performing sibling relative to the top PRSweb candidate; larger validation alone is unlikely to translate into higher benchmark rank.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match on SCC; phenotyping reported aligns, but covariates are unknown which reduces comparability.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model AUROC 0.605 (highest point estimate here) and per-SD OR 1.44; however AUROC lacks CI and covariate set is unknown, so the apparent AUROC edge is discounted.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Large EUR evaluation n=88,924 is supportive for stability, but still a weak primary signal absent PRS-only metrics and with unknown covariates.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Training sample listed as N/A and covariates unknown; method is C+T-like with only 14 variants, raising risk that reported performance is not directly comparable to the PRSweb evaluations.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Could rank well if the benchmark matches this study’s evaluation setup, but metadata gaps (unknown covariates/training) make it less reliably ‘best-supported’ than the coherent PRSweb cluster where comparisons are cleaner.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match SCC across trait/efo/phenotyping.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model AUROC 0.589 and per-SD OR 1.457; includes pseudo-R2 0.0282. Slightly weaker than PGS000461 on AUROC, pseudo-R2, and per-SD OR (despite higher top-1% OR, which is threshold-dependent).
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR evaluation n=8,473 (same PRSweb evaluation context).
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Sparse GWAS-hits (10 variants) and no PRS-only metrics; otherwise clean/basic covariates.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Highly comparable to PGS000461 but with consistently slightly weaker core signals; unlikely to outrank it in an external benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match SCC across all phenotype fields.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model AUROC 0.593 and per-SD OR 1.448; pseudo-R2 0.0268. Slightly better AUROC than PGS000465 but weaker than PGS000461 on AUROC, pseudo-R2, and per-SD OR.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR evaluation n=8,473 (same PRSweb evaluation context).
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Very sparse (7 variants) P+T; no PRS-only metrics; otherwise clean/basic covariates.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Same-family near-clone with slightly weaker overall signal than PGS000461; not the most likely #1.

rationale: All candidates are direct endpoint matches and none reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so selection leans on within-context comparability and effect-size strength. PGS000461 is in the coherent PRSweb family with clean/basic covariates and shows the strongest combined signal among the most comparable siblings (highest full-model AUROC, highest pseudo-R2, and highest per-SD OR). PGS000731 has a slightly higher AUROC and much larger validation, but unknown covariates/training make that AUROC less benchmark-predictive than the cleaner, internally comparable PRSweb evidence.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match (Psoriasis; phenotyping_reported=Psoriasis). Not horizon/incident restricted. However it is from a pan-trait UKB sparse-score framework, which is a negative archetype for external transfer despite correct label.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Has PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC≈0.692; PGS-only R2≈0.052). Full-model AUROC only slightly higher, suggesting limited covariate inflation. Metrics are strong within this shortlist, but note potential scale/definition mismatch vs heritability sanity-check and typical external drop for framework scores.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Evaluated in UKB with EUR selected record; also lists multi-ancestry eval distribution but still within same cohort context. Validation n=67,425 is decent but not independent multi-cohort replication.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: High framework-risk: '813 traits in UK Biobank' + sparse snpnet with low variant count (204) suggests internal optimization and weaker portability. Single-biobank development/validation increases optimism risk.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Good on-paper PRS-only AUROC/R2 and clean covariates, but benchmark likely rewards externally robust disease-focused construction; framework penalty meaningfully lowers expected rank despite explicit metrics.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match (Psoriasis; phenotyping_reported=Psoriasis). Endpoint is generic disease status, appropriate for target.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only partial correlation reported (partial-r≈0.0636). This is PRS-signal but less directly comparable than AUROC/R2; magnitude is modest and very close to sibling PGS002083.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: From UKB portability study; EUR selected validation with n=19,615. Portability framing implies multi-ancestry evaluation within UKB, but still not independent external cohorts.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Portability-framework archetype (UKB-derived applied to ancestry groups in same cohort) is a known weaker external-transfer signal than disease-focused multi-cohort studies. Penalized regression is reasonable but still within framework context; metrics are limited.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Moderate: clean endpoint, but weak/indirect metric and framework-style design reduce likelihood of topping an external benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match (Psoriasis; phenotyping_reported=Psoriasis). Appropriate endpoint.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Partial correlation reported (partial-r≈0.0632), essentially tied/slightly below PGS001871. Structural upside: LDpred2 genome-wide shrinkage with 71,744 variants (stronger polygenic capture signal than sparse/low-SNP scores).
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same portability-study setting as PGS001871 (UKB-derived, evaluated across ancestry groups within UKB); EUR selected validation n=19,615. No independent external cohorts shown here.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Framework/portability-study risk remains, but method family (LDpred2) and genome-wide coverage reduce the typical sparse-framework portability penalty relative to snpnet sparse scores and relative to small GWAS-hit sets.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Best structural bet for external benchmark among the framework-derived options: genome-wide shrinkage + high variant count tends to rank well when endpoint matches and other evidence is similar, even if reported metric is only partial-r.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Partial mismatch: trait_reported indicates time-to-event and phenotyping_reported='TTE psoriasis'. For a generic psoriasis target, TTE framing is a penalty versus plain case/control disease status.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Has PRS-only AUROC≈0.673 and R2≈0.050, both weaker than PGS001312. Metrics are PRS-comparable and covariate-light, but endpoint mismatch limits comparability.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same pan-trait UKB framework family as PGS001312 with EUR selected validation; n=67,425. Not independent external validation.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Two risks: (1) pan-trait sparse framework origin; (2) time-to-event endpoint packaging can reduce transfer to generic disease-status benchmarks.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Lower: weaker metrics than its sibling plus endpoint mismatch makes it unlikely to be top-ranked externally.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Partial mismatch: phenotyping_reported='Incident psoriasis' (prospective incident-only). For generic psoriasis risk/status benchmarks, incident-only can underperform or be less comparable than prevalent+incident case/control endpoints.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No AUROC/R2/PRS-only discrimination reported; only lifestyle-stratified OR/HR style summaries (e.g., HR/OR≈4.6 for 'poor lifestyle and high genetic risk'), which are not clean per-SD PRS effect sizes and are heavily confounded by joint exposure stratification.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Large EUR evaluation n=345,672, but this is within a lifestyle+genetic risk study context rather than a PRS performance validation; training is N/A and PRS construction is simple (62 GWS variants).
candidate_audits.risk_signal: High comparability risk: endpoint is incident-only and reported effects are bundled with lifestyle strata and multiple covariates; small SNP set (62) may miss polygenic signal. Metrics are not directly usable for benchmark ranking.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Despite large n, lack of PRS-comparable performance and risk-wrapper framing make it unlikely to rank #1 in an external PRS benchmark.

rationale: All candidates are UKB-centric and several are explicitly framework-derived; none shows clear independent multi-cohort external validation. Given that, the strongest predictor of external benchmark rank becomes structural PRS quality under a matched endpoint. PGS002083 keeps a direct psoriasis endpoint while using genome-wide shrinkage (LDpred2) with very high variant count, which is a more reliable external-performance signal than sparse snpnet framework scores (PGS001312/PGS001313) and more robust than a small GWS-variant incident/lifestyle-wrapped score (PGS002293). Between the two portability-study siblings (PGS001871 vs PGS002083), partial-r is essentially tied, so method/coverage breaks the tie in favor of PGS002083.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match: trait_efo thyroid carcinoma; phenotyping_reported “Thyroid cancer” (generic case/control-style disease endpoint).
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only full-model metrics with basic covariates; AUROC 0.618 and Nagelkerke R² 0.0365 are modest. Per-SD OR 1.568 suggests moderate-to-strong PRS signal; top 1% vs rest OR 5.14 is supportive but tail metrics can be unstable.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Independent evaluation in EUR with n=4,270; single record. Reasonable external-style biobank evaluation within same publication family.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Sparse P+T with 8 variants risks under-capturing polygenic signal; full-model AUROC not PRS-only (but covariates are light: age/sex/PCs/batch).
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Within the PRSweb sibling set, performance is not top; likely mid-pack given similar endpoint/covariates but lower AUROC/OR than best sibling.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match: thyroid cancer / thyroid carcinoma; phenotyping_reported “Thyroid cancer” aligns cleanly.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model AUROC 0.636 and Nagelkerke R² 0.0478 are the strongest among the PRSweb siblings; per-SD OR 1.651 is also the strongest OR signal in that cluster (supports better standalone PRS discrimination even though AUROC is full-model).
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR evaluation n=1,778 (smaller than MGI-based siblings) but same light covariates and same study family; effect-size evidence helps offset smaller n.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: GWAS-hits with 10 variants is still sparse; metrics are full-model (not PRS-only). However covariates are basic and comparable, limiting inflation concerns.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Best-supported likely #1 within the coherent direct-match PRSweb cluster because it has the strongest combined discrimination/effect-size signals under comparable endpoint/covariates.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match on trait and phenotyping (“Thyroid cancer”).
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model AUROC 0.626 and Nagelkerke R² 0.0393 are weaker than PGS000631; per-SD OR 1.598 is supportive but not top in cluster.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: n=4,270 with mixed eval ancestry listed (EUR/MAE) but selected validation ancestry is European; record_count=2 suggests multiple evals but doesn’t add much predictive value.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Sparse GWAS-hits (10 variants) and full-model-only metrics; slight ambiguity from mixed-ancestry evaluation listing could indicate heterogeneity.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Likely below PGS000631 on transferable PRS signal given weaker OR/R² under otherwise similar design.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match: thyroid cancer endpoint; phenotyping_reported aligns.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model AUROC 0.628 and Nagelkerke R² 0.0447 are close but still below PGS000631 on AUROC/R² and OR; per-SD OR 1.609 is moderate-strong.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR evaluation n=1,778; same covariates and study family as PGS000631, enabling fair within-family comparison.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Very sparse P+T with only 5 variants increases risk of missing polygenic signal; full-model-only metrics.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Near-clone of PGS000631 but structurally weaker (fewer variants) and empirically slightly weaker; unlikely to beat PGS000631 in hidden benchmark.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Phenotyping is “Incident thyroid cancer” (time-to-event/incident-only) rather than generic disease status; still close but not identical to the other direct disease endpoints.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Reported AUROC 0.701 and R² 0.31 are extreme relative to the rest and are full-model with added BMI categories; HR 1.75 is strong. However the very high R² is not PRS-comparable here and is likely not isolating PRS contribution, making it unreliable for cross-model ranking.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Very large EUR evaluation (n=391,189) is supportive for stability, but does not fix comparability issues when metrics are not PRS-only and endpoint is incident/time-to-event.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Score is a transformed reuse (“inverse variant weights”) of another PGS (PGS000087) rather than a directly trained model here; covariates include BMI (mild) but the main risk is metric/endpoint non-comparability and potential reporting-scale mismatch (R²).
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Despite eye-catching full-model metrics and huge n, the combination of incident-only endpoint + non-PRS-comparable metric reporting makes it a risky pick versus the coherent PRSweb direct-match cluster; likely not the hidden-benchmark #1 for standalone PRS performance.

rationale: All candidates are close endpoint matches, but four (PGS000630/631/632/633) form a coherent same-publication, same-covariate, same-endpoint cluster where within-family comparisons are most meaningful. Within that cluster, PGS000631 has the strongest combined signal (highest full-model AUROC and Nagelkerke R², and the strongest per-SD OR) under comparable basic covariates, making it the most likely to rank highest in an external benchmark. PGS000797’s much higher AUROC/R² is discounted because it is incident/time-to-event with non-PRS-comparable metric reporting and a reused-weight construction, which is a common selection trap when PRS-only metrics are absent.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match to target via obstructive sleep apnea (dominant clinical form of sleep apnea); phenotype reported as OSA. BMI-adjusted construction aligns with a disease-risk endpoint while attempting to isolate non-BMI-mediated genetic signal.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No PGS-only AUC/R2; only full-model AUROC=0.79 is not PRS-comparable. However, per-SD OR=1.98 is strong discriminative signal relative to peers and is the best PRS-specific performance proxy available in the shortlist.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Disease-focused multi-cohort development (FinnGen, MGBB, MVP) with multi-ancestry validation context listed and n=21,975 evaluation; suggests some transportability testing beyond a single-biobank framework.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Reported AUROC likely covariate-influenced (age/sex/race/BMI/PCs); lack of incremental/PGS-only metrics increases uncertainty. BMI adjustment may reduce apparent PRS effect for generic sleep apnea prediction in settings where BMI is not conditioned similarly.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Strong: modern genome-wide shrinkage (PRS-CSs) with very high variant count plus strong OR per SD and disease-focused multi-cohort provenance—most consistent with top external-benchmark performance among available direct matches.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Same direct OSA endpoint family as PGS005219 (good match to sleep apnea via OSA). UnadjustedBMI label suggests capturing both direct and BMI-mediated genetic components.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: No PGS-only metrics; full-model AUROC=0.79 not comparable. OR=1.53 is still strong but materially weaker than PGS005219, reducing confidence it will rank #1 within this near-clone family.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same multi-cohort disease-focused study family and same evaluation size/context as PGS005219 (n=21,975; multi-ancestry listed).
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same covariate-driven AUROC concern; absence of incremental/PGS-only metrics. If benchmark evaluates PRS independent of BMI, unadjusted construction could be penalized versus BMI-adjusted variants.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Moderate-strong but likely below PGS005219 given weaker OR with otherwise near-identical design and method.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: OSA with BMI-adjusted phenotype (directly aligned). However, constructed from only 6 genome-wide significant SNPs, which is typically underpowered for polygenic prediction.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only full-model AUROC=0.77 (not PRS-comparable) and small beta (0.066) with no OR/HR; weaker PRS signal than the PRS-CS/PRS-CSs genome-wide scores.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Validation n=40,193 is larger, but from the same MVP-centric study family; size alone is a weak differentiator and does not offset sparse model structure.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Sparse GWS-only score risks poor external ranking for a polygenic endpoint; full-model AUROC likely dominated by covariates (BMI/age/sex/PCs/batch).
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Moderate-low: despite direct endpoint, the very small variant set is a strong negative structural signal versus genome-wide shrinkage alternatives.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Label says OSA, but phenotyping_reported indicates BMI-adjusted OSA; still a direct match. Similar MVP study context as PGS003858.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model AUROC=0.77 (not PRS-comparable) and beta ~0.014 (very weak); suggests minimal PRS contribution.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Validation n=40,193 (supportive but weak as primary signal).
candidate_audits.risk_signal: 18-SNP GWS-only construction plus very weak beta implies low standalone PRS performance; covariate-driven AUROC likely.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Low: weakest PRS-specific signal among the disease-focused candidates.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Exact-label sleep apnea match, but comes from ExPRSweb framework repository; phenotype likely broad/heterogeneous compared with clinically targeted OSA endpoints.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Full-model AUROC=0.527 is very low; OR=1.106 indicates weak PRS discrimination. This is consistent with poor benchmark ranking.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: EUR-only training/dev/eval (UKB) with n~21k; limited transportability evidence and framework archetype penalty.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Framework-origin score with weak effect size and near-random AUROC; high risk of underperforming disease-focused multi-cohort OSA scores in external benchmarks.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Very low: both archetype and observed performance proxies indicate it will not rank near #1.

rationale: Across the shortlist, all candidates lack PRS-only AUC/R2, so selection should lean on endpoint fidelity, study archetype, method/variant coverage, and PRS-specific effect-size proxies. PGS005219 and PGS005220 are the strongest disease-focused, genome-wide shrinkage near-clones; PGS005219 has a materially stronger per-SD OR (1.98 vs 1.53) with otherwise similar design, making it the best-supported bet to rank #1 in an external benchmark. Sparse GWS-only MVP scores (PGS003857/PGS003858) and the ExPRSweb framework score (PGS003213) show weaker structural and/or effect-size signals.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match (T2D; phenotyping_reported: Type 2 diabetes). Not horizon/incident-restricted.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only full-model AUROC/R² reported (AUROC 0.793; R² 0.092) plus strong per-SD OR 1.96; absence of PGS-only/incremental metrics limits comparability, but OR magnitude is a meaningful PRS-strength signal.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Large and explicitly diverse evaluation context overall; selected record is European with n=54,793, and the study is explicitly trans-ancestry PRS development/validation (less like a generic framework sweep).
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Full-model metrics may be covariate-influenced (age/sex/PCs/site), but covariates are basic (no biomarkers/family history/risk-calculator packaging). Multi-ancestry GWAS mix could introduce heterogeneity, but PRS-CSx is designed for this.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Strongest combination of disease-focused trans-ancestry design + strong effect-size signal (OR~2 per SD) + reasonably large external-style validation; likely to transfer well to a hidden benchmark compared with candidates that only report incremental R² from a smaller single-cohort setting.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match (T2D; phenotyping_reported: Type 2 diabetes).
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Reports incremental R² (0.129) rather than PRS-only R²/AUROC; incremental metric is not directly comparable across studies and can be sensitive to baseline covariate model. No effect size provided.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Evaluation n=7,879 (European selected), with EVAL split EUR/GME; development is single named cohort (AllofUs) suggesting a more framework-like integrative pipeline rather than a dedicated multi-cohort disease PRS effort.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Comparability risk from relying on incremental R² without clear baseline model details beyond basic covariates; smaller validation increases uncertainty.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Despite a higher incremental R² than its sibling, the evidence is narrower (single-cohort dev, small eval, no OR/AUROC), making it less likely to be the top external-benchmark performer than a robust trans-ancestry disease-focused score with strong effect-size evidence.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match (T2D; phenotyping_reported: Type 2 diabetes).
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Incremental R² 0.099 only; no PRS-only metrics and no effect sizes. Weaker than its near-clone PGS004839 on the same metric type.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Same evaluation setting and size as PGS004839 (n=7,879; EUR selected; EUR/GME overall), so no compensating validation advantage.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: Same incremental-metric comparability limitations; smaller eval and no additional robustness signals.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Within-family dominated by PGS004839 (higher incremental R²) and overall likely below PGS002308 due to weaker and less portable evidence package.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match (T2D; phenotyping_reported: Type 2 diabetes), but ancestry-specific (SAS-only dev and eval).
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Incremental R² 0.065 only; no PRS-only metrics/effect sizes.
candidate_audits.validation_signal: Validation n=8,837 but SAS-only; if the hidden benchmark is not SAS-matched, transfer risk is substantial.
candidate_audits.risk_signal: High transportability risk outside SAS; incremental R² comparability limitations remain.
candidate_audits.benchmark_rank_signal: Ancestry-restricted evaluation makes it less likely to rank #1 in a generic external benchmark setting compared with candidates with demonstrated multi-ancestry evaluation.

candidate_audits.endpoint_fit: Direct match but phenotyping_reported is incident T2D (more specific than generic T2D status), which can reduce comparability to prevalence/case-control benchmarks.
candidate_audits.metric_signal: Only full-model AUROC reported (0.852) with basic covariates; no PGS-only/incremental metrics. Per-SD OR 1.52 is solid but notably weaker than PGS002308’s OR 1.96, suggesting lower standalone PRS discrimination despite higher covariate-boosted AUROC.
